title: The Missing Violin
hero: Dedektif Edmund Crane ve yardımcısı Tess
intro: Hartley Müzik Okulu'nda cuma gecesi 150 yıllık bir keman kayboldu. Ofis kilitliydi ve anahtar yalnızca bekçideydi. Dedektif Edmund Crane ile yardımcısı Tess, cumartesi sabahı okula geliyor.

text: The rain had stopped when Edmund Crane and his assistant Tess reached Hartley Music School on Saturday morning. The headmistress, Mrs. Pryce, was waiting at the gate with a pale face. "Miss Lowell's violin has gone," she said. "It is more than one hundred and fifty years old. She keeps it in the office cupboard, and last night the caretaker locked the office door himself."

Mr. Bell, the caretaker, was standing by the door with the key in his hand. "I locked it at half past seven," he said. "I looked inside, turned off the light and left. This morning the lock was perfect. Nobody had touched it."

Tess went straight to the window. "Then the thief climbed in here!" she said. "Look, it is open." Crane said nothing for a while. He looked at the window sill, which was covered with a thick layer of grey dust, smooth like a blanket. Then he leaned out and studied the flower bed below. It had rained heavily all evening, and the soft earth was flat and clean. Not one footprint, not one broken flower.
"Interesting," Crane said at last, and he took out his small notebook.
ch.clue: thick layer of grey dust
ch.q: What can we understand from the window sill and the flower bed?
o: Mr. Bell opened the window early in the morning
The thief did not enter or leave through the window
The window was opened from outside after the rain
The thief used a ladder and cleaned his footprints
The violin was never kept in the office cupboard
ch.hint: Pervazdaki toza ve akşam boyunca yağan yağmurdan sonra çiçek tarhının hâline dikkat et. Biri tırmansaydı bunlar nasıl görünürdü?
ch.why: Pervaz tozluydu, tarh pürüzsüzdü; pencereden kimse girip çıkmamıştı.

text: Mr. Bell took them to his small room near the front door and put a large book on the table. "Everyone who comes after school hours must sign it," he said. "On Friday evening there were three visitors."

Crane read the lines slowly. Mr. Finch, the piano tuner, had written 6:15 and left the second box empty. Ms. Rowan, a mother, had written 6:40 – 7:30. The last line said: Mr. Dale, delivery, 7:05. Again there was no time for leaving.

"I know Mr. Finch left," said Mr. Bell. "He said goodbye to me at the gate at seven, and I remember his heavy bag of tools. Ms. Rowan's son had a violin lesson until a quarter past seven, and I thanked her at the door at half past. But Mr. Dale?" He shook his head. "I was upstairs checking the windows. I did not see him arrive, and I did not see him go. I thought the building was empty when I locked up."
Tess counted the names on her fingers. "Three people," she said, "and only two of them are completely clear."
ch.clue: I did not see him arrive, and I did not see him go
ch.q: Whose visit cannot be fully explained by the book and the caretaker's memory?
o: Mr. Finch's, because he forgot to write his time
Mr. Bell's, because he was checking the windows
Mrs. Pryce's, because she met the visitors
Mr. Dale's, because nobody saw him leave
Ms. Rowan's, because her son stayed late
ch.hint: Üç ziyaretçiden hangisi için hem defterde çıkış saati hem de Bay Bell'in "gördüm" dediği bir an var? Eksik kalanı bul.
ch.why: Finch ve Rowan'ın çıkışı belliydi; Dale'in ne zaman çıktığını kimse bilmiyordu.

text: They found Mr. Dale in the coffee shop across the road. He was a thin man with a quick smile and an old brown coat. "Yes, I was there," he said easily. "I brought fifty music books from Parker's Shop. Miss Hart, the school secretary, signed for them, so I put the box on the office desk and left by the side door. That was about ten past seven."

Crane thanked him and walked back to the school. In the office, Tess lifted the box from the desk with one hand. "It's empty," she said, surprised. The label said: Fifty music books, Parker's Shop. "Fifty books are never this light," added Crane.

Mrs. Pryce looked at the label and frowned. "We did not order any books this week," she said. "And Miss Hart could not have signed anything. She was at her sister's wedding all Friday. She has not been in the school since Thursday."
Crane smiled for the first time that morning. "Mr. Dale told us a very nice story," he said quietly.
ch.clue: at her sister's wedding all Friday
ch.q: Which part of Mr. Dale's story was shown to be false?
o: That the school secretary signed for the delivery
That he left by the side door at ten past seven
That he brought the box from Parker's Shop
That he was in the coffee shop that morning
That he put the box on the office desk
ch.hint: Dale'in anlattığı her cümleyi Müdire Pryce'ın söylediği şeylerle karşılaştır. Hangi cümle gerçekle uyuşmuyor?
ch.why: Sekreter cuma günü okulda yoktu; Dale'in "imzaladı" demesi yalandı.

text: Back in the office, Crane knelt behind the desk. On the floor there was a tiny piece of green cloth. "Tess, what colour is the inside of Miss Lowell's violin case?" he asked. "Green," she answered. "Dark green, like velvet."
Crane walked slowly to the window, and Mr. Bell followed him. "Think carefully about Friday evening," Crane said. "Did you see anything unusual from the upstairs windows?"

The caretaker closed his eyes. "I saw a man at the side gate, at about twenty-five past seven," he said. "He was carrying a big box to a white van. I did not worry, because I knew the delivery man had come that evening. I thought he was taking back an empty box. But now I remember that he held it with both arms, and he walked very, very slowly. As if it was valuable."
Tess's eyes opened wide. "At half past seven you locked the office, and you only looked inside the room," she said. "You never opened the cupboard."
"Exactly," said Crane. "The violin was already gone."
ch.clue: held it with both arms, and he walked very, very slowly
ch.q: How did the violin leave an office that was locked all night?
o: Ms. Rowan's son took it after his lesson
It was taken from the cupboard on Saturday morning
Someone carried it out in the box before the door was locked
The thief climbed in and out of the window
Mr. Bell hid it in the white van himself
ch.hint: Pencere ve kilit bilgisini, Dale'in kutusunu ve Bay Bell'in 7:25'te gördüğü adamı birleştir. Ofis tam olarak ne zaman kilitlenmişti?
ch.why: Dale 7:25'te içinde keman olan kutuyu vana taşıdı; ofis 7:30'da kilitlenmeden önce keman gitmişti.

outro: Polis, Dale'in beyaz minibüsünde yeşil kadife kaplı kemanı buldu. Crane defterini kapatırken Tess'e şöyle dedi: kilit hiç bozulmamıştı, bu yüzden kilitten önce bakmak gerekiyordu.

title: The Wrong Tablets
hero: Genç doktor Mara Quinn ve hemşire Joe
intro: Mr. Evans kalp tabletlerini aldıktan sonra sersemlemiş ve tansiyonu düşmüş. Doktor Mara Quinn ile hemşire Joe, bunun nedeninin hastanenin bir hatası mı yoksa başka bir şey mi olduğunu araştırıyor.

text: Doctor Mara Quinn was finishing her morning round at St. Luke's Hospital when Nurse Joe called her to Ward 4. Mr. Evans, a kind old man of seventy, was lying in bed with a very pale face. "I feel strange," he said slowly. "The room is moving, even when I am lying still."

Mara checked his blood pressure. It was very low, much lower than usual. Then she looked at his chart. Every morning Mr. Evans took one small white heart tablet, 10 mg. He had taken the same medicine for two years without any trouble. "Why now?" she asked.

Joe brought the new bottle from the cupboard beside the bed. The label was clear and neat: Heart tablets, 10 mg. It had come from the hospital pharmacy on Monday. Mara opened it and poured a few tablets into her hand. They were small, white and round, exactly as usual. But when she looked closer, she saw something on every tablet. Each tablet had the number 40 printed on it.
Joe looked at the label, then at the tablets. Neither of them spoke for a moment.
ch.clue: Each tablet had the number 40 printed on it
ch.q: What did Mara understand from the tablets and the label?
o: Mr. Evans had been taking 40 tablets every day
The pharmacy had sent tablets for another disease
The tablets were stronger than the label said
The tablets were too old to work properly
Mr. Evans had taken the tablets twice that day
ch.hint: Etikette yazan doz ile tabletlerin üzerinde basılı olan sayıyı karşılaştır. Aralarındaki fark sence ne anlama gelir?
ch.why: Etiket 10 mg diyordu ama tabletlerin üzerinde 40 yazıyordu; hasta fazla güçlü ilaç almıştı.

text: "Pull the bottle from the ward," Mara said quickly, "and call the pharmacy." She wrote down the name of the pharmacist, Mrs. Ross, and went downstairs with the bottle in a clean plastic bag.

The hospital pharmacy was small and very quiet. A young assistant named Ben was working at the counter. Mara put the bottle on the table. "Where do you keep the heart tablets?" she asked. Ben pointed to the second shelf. There were two rows of bottles with almost identical blue labels. The first row said 10 mg. The second row, right next to it, said 40 mg.

Mara took a bottle from each row and compared them. The 40 mg label was perfectly normal. But the bottle from the ward looked different. The edge of its label was lifting, like a sticker that had been put on in a hurry. Very carefully, she pulled it up with her fingernail. Underneath there was another label, in the same blue colour. It said: Heart tablets, 40 mg.
"Someone stuck a new label on top of the old one," Mara said.
ch.clue: Underneath there was another label
ch.q: How did the strong tablets reach the ward with a 10 mg label?
o: A nurse took the label from another bottle
Mr. Evans changed the label himself
The factory printed the wrong number on the tablets
The bottle fell and the label moved
A wrong label was stuck over the correct one at the pharmacy
ch.hint: Etiketin kenarı kalkık ve altında başka bir yazı var. Bu durum, hatanın nerede ve nasıl yapıldığı hakkında ne söylüyor?
ch.why: Üstteki 10 mg etiketi, altındaki 40 mg etiketinin üzerine yapıştırılmıştı; hata eczanede olmuştu.

text: Mara asked Ben to explain how the labels were printed. "On Monday afternoon I printed the labels for all the heart tablets," he said, a little nervous. "It was my third day at work. I used the list on the computer, and I stuck each label on a bottle." Mara looked at the printer record. At ten past three, eight labels for 10 mg had been printed. Not one label for 40 mg.

"So the labels you printed were right," said Mara. "The tablets inside one bottle were not." She looked at the wall, where a paper said: Every bottle must be checked by the senior pharmacist before it leaves the pharmacy. Under it, there was a small box for the signature of Mrs. Ross.
"Where is Mrs. Ross?" Mara asked. Ben looked down. "She is on holiday until Tuesday," he said quietly. "On Monday nobody checked my work. I did not know that I could ask another pharmacist."
Joe, who had followed them, said softly, "So the mistake is not only Ben's."
Mara nodded. "A mistake can happen to anyone," she said. "Checking is there to stop it."
ch.clue: She is on holiday until Tuesday
ch.q: Why was the mistake not discovered on Monday?
o: The nurses never read the labels on bottles
The person who normally checks the bottles was away
Ben did not print any labels at all
The printer had stopped working that afternoon
The pharmacy was closed on Monday afternoon
ch.hint: Duvardaki kural kimin imzasını istiyor ve o kişi pazartesi nerede? Hatayı durdurması gereken kontrol neden çalışmamış olabilir?
ch.why: Etiketleri kontrol etmesi gereken kıdemli eczacı tatildeydi; kimse Ben'in işini kontrol etmemişti.

text: "Ben," said Mara, "how many bottles of heart tablets left the pharmacy on Monday afternoon?" Ben looked at the list. "Three," he answered. "One went to Ward 4 for Mr. Evans. One went to Ward 2. And one went to Ward 3."

Mara took the list and read the names carefully. Ward 2 was for Mrs. Hart. The note said that she had started the new tablets on Tuesday morning, and last night a nurse had written that her heartbeat was very slow. Ward 3 was for Mr. Clarke. But next to his name there was a different note: he had used the same tablets since last year, and the Monday bottle was still closed in the cupboard. "He has been using an old bottle," Joe said. "He has not opened the new one yet."
Mara stood up at once. "Joe, go to Ward 2 now and take Mrs. Hart's blood pressure. We must also take the Monday bottle away from Mr. Clarke before tomorrow morning."
"So Mr. Evans is not the only one in danger," said Joe.
"No," said Mara. "But now we know who is."
ch.clue: the Monday bottle was still closed in the cupboard
ch.q: Besides Mr. Evans, who needed urgent help first?
o: Ben, who printed all the labels
Mrs. Ross, who was on holiday
Mr. Clarke, who had used the tablets for a year
Mrs. Hart, who started the tablets on Tuesday
Nobody, because the other bottles were correct
ch.hint: Pazartesi çıkan üç şişenin notlarını karşılaştır. Hangi hasta yeni şişeden ilaç almaya başlamış, hangisi henüz başlamamış?
ch.why: Mrs. Hart yeni şişeden salı günü başlamıştı ve nabzı yavaşlamıştı; Mr. Clarke ise şişeyi hiç açmamıştı.

outro: Eczanede etiket kuralı yeniden yazıldı ve iki hasta da iyileşti. Mara, Joe'ya "Küçük bir etiket büyük bir hataya yol açabilir" dedi.

title: The Silent Radio
hero: Komutan Noor Hale ve mühendis Pip
intro: Aurora uzay istasyonunda radyo bir sabah birden sustu. Komutan Noor Hale ile mühendis Pip, Dünya ile bağlantının neden koptuğunu bulmak zorunda. Çünkü yeni ikmal gemisi yakında gelecek.

text: Commander Noor Hale woke up to a strange sound, or rather, to no sound at all. Every morning the radio of the Aurora space station played the voice of Mission Control. Today the speaker was silent. She floated to the control room, where the engineer Pip was already looking at the screen.
"The radio is fine," Pip said. "Look, the power light is green, and the test says that everything inside works. But the signal is zero. We cannot hear Earth, and Earth cannot hear us."
"How long?" asked Noor. "Since 2:10 this morning," said Pip. "The computer wrote it in the log."

Noor opened the outside camera. The big white antenna stood on the side of the station, like a giant plate. She looked at it for a few seconds and held her breath. In the picture the antenna was pointed at the black empty space on the far side of the station, not at the blue planet shining below them.
"Pip," she said slowly, "the radio is not broken. Somebody has turned our ears away from Earth."
ch.clue: pointed at the black empty space
ch.q: What was the problem with the radio?
o: Mission Control had turned off its radio
The camera could not see the planet
The speaker was broken inside
The antenna was aimed away from Earth
The radio had no electricity
ch.hint: Pip radyonun içinin sağlam olduğunu söylüyor. Peki Noor kameradaki antenin neresine bakıyor?
ch.why: Radyo sağlamdı; anten Dünya'ya değil boş uzaya dönmüştü.

text: "Who moved the antenna?" asked Pip. Noor opened the computer log and read it aloud. "No person touched it," she said. "At 2:10 the antenna turned by itself. The automatic system moved it to follow a target called Cargo-7."
Pip made a face. "Cargo-7? That ship left the station last Tuesday. It is on its way to the Moon, far away from Earth. I saw it leave."

"Then the computer is still following a ship that is not here," said Noor. She looked at the list on the screen. The list of targets had two lines. The first line said Cargo-7. The second line said nothing at all; it was empty. "The system always follows the first target," Noor said. "As long as Cargo-7 is on the list, the antenna will turn toward it, even when that means turning away from Earth."
Pip nodded. For a moment the control room was very quiet, except for the soft noise of the fans.
"The computer is not stupid," he said finally. "It is just very obedient."
ch.clue: The system always follows the first target
ch.q: Why did the antenna turn away from Earth at 2:10?
o: It followed an old ship that was still on the list
The Moon was blocking the signal
The automatic system was switched off
Pip moved it by hand to test it
A new ship had just arrived at the station
ch.hint: Günlük kaydı dikkatle oku: anten kimin komutuyla döndü ve sistem hangi hedefi izliyor? O hedef şu an nerede?
ch.why: Otomatik sistem listenin ilk hedefi olan eski Cargo-7'yi izliyordu; gemi Dünya'dan uzaktaydı.

text: "Who should have removed Cargo-7 from the list?" asked Noor. Pip opened a drawer and took out the paper checklist for ships that leave the station. The last step said: Delete the old target and add the next one. There was a tick next to every step, except the last one.

"The list says that Eli did the work last Tuesday," Pip said. "He is the careful type. I cannot believe he forgot." They found Eli in the kitchen, drinking tea from a plastic bag. When Noor showed him the checklist, he put his hand on his forehead.

"Oh no," he said. "I remember now. I was just going to do it after lunch. Then the water pump broke, and the whole crew had to repair it until night. Look, I wrote a note." He took a small pad from his pocket. On it, in fast letters, he had written: Water pump! Code for Cargo-8 later. Under it was a little drawing of a pump with water coming out of it.
"I put the note away and forgot it," Eli said sadly.
Noor smiled a little. "It was a good reason," she said, "but a very expensive one."
ch.clue: Water pump! Code for Cargo-8 later
ch.q: Why was the last step of the checklist not done?
o: Eli wanted the antenna to turn away
The computer refused to delete the target
An urgent repair made Eli forget it
Eli did not know how to use the list
The paper list was lost for a week
ch.hint: Eli'nin cebindeki notu ve o gün istasyonda neler olduğunu birlikte düşün. Son adım unutulmuş; onu unutturan ne?
ch.why: Eli son adımı yapmak üzereyken su pompası bozuldu; acil onarım yüzünden notu unuttu.

text: Pip typed the new code for Cargo-8 into the system and deleted the old line. On the screen the antenna began to move. Slowly, like a big flower looking for the sun, it turned until it faced the blue planet again. A green number appeared. Then another. Then a voice, tired and happy, filled the room.
"Aurora, this is Mission Control. We have called you every hour since midnight. Are you all right?"
"We are fine," Noor said, laughing. "We had a small problem with an old ship."

When the call ended, the whole crew gathered in the control room. Eli said he was sorry again, but Noor stopped him. "Nobody wants to blame you," she said. "I want everyone to understand what happened, so it never happens again. Listen carefully. One small thing at the end of a long chain made the whole station silent."
She took a marker and started to write the chain of events on the white board, one line under the other.
ch.clue: One small thing at the end of a long chain
ch.q: Which order of events explains why the radio stayed silent?
o: The antenna turned, the pump broke, the old target stayed, the signal was lost
The old target was deleted, the antenna turned, the pump broke, the signal was lost
The signal was lost, the old target was deleted, the pump broke, the antenna turned
The signal was lost, the pump broke, the antenna turned, the old target stayed
The pump broke, the old target stayed, the antenna turned, the signal was lost
ch.hint: Önce hangi olay diğerlerinin hepsini başlattı? Sonra her olayın bir sonrakine nasıl yol açtığını sırayla takip et.
ch.why: Pompa arızası listenin güncellenmesini engelledi; eski hedef kaldı, anten döndü, sinyal kesildi.

outro: Radyo yeniden çalıştı ve Dünya'dan yüzlerce mesaj aktı. Noor, listeyi kimin silmesi gerektiğini ekip panosuna kocaman harflerle yazdı.

title: The Map in the Wall
hero: Arkeolog Dr. Amira Kent ve öğrencisi Leo
intro: Küçük bir köyün eski kilisesinin duvarından yüzlerce yıllık gibi görünen bir harita çıktı. Arkeolog Dr. Amira Kent ile öğrencisi Leo, haritanın gerçek mi sahte mi olduğunu anlamaya çalışıyor.

ch.t: The Bridge That Was Not There
text: The village of Marlow was very small, but on Saturday morning it was full of excited people. Workers had been repairing the stone wall of the old church, and inside the wall they found a brown paper, folded many times. It was a map. In the top corner someone had written the year: 1650.

Dr. Amira Kent came from the university and carried the map into the church hall very carefully. Her student Leo followed her with a small camera. A hundred villagers stood behind them, hardly breathing. "Is it real?" asked the mayor. "Is there treasure?"

Amira put the map under a bright lamp. It showed the river, the church, a market square and a small forest. It also showed a stone bridge over the river, and under the bridge, in beautiful letters, were the words: Queen Anne's Bridge. Amira read the words twice and smiled strangely.
"Leo," she said, "please check the village history book. When was Queen Anne's Bridge built?"
Leo searched for a minute. "In 1790," he said. "A hundred and forty years later."
ch.clue: Queen Anne's Bridge
ch.q: What is strange about the map?
o: It shows the river in the wrong place
It was folded many times
It has no name of the village
It was found inside a church wall
It shows a bridge that did not yet exist in 1650
ch.hint: Haritadaki tarihe ve köprünün inşa edildiği tarihe bak. Harita yazıldığı tarihte köprü var mıydı?
ch.why: Harita 1650 tarihli ama 1790'da yapılan bir köprüyü gösteriyordu; tarih ve çizim uyuşmuyordu.

text: "Maybe the village changed the name of the bridge later," said the mayor hopefully. "Maybe it had another name in 1650." Amira shook her head gently. "A bridge cannot appear on a map before it exists, whatever its name is. But let us not decide too fast. Let us look at the paper."

She turned the map and held it against the lamp. Inside the paper there was a faint mark, like a very pale picture. It was a small circle with two letters inside it: P&S. "This is called a watermark," she explained to the villagers. "Paper makers put it in the paper when they make it. Each factory has its own mark."
Leo opened his laptop and found the list of old paper factories. "P&S means Parker and Stone," he read. "A factory in the north of England. It was opened in 1921."
The room became very quiet. An old woman at the back said, "So the paper is not four hundred years old?"
"It is not even a hundred years old," said Amira. "Somebody wanted us to think it was."
ch.clue: small circle with two letters inside it
ch.q: What does the watermark show about the map?
o: The paper came from a church in the north
The paper was made long after 1650
The paper is older than the church wall
The map belongs to the factory owner
The map was copied from an older map in 1650
ch.hint: Filigranın hangi fabrikaya ait olduğunu ve o fabrikanın ne zaman açıldığını karşılaştır. Kâğıt haritadaki tarihten önce var olabilir miydi?
ch.why: Kâğıt 1921'de açılan bir fabrikanın filigranını taşıyordu; harita 1650'den kalma olamazdı.

text: "So it is a fake," said the mayor sadly. "But who made it, and why?" Amira smiled for the first time that day. "Let us find the person. Fakes always have small clues, because everybody writes in their own way."

She put the map next to some old school notices from the village. Leo photographed the numbers. In the map, the number seven was written with a little line through the middle. The same strange seven was on the notice from the primary school, and also on a poster for the church fair. Amira checked the names under the notices. All the sevens with a line were written by one person: Mr. Hobbs, the history teacher.
"Hobbs is not a thief," said the mayor, surprised. "He is the most honest man in the village. He loves history more than anyone."
"Maybe that is why," Amira said quietly. "People who love history sometimes make mistakes. I am not saying he is a bad man. I only say that his handwriting is on the map."
ch.clue: the number seven was written with a little line
ch.q: Who most likely made the map?
o: The mayor, because he asked about treasure
Leo, because he used the camera
The church workers, because they found it
Mr. Hobbs, because the handwriting matches his
Nobody, because the map is real
ch.hint: Haritadaki yedi rakamının özel yazılışını, köydeki diğer belgelerle karşılaştır. Aynı yazı biçimi kimin belgelerinde var?
ch.why: Yedi rakamındaki çizgi, öğretmen Bay Hobbs'un okul duyurularındaki yazı biçimiyle aynıydı.

text: They found Mr. Hobbs in the small village museum. It was a cold room with a few old pots and no visitors. When Amira showed him the map, he sat down heavily. "I am sorry," he said at once. "I made it. I only wanted to help the village."

On his desk there was a bright yellow leaflet. Leo picked it up and read aloud: "Treasure Trail Weekend at Marlow! Follow the old map! Tickets: five pounds. All money goes to the museum." The date was only two weeks away.

"The museum has no money," Mr. Hobbs explained. "The roof leaks, and nobody comes here. I thought a mystery would bring visitors, the way stories do. I put the map in the wall last month when the workers were out for lunch. I never wanted to hurt anyone."
Amira looked at the leaflet and then at the old man. She did not say that what he did was right. But she said, "A real story about a fake map may bring visitors, too, if you tell it honestly."
For the first time, Mr. Hobbs smiled.
ch.clue: Tickets: five pounds
ch.q: What was Mr. Hobbs's real reason for making the map?
o: He wanted visitors and money for the poor museum
He wanted to prove the church was very old
He hoped to sell the map to a collector
He wanted to make the mayor look foolish
He was angry with the church workers
ch.hint: Masasındaki sarı broşüre, biletlere ve paranın nereye gideceğine dikkat et. Bay Hobbs haritadan ne bekliyordu?
ch.why: Bay Hobbs, bilet gelirinin müzeye gideceği bir hazine hafta sonu için ziyaretçi çekmek istemişti.

outro: Köyün müzesi hazinesiz kaldı ama gerçek bir hikâye öğrendi. Amira, Leo'ya şunu söyledi: bir belgeyi anlamanın yolu, ona inanmadan önce onu sınamaktır.

title: The Yellow Plants
hero: Bilim insanı Dr. Ilan Voss ve asistanı Dana
intro: Laboratuvardaki bitki deneyinde yalnızca bir grup bitki sararıp solmaya başladı. Dr. Ilan Voss ile asistanı Dana, tüm koşullar aynıyken neden yalnızca o grubun bozulduğunu araştırıyor.

text: Dr. Ilan Voss opened the door of the plant room and stopped. For three weeks he had been testing a new plant food. The experiment was simple. Thirty small bean plants stood on three tables: Table A, Table B and Table C. Each table had ten plants, and each plant had the same soil, the same pot and the same light from the big window.
Today, the plants on Table A and Table C were bright green and tall. The plants on Table B were different. Their leaves were yellow at the edges, and some were falling down like tired people.
His assistant Dana came in with her coffee and looked worried. "I water them every morning," she said. "I use exactly the same method for all of them."

Ilan looked at the three tables slowly. The temperature was the same. The window gave light to all of them equally. Then he checked the little cards in front of each table. Tables A and C had a card that said: Tap water. Table B had a card that said: Tap water with plant food.
"So there is one difference," Ilan said. "Only Table B got the plant food."
ch.clue: Tap water with plant food
ch.q: What is the only difference between Table B and the other tables?
o: Table B received water with plant food
Table B was watered less often
Table B had warmer air around it
Table B had a different kind of soil
Table B had less light from the window
ch.hint: Üç masada da ışık, toprak ve saksı aynı. Masaların önündeki kartlarda yazan şeyleri karşılaştır; yalnızca birinde farklı bir şey var.
ch.why: Tüm koşullar aynıydı; yalnızca B masasındaki bitkiler besin katkılı su almıştı.

text: "The plant food is supposed to help," said Dana. "The company says it makes plants grow faster." Ilan took the bottle from the shelf. The label said: Mix one small spoon with one litre of water. He held the bottle against the light. It was almost empty.
"For ten plants for three weeks," Ilan said, thinking aloud, "we should have used only a little. But the bottle is nearly finished. That is far too much plant food."

"Maybe the plants are sick because of too much food, not too little," said Dana. Ilan nodded. "A plant is like a person. A little medicine helps, but a lot of it can hurt. Too much plant food burns the roots. The leaves turn yellow at the edge, exactly like these."

He wrote a short sentence in his notebook: Table B may have received too much plant food. Then he looked at Dana. "Tell me how you measured it, step by step. I am not angry. I need the exact picture."
Dana took a deep breath and began to remember.
ch.clue: the bottle is nearly finished
ch.q: What does the almost empty bottle suggest?
o: The plants needed much more food
The plant food was too old to work
Too much plant food was used
The company sent a bottle that was too small
Someone drank the plant food
ch.hint: Etikete göre üç haftada ne kadar ürün gitmesi gerekirdi, şişenin hâli ise nasıl? Ilan'ın bitki ve ilaç benzetmesine de dikkat et.
ch.why: Şişe neredeyse boştu; B masasına gereğinden çok bitki besini verilmişti.

text: "The bottle came with two caps," Dana said slowly. "A tiny blue cap for measuring one small spoon, and a big red cap for closing the bottle. In the first week, the blue cap fell behind the sink, and I could not find it. I did not want to stop the experiment, so I used the red cap to measure instead."

Ilan took the red cap and filled it with water from the sink. Then he poured the water into the small measuring spoon. "How many small spoons fit in this red cap?" he asked. Dana counted. "Ten," she said in a very small voice. "The red cap holds ten small spoons."
"Then every morning you gave the plants ten times more than you should have," said Ilan.
"I am so sorry," said Dana, and her eyes were wet. "I should have told you about the cap."
Ilan put his hand on her shoulder. "Yes, you should have told me," he said gently. "But now we know. A good scientist learns more from a mistake than from an easy day."
ch.clue: The red cap holds ten small spoons
ch.q: Why did the plants on Table B get too much plant food?
o: Dana poured it on the soil by accident
Ilan forgot to tell Dana the amount
The label gave a wrong number
The blue cap was too small to use
Dana used a bigger cap to measure it
ch.hint: Dana ölçüyü hangi kapakla yaptı ve o kapak mavi kapaktan kaç kat fazla alıyor? Bu fark bitkilere ne yapmış olabilir?
ch.why: Dana mavi kapak yerine on kat fazla alan kırmızı kapakla ölçmüştü.

text: Ilan did not want to guess. "Now we must prove it," he told Dana. "Anyone can make a nice story. A real scientist needs a real test."

They planted twenty new bean plants and put them on two new tables, D and E. Everything was the same: soil, pots, light, tap water, temperature. Table D received the plant food with a proper blue cap, exactly one small spoon in each litre. Table E received the plant food with the red cap, ten spoons in each litre, like Table B before.

Dana wrote the results every day in a green notebook. After seven days, the plants on Table E started to have yellow edges. After ten days, they were almost the same as the plants on Table B. The plants on Table D were tall and green, and some of them even had new flowers.
Dana closed the notebook and smiled for the first time in two weeks. "Now we know," she said.
ch.clue: Everything was the same
ch.q: Why is the second experiment a good proof?
o: The plants on Table D got no water
Only the amount of plant food was different
It used more tables and more plants than before
Dana wrote the results in a green notebook
It was done after the first experiment
ch.hint: İyi bir deneyde yalnızca bir şeyin değişmesi gerekir. Yeni masalarda neler aynı tutulmuş, neler değiştirilmiş?
ch.why: Toprak, ışık ve su aynıydı; yalnızca besin miktarı farklıydı, bu yüzden sonuç net bir kanıttı.

outro: Deney yeniden yapıldı ve bu kez tüm bitkiler yemyeşil kaldı. Ilan, deney defterine büyük bir not düştü: önce neyin değiştiğini bul, sonra suçlu arama.

title: The Sunny Photo
hero: Muhabir Jonas Reid ve fotoğrafçı Ellie
intro: Yerel gazetenin ön sayfasında belediye başkanının yeni kütüphaneyi açtığı güneşli bir fotoğraf yayımlandı. Ama bir okur fotoğrafın sahte olduğunu yazdı. Muhabir Jonas Reid ile fotoğrafçı Ellie gerçeği bulmaya çalışıyor.

text: On Monday morning, a letter was waiting on Jonas Reid's desk at the Kingsbridge Daily. It was short and angry. "Your front page is not honest," the writer said. "The photo of Mayor Dalton opening the library was not taken on Saturday. Please check."

Jonas looked at the newspaper. The photo was big and beautiful. The mayor stood in front of the new library with a pair of large scissors and a wide smile. Behind her, a crowd was clapping. The caption said: Mayor Dalton opens the new library on Saturday. Many people in the crowd were wearing sunglasses, and every person had a long, sharp shadow on the dry ground.

Jonas picked up the weather report from Saturday, which his colleague had pinned on the wall. It said: Heavy rain from nine in the morning until six in the evening. The library had opened at eleven o'clock.
He looked at the photo again, then at the report. Then he called to the next room. "Ellie! I think we have a problem."
ch.clue: Heavy rain from nine in the morning until six in the evening
ch.q: What does the weather report suggest about the photo?
o: The mayor was not at the library at all
It was probably taken on a different day
The photographer used a very old camera
It was taken before the library opened that morning
The crowd was not real
ch.hint: Fotoğraftaki gölgelere, güneş gözlüklerine ve kuru zemine bak. Sonra cumartesi günü hava durumunun ne olduğunu hatırla.
ch.why: Cumartesi sağanak yağmur vardı ama fotoğrafta güneş ve kuru zemin vardı; fotoğraf başka bir günde çekilmiş olmalıydı.

text: Ellie, the newspaper's photographer, came in with her laptop. She had been at the library on Saturday, in the rain, with a plastic bag over her camera. "That is not my photo," she said at once. "I took forty pictures on Saturday, and nobody smiled like that. People were wet and cold."

She opened her pictures on the screen and put one next to the front page. The two photos showed the same wall of the library, but there was a clear difference. In Ellie's picture, the wall was clean and freshly painted, and a big sign said: Opening Today. In the newspaper photo, there was no sign. Instead, a tall ladder was leaning against the wall, and a bucket of white paint stood on the ground next to it.
"Nobody leaves a ladder and a bucket on the day of an opening," Ellie said. "The painters were still working when this was taken."
Jonas wrote in his notebook: Photo taken earlier, before the painting was finished. Then he asked, "But who gave us this picture?"
ch.clue: a tall ladder was leaning against the wall
ch.q: What do the ladder and the paint bucket tell us?
o: Ellie took the photo from a different street
The newspaper changed the wall with a computer
The library was not painted at all
The photo was taken before the painting work was finished
The painters were angry about the opening
ch.hint: Ellie'nin cumartesi fotoğrafındaki duvarla gazete fotoğrafındaki duvarı karşılaştır. Biri boyalı ve temiz, diğerinde ise merdiven ve kova var. Hangisi daha erken olabilir?
ch.why: Gazete fotoğrafında hâlâ merdiven ve boya kovası vardı; boya işi bitmeden önce çekilmişti.

text: Jonas asked the editor's assistant to find the email with the photo. The assistant searched for a few minutes. "It was sent last Thursday at four in the afternoon," he said. "The sender is Mr. Penn, the head librarian. The file name is 'opening_mayor.jpg'."

Jonas phoned Mr. Penn, who answered in a nervous voice. "Oh, that photo," he said. "Yes, the mayor visited the library on Thursday. She promised to cut the ribbon on Saturday, but she also said it might rain. So I took a picture of her with the scissors on Thursday, in the sun, in case the weather was bad. I only wanted to help your newspaper. I wrote in my email that it was from Thursday."
Jonas opened the email again. At the very bottom, in small grey letters, there was a line: This photo was taken on Thursday, before the opening. Nobody at the paper had read that far.
"So the librarian told us the truth," said Ellie. "Our paper did not read it."
ch.clue: This photo was taken on Thursday, before the opening
ch.q: Whose mistake was it that the old photo appeared as Saturday's news?
o: The newspaper's, because nobody read the whole email
The readers', because they wrote letters
The librarian's, because he hid the date
The painters', because they left a ladder there
The mayor's, because she asked for the photo
ch.hint: E-postanın en altındaki küçük gri satırı kim okumamış? Bay Penn bilgiyi saklamış mı, yoksa gazete mi bu bilgiyi gözden kaçırmış?
ch.why: Bay Penn tarihi e-postanın sonunda yazmıştı; gazetede kimse o satıra kadar okumamıştı.

text: By afternoon, the editor, Mrs. Cole, had read everything. She was not angry with Mr. Penn. "He only tried to help," she said. "Our paper made the mistake, so our paper must correct it." She asked Jonas to write a short note for tomorrow's front page, and Ellie to choose a better photo from Saturday, even a wet one.

Jonas thought carefully about each word. A correction must be as clear as a good story. He wrote three possible sentences on a piece of paper and read them aloud to Ellie, one by one. The first sentence said that the opening had been in the sun. The second said that the mayor had cut a ribbon on Thursday. The third one was longer, and it was exactly right: it said that Thursday's picture showed the mayor with the scissors before the opening, and that the real opening on Saturday was in the rain.
"Print the third one," said Mrs. Cole. "And put Ellie's rainy picture next to it."
Ellie smiled. "Wet and honest," she said. "I like it."
ch.clue: before the opening, and that the real opening on Saturday was in the rain
ch.q: Which caption would be the most honest for the old photo?
o: Mayor Dalton cuts the ribbon on Thursday afternoon
Mayor Dalton opens the library on a sunny Saturday
Mayor Dalton with the scissors on Thursday, before the opening
Mayor Dalton and the painters outside the library
Mayor Dalton practises a speech in the rain
ch.hint: Doğru başlık hem fotoğrafın gerçek gününü hem de ne olduğunu doğru söylemeli. Önceki bölümlerde hangi gün ve ne zaman çekildiğini öğrendin.
ch.why: Fotoğraf perşembe günü, açılıştan önce çekilmişti; doğru başlık bunu açıkça belirtmeliydi.

outro: Gazete ertesi gün düzeltme yayımladı ve okurlardan özür diledi. Jonas, masasına yeni bir kural astı: haber tarihini ve fotoğrafın tarihini her zaman ayrı ayrı doğrula.

title: The Lost Walkers
hero: Park korucusu Wren Calder ve köpeği Bracken
intro: Raven Tepesi'ndeki iki yürüyüşçü akşam yemeğine dönmedi. Hava kararıyor ve yağmur şiddetleniyor. Park korucusu Wren Calder ile köpeği Bracken, ayak izlerini ve küçük işaretleri takip ederek onları bulmaya çalışıyor.

text: It was six o'clock, and the sky above Raven Hill was turning grey. Ranger Wren Calder stood at the fork in the path with her dog Bracken beside her. Two walkers, a man called Tom and a woman called Rosa, had left the hostel at nine that morning. They had planned to return for dinner at five. They were already one hour late, and the first drops of rain were falling.

Bracken sniffed the ground and found a blue backpack under a tree. Inside there were two sandwiches, a map and an empty water bottle. "They have left the bag on purpose," said Wren. "Maybe they wanted to walk faster."

The ground at the fork was soft and wet. Wren knelt and studied it. There were two sets of boot prints, one small with a smooth sole and one big with deep zigzag lines. At the fork, the prints did not go right, toward the safe path to the hut. They went left, along the narrow path that followed the river.
"Left," she said to Bracken. "They chose the river."
ch.clue: the prints did not go right
ch.q: Which way did the walkers go?
o: Up the hill behind the big tree
Back to the hostel they started from
Toward the river on the left path
Along the safe path to the hut
They stayed at the fork under the tree
ch.hint: Çatalda ayak izlerinin hangi yöne gittiğine ve metnin bunu nasıl anlattığına dikkat et. Sağ yol güvenli yol, sol yol nehir yoluydu.
ch.why: İzler güvenli sağ yola değil, nehri izleyen sol yola gidiyordu.

text: The path along the river was narrow and slippery. Wren walked slowly, with her torch in one hand and Bracken's rope in the other. The rain was heavier now, and the river made a loud noise, much louder than in the morning. After twenty minutes, she reached a place where the path went straight into the water. On the other side she could see a small beach.

"There should be flat stones here," Wren said, and she shone her torch into the river. A line of big stones was there, but the water was running over them, deep and brown. Last night had been rainy too, and the river had risen.

Then Bracken barked once. On a rock on the far bank, something small and red was moving in the wind. Wren raised her torch. It was a woolly scarf, caught on the sharp edge of the rock, the sort of scarf that a woman would wear around her neck on a cold morning.
"Rosa's scarf," said Wren. "She must have lost it when she was crossing."
ch.clue: caught on the sharp edge of the rock
ch.q: What did the walkers probably do at the river?
o: They returned along the path
They climbed the tree near the fork
They swam down the river
They slept next to the stones
They crossed to the other side
ch.hint: Kırmızı eşarp nerede asılı kalmış? Orası nehrin hangi yakası ve yürüyüşçüler oraya nasıl ulaşmış olabilir?
ch.why: Rosa'nın eşarbı nehrin karşı kıyısındaki kayaya takılmıştı; ikisi de karşıya geçmişti.

text: Wren could not cross. The water was much too high for her. She called Bracken back and climbed a little higher on her side of the river to see the other bank. In the grey light she could see the beach, a few trees, and, a hundred metres beyond them, the dark shape of an old stone building.
"The shepherd's hut," she said softly. "Nobody has used it for years."

She pointed the torch at the roof. For a second she could see nothing. Then the wind changed direction, and a thin line of white smoke rose from the chimney. It twisted in the air and disappeared. Bracken stood very still, ears up, looking exactly in the same direction.

"Somebody lit a fire," Wren said. "Somebody who knows that smoke is a message and fire is a friend." She took a deep breath. A few minutes ago she had felt afraid. Now she felt something very different.
She took her radio from the belt and pressed the button. "Base, this is Wren," she said. "I think I have found them."
ch.clue: a thin line of white smoke rose from the chimney
ch.q: Where are Tom and Rosa most likely to be?
o: Back at the hostel eating dinner
In the old hut on the far side of the river
On the beach next to the stones
Still walking along the left path
Under the tree where the bag was
ch.hint: Wren'in feneri çatıya ne gösterdi? Kimse kullanmayan bir kulübeden duman çıkıyorsa içeride ne olabilir?
ch.why: Terk edilmiş çoban kulübesinin bacasından duman çıkıyordu; biri ateş yakmıştı.

text: At eight o'clock a rescue team arrived with a rope and a small boat. They crossed the river together and found Tom and Rosa sitting by a little fire, wrapped in old sacks. Both of them were tired, but they were smiling.

"We are so sorry," said Rosa. "We wanted to see the waterfall, so we went to the beach by the river, and we crossed on the stones around three. It was easy then, the water was only to our ankles." Tom put his foot out. His left ankle was swollen like a ball. "I slipped on the way back," he said. "I could not walk. And when we came to the stones again, the water was already up to the top of them. We could not cross with a hurt ankle, so we came to the hut and lit a fire."
Wren looked at the small fire, at the two tired walkers, and at the empty water bottle. "You did the right thing," she said. "You stayed warm, you stayed together, and you made smoke."
Bracken licked Tom's hand, as if he agreed.
ch.clue: the water was already up to the top of them
ch.q: Why did Tom and Rosa not come back by themselves?
o: They wanted to sleep in the old hut
The rescue team told them to wait
Rosa had lost her boots in the river
Tom was hurt and the river had risen
They did not know the way to the hostel
ch.hint: Tom ayağını nasıl yaralamış ve dönüşte nehrin hâli nasılmış? İki durumu birlikte düşün.
ch.why: Tom'un ayak bileği incinmişti ve nehir taşlarının üstü sularla kapanmıştı; geri geçemediler.

outro: Yürüyüşçüler sıcak bir battaniyeyle sarıldı ve sabaha kadar kulübede dinlendi. Wren, defterine şunu yazdı: doğa küçük işaretlerle konuşur, yeter ki acele etmeyelim.

title: The Wrong Label
hero: Küratör Hugo Laurent ve güvenlik görevlisi Mina
intro: Şehir müzesindeki "Mavi Liman" tablosunun etiketinde bir hata var gibi görünüyor. Küratör Hugo Laurent ile güvenlik görevlisi Mina, tablonun gerçekte ne zaman ve kim tarafından yapıldığını anlamaya çalışıyor.

text: Every Tuesday, Mina walked slowly through the quiet rooms of the City Museum and said good morning to the paintings. Her favourite was Blue Harbour, a large picture of boats and a stone pier in the evening light. The small card on the wall said: Blue Harbour. Anders Lund, 1890.

That Tuesday, an old man with a walking stick stopped in front of it for a long time. "Excuse me," he said at last. "I think your card is wrong." Mina came closer. "Wrong?" she asked politely. "Look at the sky, on the right," said the man.
Mina looked. At the top right corner, among the pink clouds, there was a very small shape with two wings and a tail. It was easy to miss. It was a little aeroplane.
"In 1890," the old man said with a smile, "nobody was flying aeroplanes. The first aeroplane flew thirteen years later. A painter cannot paint something he has never seen."
Mina felt a cold feeling in her stomach. She picked up the phone and called the curator.
ch.clue: a very small shape with two wings and a tail
ch.q: Why did the old man think the card was wrong?
o: The painter's name was spelled incorrectly
The boats in the picture were too modern
The colours were too bright for old paint
The painting shows something that did not exist in 1890
The picture was hanging on the wrong wall
ch.hint: Tablonun sağ üst köşesinde ne görünüyor ve o şey 1890'da var mıydı? Yaşlı adamın tarihi hatırlatmasına dikkat et.
ch.why: Tabloda bir uçak vardı ama 1890'da henüz uçak yoktu; tarih yanlış olmalıydı.

text: Hugo Laurent, the curator, arrived in ten minutes. He was a tall man with grey hair and very careful hands. Together with Mina, he took the heavy painting from the wall and laid it face down on a soft table.
On the back of the canvas there was a rectangle of old paper, yellow at the edges. Hugo read it aloud: Art Supply Company, London, 1931. Under it was a handwritten number.

"Artists buy the canvas and paint on it later," he said. "The company stamped it in 1931, so the painting cannot be older than that. It is a mistake to call it an 1890 picture." Mina asked, "Could somebody have painted on an older canvas?" Hugo shook his head. "Then the stamp would be older, not newer. A canvas can wait for the artist, but the artist cannot paint before the canvas exists."
He opened the museum's big record book and looked for Blue Harbour. "It came as a gift in 1950," he read, "from Mr. Grey, who bought it at a street market. Painter: unknown. Date: around 1935."
"Around 1935," Mina repeated. "So the card is very wrong."
ch.clue: Art Supply Company, London, 1931
ch.q: What does the stamp on the canvas show?
o: The painting was made in 1931 or later
The painting came to the museum in 1931
The painter was from London in 1890
The canvas was older than the painter
The painting was repaired in 1931
ch.hint: Kanvasın arkasındaki damga tarihini oku. Ressam kanvas satın alınmadan önce o kanvasa resim yapabilir miydi?
ch.why: Kanvasın damgası 1931'di; resim bu tarihten önce yapılamazdı.

text: "But the old card said 'Painter unknown, around 1935'," said Hugo. "I remember it. Who changed it?" Mina thought for a moment. "Last month, the card fell from the wall. I picked it up, and a young man from the office, Mr. Dunn, took it and said he would print a new one."

They found Mr. Dunn in the small office behind the café. He showed them the museum catalogue, a big list of every picture and every card. "I only copied from this," he said, a little hurt. "Look, here is Blue Harbour, and next to it..." He stopped. On the page, two paintings were listed one after another. The first line said: Blue Harbour — painter unknown, around 1935. The second line said: Harbour Light — Anders Lund, 1890.
Mr. Dunn turned white. "I copied the line under it," he whispered. "I took the wrong line."
Hugo looked at the page and nodded. "It was an honest mistake, but it is a serious one. Now, where is Harbour Light?"
ch.clue: I copied the line under it
ch.q: How did the mistake with the card happen?
o: The catalogue said Lund painted Blue Harbour
Mina printed the wrong card
Mr. Dunn copied the line of the next painting
Hugo wrote the date from memory
Mr. Dunn changed the card on purpose
ch.hint: Dunn katalogdan nasıl kopyalamış? Sayfada alt alta iki tablo var; Dunn hangi satırı almış ve neden?
ch.why: Dunn, katalogda Mavi Liman'ın altındaki satırı, yani başka bir tablonun bilgisini kopyalamıştı.

text: Harbour Light hung in the next room, and its card said: Harbour Light. Painter unknown, around 1935. Hugo and Mina looked at each other. "So the two cards are in the wrong places," said Mina. "Dunn made a new card for Blue Harbour, and the old Blue Harbour card was fixed under the other one, by someone who did not read it."

Hugo lifted Harbour Light from the wall and turned it over. This time the back was very different. The wooden frame was dark with age, and on the canvas there was a small label in thin brown ink: A. Lund, 1890, oil on canvas. Even the style was old. The boats had sails, no engines, and the street lamps in the picture burned gas. There was no aeroplane anywhere.
"Here is the real Anders Lund," said Hugo, and his voice was full of joy. "We have been hanging a masterpiece with the wrong card for many years, and a young painter's picture with a famous name."
Mina laughed. "And everything started because of a man with a stick."
ch.clue: A. Lund, 1890, oil on canvas
ch.q: What is the true situation with the two paintings?
o: Both paintings were painted by Anders Lund
Both paintings were made around 1935
The museum owns only one of the paintings
Harbour Light was painted after Blue Harbour
The two cards were swapped between the paintings
ch.hint: Harbour Light'ın arkasındaki etikette hangi ressam ve yıl yazıyor? Bu bilgiyi iki tablonun kartlarıyla karşılaştır.
ch.why: Harbour Light'ın arkasında A. Lund 1890 yazıyordu; iki tablonun kartları birbirinin yerine takılmıştı.

outro: Etiketler doğru yerlere takıldı ve müze bir ziyaretçiye teşekkür mektubu yazdı. Hugo şöyle dedi: küçük bir kâğıt parçası bile bir müzenin bütün hikâyesini değiştirebilir.

title: The Sleeping Cat
hero: Oyun testçileri Zoe ve Max
intro: Zoe ve Max, yeni bir kaçış odasını açılıştan önce test ediyor. Kapı arkalarından kilitlendi ve bir saatleri var. Çıkmak için duvardaki saat, bir kedi posteri ve birkaç ipucu yardımcı olacak.

text: The door closed behind them with a loud click, and a red number appeared on the wall: 60:00. Zoe and Max had one hour to leave the Clock Room. The owner of the escape room had asked them to test it before the opening day, and both of them loved puzzles.

The room was small and warm. On the left, there was a wooden desk with four drawers, numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4. On the right, there was a tall bookshelf full of old books. Above the desk hung a big round clock with a white face. Its hands were stopped at a quarter past three. Beside the clock, there was a poster of a fat orange cat, sleeping in a basket.
Under the poster, someone had written in small letters: The cat sleeps where the short hand points.

"Cats and clocks," said Max. "What does that mean?" Zoe stood in front of the clock. "The short hand is the hour hand," she said slowly. "At a quarter past three, it points almost exactly at one number. Max, I think I know where our first drawer is."
ch.clue: The cat sleeps where the short hand points
ch.q: Which drawer should they open first?
o: Drawer 4
The drawer with the poster
Drawer 2
Drawer 1
Drawer 3
ch.hint: Kısa ibre saati gösteren ibredir. Saat üçü on beş geçeyi gösterirken kısa ibre hangi sayıya yakındır?
ch.why: Kısa ibre üç sayısını gösteriyordu; kedi üç numaralı çekmecede uyuyordu.

text: In the third drawer, Zoe found a thick old book with three coloured bookmarks in it. The first bookmark was red and stood at page 12. The second was blue and stood at page 7. The third was green and stood at page 9. Under the book there was a note, written in careful handwriting: Red walks first, blue walks in the middle, green walks last. Only the last number of each page can talk to the box.

"The box," said Max, and pointed at a small metal box on the desk. It had a lock with three round wheels, each with the numbers 0 to 9. "So the numbers on the wheels should be the last digits of the pages, in the order of the walkers."

"Red walks first, blue in the middle, and green last," Zoe said slowly. "Let us not hurry. A wrong code on a lock like this may start the clock faster." Max nodded and looked at the three wheels. Each one waited at zero, quiet and round, like a small closed eye.
ch.clue: Red walks first, blue walks in the middle, green walks last
ch.q: Which code opened the box?
ch.hint: Her sayfa numarasının yalnızca son rakamı önemli. Sonra bu rakamları yürüyüş sırasına göre diz: önce kırmızı, ortada mavi, sonda yeşil.
ch.why: Kırmızı 12'nin son rakamı 2, mavi 7, yeşil 9'du; sıra 2-7-9 olduğu için kod 279'du.

text: The little lock gave a soft click, and the lid of the box opened. Inside there was a small silver key and a folded paper.

The silver key was too small for the door. It opened only a tiny cabinet on the wall, hidden behind a curtain. Inside the cabinet there was no key, only a keyboard with letters and a short riddle on the paper they had found in the box: I have a face, but I have no eyes. I have two hands, but I cannot clap. I always tell the truth, but I never speak. What am I?
"A mirror?" said Max. "A mirror has a face, but it shows what you look like." Zoe shook her head. "A mirror does not have hands. And it does not tell you the time. Look around the room, Max."

Max turned slowly on the spot and looked at everything in the room: the poster, the desk, the bookshelf and the wall above the desk. Zoe was already holding her fingers over the small keyboard. The red number on the wall said 18:42. They had used more than forty minutes.
ch.clue: I have two hands, but I cannot clap
ch.q: What is the answer to the riddle?
o: A key
A book
A cat
A clock
A mirror
ch.hint: Bilmecedeki iki eli, yüzü ve gerçeği söyleyip konuşmaması ne anlama gelebilir? Max'in baktığı şey odanın duvarında asılı.
ch.why: Yüzü ve iki eli olan, doğruyu söyleyen ama konuşmayan şey duvardaki saatti.

text: Zoe typed the answer, and the screen turned green. The new clue was a short sentence on it: The last door is not a door. Look where the cat is looking.

Max ran to the poster. The orange cat slept in its basket, but if you looked carefully, one of its eyes was open. It was a drawn eye, small and yellow, and it was not looking at the door, or at the clock, or at the desk. It was looking sideways, at the tall bookshelf.

"The bookshelf," Zoe said. "But which book?" On the bookshelf there were about forty books. Zoe stepped back and drew an imaginary line from the cat's eye across the room. The line ended at one book on the third shelf, a thin blue book without a title. Its spine was a little brighter than the others.
Max pulled it out. Behind it, there was a round green button. "Ready?" he asked. "Always," said Zoe, and they pressed it together. A deep sound came from the wall, and a hidden door slowly opened.
ch.clue: one of its eyes was open
ch.q: How did Zoe and Max find the last button?
o: They followed the direction of the cat's eye
They looked under the desk drawers
They read the title of every book
They turned the clock backwards
They counted the books on the shelf
ch.hint: Son ipucu "kedinin baktığı yere bak" diyor. Posterdeki kedinin gözü neye doğru bakıyordu?
ch.why: Kedinin açık gözü kapıya değil, kitaplığa bakıyordu; çizgiyi izleyince düğmeyi buldular.

outro: Kapı açıldı ve Zoe ile Max dışarı çıktı. Oda sahibi onlara teşekkür etti; en iyi bulmaca, doğru yere bakmayı hatırlatan bulmacadır.

title: The Wrong Suitcase
hero: Havalimanı görevlisi Dara Mills ve stajyer Sam
intro: Mrs. Lin otele gidip bavulunu açınca içinde erkek giysileri buldu. Havalimanı görevlisi Dara Mills ile stajyer Sam, bavulun nasıl karıştığını ve doğru bavulun nerede olduğunu çözmeye çalışıyor.

text: It was a busy afternoon at Heathfield Airport. Dara Mills, an airport officer, was drinking her tea when her young trainee Sam ran into the office. "Dara, there is a lady on the phone," he said. "She is very upset."

Dara took the phone. The woman's name was Mrs. Lin, and she was staying in a hotel near the airport. "I came from Madrid this afternoon," she said. "I took my suitcase from the belt, a red suitcase with a yellow ribbon on the handle. When I opened it in my room, it was full of men's clothes! Big grey trousers, two shirts and a pair of black shoes."

"I am very sorry," said Dara kindly. "Is there a name tag on the case?" Mrs. Lin looked. "No," she said. "The tag is gone. But the red colour and the yellow ribbon are exactly like mine. I am very sure that it is a suitcase just like mine."
Dara put down the phone and looked at Sam. "Somebody has my customer's suitcase," she said. "And she has somebody else's."
ch.clue: full of men's clothes
ch.q: What probably happened to Mrs. Lin's suitcase?
o: Another passenger took it by mistake
The hotel gave her a different case
Mrs. Lin packed the wrong clothes
The airline lost it in Madrid
A thief opened it and changed the clothes
ch.hint: Mrs. Lin içinde başkasının eşyalarının olduğu, ama tıpatıp kendi bavuluna benzeyen bir bavul bulmuş. Bu durum en çok hangi olasılığa uyar?
ch.why: Bavul tıpatıp benziyordu ama içinde başka birinin eşyaları vardı; biri yanlışlıkla Mrs. Lin'in bavulunu almıştı.

text: "We need to know who took her suitcase," said Dara. She and Sam went to the baggage hall and asked the security office for the camera pictures from the afternoon. The security officer showed them the belt. At 2:20, a man with a blue cap took a red suitcase with a yellow ribbon from the belt and walked away quickly. Two minutes later, Mrs. Lin took another red suitcase with a yellow ribbon from the same belt.

"Look at the screen above them," said Sam. Above the belt there were two flights on the information board. One said: Madrid, landed 2:10. The other said: Berlin, landed 2:15. Both flights used the same belt, one after the other. The suitcases from the two flights came out almost at the same time.
"So we have two red cases with yellow ribbons, two flights at the same belt, and two tired passengers," said Dara. "Neither of them looked at a name tag, and Mrs. Lin's tag had fallen off."
"That is a very bad day for a red suitcase," said Sam.
ch.clue: the same belt, one after the other
ch.q: Why did the two suitcases get mixed up?
o: The airline put both cases on the wrong belt
Sam read the information board incorrectly
Two similar cases came from two flights at the same belt
Mrs. Lin's flight landed in another airport
The man in the blue cap was a thief
ch.hint: Güvenlik kamerasında kimler ne zaman aynı banttan bavul almış ve bilgi panosunda hangi iki uçuş görünüyor? Bunları birleştir.
ch.why: Madrid ve Berlin uçuşları aynı banda art arda inmişti ve iki bavul birbirine çok benziyordu.

ch.t: The Man in the Blue Cap
text: The office had a small shelf for lost things, and on the shelf there was a red suitcase with a yellow ribbon. It was not Mrs. Lin's. Dara read the tag: Mr. T. Brandt, flight from Berlin. Under the name there was a phone number.

She dialled it. A man answered after a long time, and in the background there was the noise of a train. "Hello?" he said. "This is Brandt." Dara explained. For a moment there was silence, and then the man started to laugh. "I thought something was very strange!" he said. "I am on the train to Cambridge, and I have just opened my bag in the toilet. It is full of ladies' dresses and a beautiful orange scarf. I wanted to phone, but I have no number."

"Please do not worry," said Dara. "Can you bring the case back to the airport?" Mr. Brandt thought for a moment. "I cannot return tonight," he said. "The train is going far north. But I can leave it in the left-luggage office of Cambridge station before the shop closes at six."
Dara wrote it down: Cambridge station, left luggage.
ch.clue: I can leave it in the left-luggage office of Cambridge station
ch.q: Where will Mrs. Lin's suitcase be left for her?
o: At the security office of Heathfield Airport
At the hotel near the airport
On the belt in the baggage hall
At Mr. Brandt's house in Berlin
At the left-luggage office of Cambridge station
ch.hint: Bay Brandt tren yolculuğunda nereye gittiğini ve çantayı nerede bırakabileceğini söylüyor. Hangi yer ve ne zamana kadar?
ch.why: Bay Brandt, bavulu Cambridge istasyonunun emanet bürosuna bırakacağını söyledi.

text: Mrs. Lin was waiting in the airport café, drinking a cup of tea that she did not want. Dara explained the plan, and Sam added a small joke about suitcases, but Mrs. Lin did not smile. She took a deep breath. "My sister is getting married tomorrow at ten o'clock," she said. "My dress is in that suitcase. I cannot go to the wedding without it."

"The church is thirty minutes from your hotel," Dara said, looking at the paper. "Mr. Brandt will leave your bag at Cambridge station tonight. A courier from our company will pick it up at once. The courier promised to bring it to your hotel by eight o'clock tomorrow morning."

Mrs. Lin counted on her fingers. "Eight o'clock for the suitcase," she said. "Half an hour to get ready, and thirty minutes to the church..." She looked up and smiled for the first time. "That is plenty of time."
"We will also call you tomorrow at seven to check," said Sam. "And next time, we will tie a ribbon of a different colour on your handle."
ch.clue: by eight o'clock tomorrow morning
ch.q: Will Mrs. Lin arrive at the wedding on time?
o: No, because the bag will come after the wedding
Yes, because the bag will arrive two hours before the wedding
Yes, but only if she skips breakfast
No, because the church is too far away
It is impossible to know from the story
ch.hint: Bavul saat kaçta otelde olacak, düğün saat kaçta ve kiliseye ne kadar sürede gidiliyor? Zamanları karşılaştır.
ch.why: Bavul saat sekizde otelde olacak, düğün onda; kiliseye yarım saatlik yol var, zaman fazlasıyla yeterli.

outro: Mrs. Lin'in bavulu sabah erkenden otele ulaştı ve düğüne yetişti. Dara, Sam'e şunu hatırlattı: iki bavul birbirine benziyorsa her zaman etiketi kontrol et.

title: The Birthday Cake
hero: Dedektif Edmund Crane ve yardımcısı Tess
intro: Belediye başkanının 60. doğum günü pastası, fırının vitrininden gece kayboldu. Parti öğlen saat on ikide başlayacak. Dedektif Edmund Crane ile yardımcısı Tess, pastayı bulmak için sabahın erken saatinde fırına geliyor.

text: At half past six on Saturday morning, Mrs. Fenn was crying behind the counter of her bakery. "It was the best cake I have ever made," she said. "Three layers of chocolate, ten kilos, for Mayor Hobb's sixtieth birthday. The party begins at noon. And now it is gone!"

Edmund Crane and Tess looked around quietly. The window where the cake had stood all night was empty, and the shop door was still locked. "The back door was closed, but not locked with the key," said Mrs. Fenn. "I keep the key under the blue flowerpot. Nobody forced the door."

The two detectives went out into the yard, where it had rained in the night. The ground was soft and muddy. Near the door, Crane found a line of small boot prints. They were light and shallow on the way in, but deep, almost twice as deep, on the way out. Next to the prints ran two thin parallel lines, as if something with small wheels had been pulled through the mud.
"A small person, a heavy load and a cart," said Crane. "That is already a good beginning."
ch.clue: deep, almost twice as deep, on the way out
ch.q: What do the shallow prints going in and the deep prints coming out suggest?
o: The person was running away from the shop
The person came out carrying or pulling something heavy
Two different people used the same door
The person was much heavier when entering
The person came in a hurry and left slowly
ch.hint: İzlerin içeri girerken hafif, dışarı çıkarken derin olmasının nedenini düşün. Yanındaki iki ince çizgi de bir şeyin taşındığını mı gösteriyor?
ch.why: Çıkış izleri daha derindi ve yanında tekerlek çizgileri vardı; kişi ağır bir yükü çekerek çıkmıştı.

text: "Mrs. Fenn," said Crane, "who knows where you keep the key?" The baker counted slowly on her fingers. "Only my three helpers," she said. "My delivery boy Sam, who is seventeen. My apprentice Lily, who is sixteen. And my old friend Mr. Crumb, who has the bakery in the next street."

"Mr. Crumb is a rival," Tess whispered to Crane. Mrs. Fenn heard her and laughed sadly. "He is my rival in the shop, but he is my friend at home. He was in hospital for two days last week, and he is still there. The nurse told me this morning."

Crane looked at the boot prints in his notebook. He had measured them carefully. They were only size four, much smaller than a grown man's boots. "Sam is a big boy," Mrs. Fenn said, following his eyes. "He is six feet tall, and his boots are size nine. Lily is very small, but she is strong. She carries our flour sacks every morning."
Crane closed his notebook. "Mrs. Fenn," he said gently, "where is your apprentice at this moment?"
ch.clue: size four, much smaller than a grown man's boots
ch.q: Who knew about the key and could have left the small prints?
o: Sam, the tall delivery boy
Mrs. Fenn, the owner of the bakery
A stranger who found the key by chance
Lily, the small apprentice
Mr. Crumb, the baker from the next street
ch.hint: Anahtarı bilen üç kişiden birini hastane eledi. Kalan ikisinin ayak numaralarını, bulunan izlerin numarasıyla karşılaştır.
ch.why: Anahtarı bilen ve küçük ayak izine uyan tek kişi Lily'ydi; Sam'in ayakkabısı çok büyüktü, Bay Crumb ise hastanedeydi.

text: Lily lived in a small flat above the grocer's shop. When Crane and Tess knocked, her mother opened the door in her dressing gown. "Lily went out before five," she said, worried. "She said she had to do something very important for Mrs. Fenn. She took her coat and ran."
"Where did she go?" asked Tess. "I don't know," said the mother. "She said she had left a note at the bakery."

Back at the shop, Tess went down on her knees and looked under the counter. After a minute, she stood up with a small piece of paper in her hand. It had been lying behind the heavy counter, in the dust, where no one could see it. The writing was round and a little nervous: Dear Mrs. Fenn, don't be afraid! I have taken the cake. Please call me at once. Lily.
Mrs. Fenn read it twice, and her face changed from pale to pink. "But I never saw this note," she said. "My phone is always off at night. And the note must have slid down when I opened the door."
ch.clue: behind the heavy counter
ch.q: Why did Mrs. Fenn not know where the cake was?
o: Lily's note had fallen down behind the counter
The note was written in another language
Mrs. Fenn read the note and forgot it
Lily forgot to write a note for her
Lily's mother hid the note from her
ch.hint: Tess notu nerede buldu? Bayan Fenn sabah dükkâna geldiğinde neden onu görmemiş olabilir?
ch.why: Not tezgâhın arkasına düşmüştü; Bayan Fenn onu hiç görmemişti ve telefonu da gece kapalıydı.

text: The wheel marks in the mud led from the back yard, along the lane and straight to the Town Hall, two hundred metres away. At the side entrance, a cleaner named Mrs. Rudd was mopping the floor. "Are you looking for the cake?" she asked. "It is in the cold room, safe and sound. Lily brought it at five in the morning, on the old handcart."

In the cold room, the great chocolate cake stood on a silver table, tall and shining, with sixty small candles around it. Lily sat on a chair next to it, tired and pale. When she saw Mrs. Fenn, she jumped up.

"I'm so sorry!" she said. "I came to the bakery at four, as I always do to help with the oven. The shop was warm, and the fridge in the corner was dead. It had stopped working at midnight, and the frosting was already starting to melt, like in the summer. I knew the Town Hall has a cold room, so I took the cake there. I wrote a note, but I could not call you. I did not want to wake you up in the middle of the night."
Mrs. Fenn put both arms round her. "My brave girl," she said.
ch.clue: the fridge in the corner was dead
ch.q: Why did Lily take the cake to the Town Hall?
o: She wanted to eat some before the party
The bakery door was locked and the key was lost
The bakery fridge broke and the frosting was melting
The mayor had asked her to bring it early
She wanted to hide it from Mr. Crumb
ch.hint: Lily dükkâna gittiğinde buzdolabının durumu nasıldı ve krema ne olmaya başlamıştı? Belediyedeki soğuk oda neden işe yaramıştı?
ch.why: Fırının buzdolabı gece yarısı bozulmuş ve krema erimeye başlamıştı; Lily pastayı belediyenin soğuk odasına taşımıştı.

outro: Pasta tam zamanında masaya konuldu ve herkes Lily'yi alkışladı. Crane, Tess'e gülümsedi: her kayıp şey çalınmış olmak zorunda değildir.

title: The Birthday Party Rash
hero: Genç doktor Mara Quinn ve hemşire Joe
intro: Sekiz yaşındaki Leo, bir doğum günü partisinden sonra dudakları şişmiş hâlde acile getirildi. Doktor Mara Quinn ile hemşire Joe, hangi yiyeceğin buna neden olduğunu ve Leo'nun neye dikkat etmesi gerektiğini bulmaya çalışıyor.

text: On Saturday afternoon, a worried mother carried her son Leo into the emergency room of St. Luke's Hospital. The boy was eight years old, and his lips were swollen and red. He was breathing a little fast, but he was awake and talking.

Doctor Mara Quinn gave him a small dose of medicine and watched him carefully. After half an hour, the swelling started to go down. "He is better," she told the mother. "Now we need to find out why this happened. Tell me exactly what he ate at the party."

The mother took a piece of paper from her bag. She had written down everything. "Pizza, orange juice, a fruit salad, a chocolate cake with white cream, and a small biscuit from a gift bag," she read. "But I do not understand. Leo eats pizza every Friday. He drinks orange juice every morning. He has eaten fruit salad since he was a baby, and the biscuits were the same ones we buy at home."
Joe, the nurse, looked at the paper. "Then only one thing on the list is new," he said slowly.
ch.clue: Leo eats pizza every Friday
ch.q: Which food is the most suspicious?
o: The fruit salad
The pizza
The chocolate cake with white cream
The orange juice
The biscuit from the gift bag
ch.hint: Annenin yazdığı listeyi dikkatle oku: hangi yiyecekleri Leo her hafta ya da her gün yiyip içiyor? Listede kalan yeni yiyecek ne?
ch.why: Pizza, portakal suyu, meyve salatası ve bisküvi Leo'nun her zaman yediği şeylerdi; yalnızca pasta yeniydi.

text: The next day, Mara phoned the mother of the birthday girl and asked about the chocolate cake. The mother was surprised. "It was not from a shop," she said. "I made it myself from a very old family recipe. Do you want the recipe?" Mara said she would like it very much.

The recipe arrived by email an hour later. Mara read it with Joe in the doctors' room. It listed eight things: flour, sugar, eggs, butter, cocoa, milk, vanilla and ground almonds. "Ground almonds make the cake soft," Joe read. "Many family recipes use them."

Mara checked Leo's medical card. A year ago, a doctor had tested him for peanuts and eggs, and both tests were negative. "He eats eggs every day, so it is not the eggs," she said. "And the doctor tested peanuts, not almonds. Almonds are a different kind of nut, and some people react to them even if they are fine with peanuts."
"So almonds are the only thing in the cake that Leo has never been checked for," Joe said.
Mara nodded. "That is my first guess. Now we need to test it."
ch.clue: ground almonds
ch.q: Which ingredient is the most likely cause?
o: The eggs
The vanilla
The flour
The cocoa
The ground almonds
ch.hint: Leo'nun kartında hangi maddeler için test yapılmış? Pastadaki sekiz malzemeden hangisi bu testlerde hiç yer almamış?
ch.why: Leo yumurta ve fıstık için test edilmişti; pastadaki kuru bademe hiç bakılmamıştı.

text: On Monday morning, Leo came to the allergy room with his mother. Nurse Joe put a few tiny drops on the skin of his arm, one next to the other. Each drop was a different thing: peanut, egg, milk, wheat and almond. Then he made a very small mark under each drop with a clean needle. It did not hurt, but Leo made a funny face anyway.

"Now we wait for fifteen minutes," said Joe. "Please don't scratch." Leo sat very still and counted the ceiling lights, nine of them. When Mara came back and looked at his arm, four of the places were calm and white. At the fifth place, under the almond, there was a red, raised spot as big as a coin.
"There it is," said Mara. "Your son is allergic to almonds."

"But why did nothing happen before?" asked the mother. "Because he had never eaten almonds," said Mara. "Allergy often shows itself the first time the body meets something. Or the second time. It is nobody's fault. The cake was made with love."
"I will never use almonds in a cake again," said the mother softly.
ch.clue: a red, raised spot as big as a coin
ch.q: Why had Leo never reacted to almonds before the party?
o: The almonds in the cake were too old
He had never eaten almonds before the party
He had eaten almonds every day without problems
He was allergic to the party only
The doctor had already given him medicine
ch.hint: Beden alerjiyle ilk karşılaştığında nasıl tepki verebilir? Leo daha önce badem yemiş miydi?
ch.why: Leo daha önce hiç badem yememişti; alerji bir maddeyle ilk karşılaşmalarda ortaya çıkabilir.

text: Before they left, Mara gave Leo a green card to keep in his school bag. It said: I am allergic to almonds. Please call my mother. Then she turned to the mother and showed her a small table on the wall. "From now on," she said, "you must read the label on every packet, every time. Companies change recipes."

She took four different snacks from a shelf and put them on the desk. "Let us practise. Look at the labels and tell me which snack is safe for Leo." The first packet said: Chocolate cookies. May contain traces of nuts. The second said: Marzipan sweets: sugar, ground almonds. The third said: Fruit jelly: sugar, fruit juice, gelatine. The fourth said: Almond milk biscuits.
Leo read the labels carefully, with his finger under every word, and then he pointed. "This one," he said proudly. "It only has sugar, juice and jelly. No nuts at all."
"Excellent," said Mara. "A good detective always reads the evidence."
ch.clue: sugar, fruit juice, gelatine
ch.q: Which snack is safe for Leo?
o: None of them is safe
The almond milk biscuits
The chocolate cookies
The fruit jelly
The marzipan sweets
ch.hint: Leo yalnızca bademe alerjik. Etiketlerde bademin, fındığın ya da "iz miktarda" fıstığın adı geçen paketleri ele. Geriye ne kalıyor?
ch.why: Sadece meyve jölesinin içinde badem ya da fındık yoktu; diğerlerinde badem ya da kuruyemiş izi vardı.

outro: Leo'nun ailesi bir alerji kartı aldı ve etiket okumayı öğrendi. Mara şöyle dedi: bir yiyeceğin etiketini okumak, birçok soruyu baştan çözmek demektir.

title: The Falling Oxygen
hero: Komutan Noor Hale ve mühendis Pip
intro: Aurora istasyonunda oksijen seviyesi saat başına biraz azalıyor. Henüz tehlike yok ama sebep bulunmalı. Komutan Noor Hale ile mühendis Pip, havanın nereden kaçtığını bulmak için istasyonun modüllerini tek tek kontrol ediyor.

text: At breakfast, the little screen on the wall of the Aurora space station made a polite beep. Commander Noor Hale looked at it and felt her heart become a little heavier. The oxygen level was 20.1 percent. Yesterday it had been 20.9. The numbers had been falling for ten hours.

"It is not dangerous yet," said Pip, the engineer, floating beside her. "But air does not disappear. If we are losing it, it is going somewhere." The station had three modules: A, where the crew slept; B, where they cooked and worked; and C, the science module. The hatches between the modules were closed to keep the air in each place.

Pip opened the report from the sensors. In Module A, the pressure was normal. In Module B, it was normal, too. In Module C, the pressure was dropping by one small step every hour, and the oxygen with it.
"So the air is not escaping from the whole station," Noor said slowly. "It is escaping from one place."
"Module C," Pip said, and put on his tool belt. "I will go and look for the hole."
ch.clue: In Module C, the pressure was dropping
ch.q: Where should Pip look for the leak?
o: In the hatches between the modules
In Module A, where the crew sleeps
In Module B, where they cook
In Module C, the science module
Outside the station, near the antenna
ch.hint: Üç modülün basınç değerlerini karşılaştır. Hangisinde sürekli düşüş var, hangisinde normal?
ch.why: Yalnızca C modülünde basınç düşüyordu; A ve B normaldi, sızıntı da orada olmalıydı.

text: Module C was full of boxes and strange machines. Pip floated slowly in the middle and listened. He could hear the fans, a soft click from a computer, nothing more. "A tiny hole makes only a tiny noise," he said to himself. "Our ears are not enough."

He took a thin paper tissue from his pocket and let it go in the air, a few centimetres from his hand. In the station, air does not move much, and the tissue hung quietly in the middle. Pip waited. After ten seconds, it began to drift. It moved very slowly at first, then a little faster, always in the same direction, toward the wall where the round science window was. It stopped at the edge of the window frame and stayed there, shaking softly, as if somebody were holding it with a very thin finger.
Pip smiled. "Thank you, little friend," he whispered. He put his hand next to the tissue and felt a very gentle, cold breath on his skin.
"The air is moving toward the window frame," he said into the radio. "I think I found the place."
ch.clue: toward the wall where the round science window was
ch.q: What does the movement of the tissue show?
o: Air is flowing toward the leak near the window frame
The tissue is attracted by the machines
The window is open to the outside of the station
The fans are blowing the air toward the window
There is no leak in Module C at all
ch.hint: Mendil havada hangi yöne sürüklendi ve nerede durdu? Havanın hareketi bir sızıntıya doğru olabilir mi?
