ch.why: Mendil pencere çerçevesine doğru sürüklendi ve orada durdu; hava oradaki sızıntıya doğru akıyordu.

text: Pip looked carefully at the edge of the window. The frame was made of strong metal, and between the metal and the glass there was a black rubber seal that kept the air inside. All around the window, the seal was smooth and perfect. But at the bottom, there was a small round hole in the rubber, as small as a coin. A thin white cable came through the hole, from inside to outside.
"Noor," Pip called, "somebody has put a cable through the window seal." Noor floated into the module and read the label on the cable: Experiment 14, installed yesterday, Dr. Sato.

Dr. Sato arrived a minute later, rubbing his sleepy eyes. "Yes, that is my experiment," he said. "I needed a camera on the outside of the window, so I made a small hole for the cable. I planned to close the space around it with putty, but dinner came, and then it was late, and I forgot."
"So the hole was never closed," said Noor.
"The cable fills the hole," said Pip, "but not completely. The air escapes around it, very slowly, in the dark."
ch.clue: I planned to close the space around it with putty
ch.q: What caused the leak?
o: A meteorite that hit the science window
A crack in the window glass
A hole for a cable that was never sealed with putty
A broken hatch between two modules
An old rubber seal that wore out
ch.hint: Kablonun içinden geçtiği delik hakkında Dr. Sato ne diyor? Planladığı son işlemi yapmış mı?
ch.why: Dr. Sato kablo için küçük bir delik açmıştı ama etrafını macunla kapatmayı unutmuştu.

text: Pip put a soft grey putty around the cable and pressed it with both hands until it filled every small space around the hole. It looked ugly, like a piece of chewing gum on a window, but it was exactly what he needed. "Now we wait," he said, and floated away from the wall.

The crew gathered in the control room and watched the screen. The first hour, the pressure in Module C did not fall. It did not rise, either. "Good, but it is only one hour," said Noor. The second hour passed, and the third. The little line on the screen was flat, like a calm sea. In the fourth hour, Dr. Sato gave a quiet cheer. In the fifth hour, Noor allowed herself a smile.
After six hours, she asked, "How can we be sure that the leak is really closed?"
Pip pointed at the screen. "Because the numbers have stopped falling, and nothing else has changed. Same module, same temperature, same crew. Only the putty is new."
ch.clue: the numbers have stopped falling
ch.q: How do they know that the leak is closed?
o: The putty looks strong and thick around the cable
The tissue no longer moves near the window
Dr. Sato said that the cable was fine
Module C is warmer than the other modules
The pressure stayed the same for many hours after the repair
ch.hint: Onarımdan sonra ekran saatlerce ne gösterdi? Bir onarımın işe yaradığını anlamak için en güvenilir kanıt hangisi?
ch.why: Onarımdan sonra basınç saatlerce sabit kaldı; sayılar artık düşmüyordu ve başka bir şey değişmemişti.

outro: Oksijen seviyesi sabitlendi ve alarm sustu. Noor, ekibe şunu söyledi: bir sızıntı, en küçük delikte bile bir sorundur; o yüzden hepsine bakarız.

title: The Missing Page
hero: Arkeolog Dr. Amira Kent ve öğrencisi Leo
intro: Küçük bir kasabanın arşivindeki 1830 tarihli günlükten bir sayfa kesilmiş. O sayfada kasabadaki büyük sel anlatılıyormuş. Dr. Amira Kent ile öğrencisi Leo, sayfayı kimin neden kestiğini bulmak için arşive geliyor.

text: The town archive of Stonebridge was a quiet room that smelled of dust and old paper. Dr. Amira Kent and her student Leo had come at the request of the librarian, Miss Garner, who was walking nervously from one shelf to another. "It happened last week," she said. "Someone has damaged the Blake diary."

The Blake diary was a thick brown book from the year 1830. It was written by the town clerk, Mr. Blake, who wrote down everything that happened in Stonebridge, day by day. Miss Garner opened it carefully on the table under the lamp. Amira looked at the pages. Page 46 ended in the middle of a sentence: The rain began in the night, and by morning... Page 48 started with a new sentence: The church bell rang at six.

Leo ran his finger along the inner edge of the book. "Between 46 and 48, there is no page," he said. The edge was very smooth, with no tears. Amira knelt and looked at it with a small magnifying glass. "A sharp blade," she said. "It was cut slowly and on purpose, to look like nothing."
ch.clue: Page 46 ended in the middle of a sentence
ch.q: What do the smooth edge and the unfinished sentence show?
o: The page was torn by a child by accident
The page fell out because the glue was old
Mr. Blake forgot to write on page 47
The book was printed with a missing page
The page was cut out on purpose with a sharp blade
ch.hint: Sayfa 46 cümle ortasında bitiyor ve kenar pürüzsüz, yırtık yok. Bu iki ayrıntı kazayla mı yoksa bilerek mi bir kesimi gösterir?
ch.why: Sayfa 46 cümle ortasında kesilmişti ve kenar pürüzsüzdü; sayfa keskin bir bıçakla bilerek çıkarılmıştı.

text: "Who has used the diary in the last month?" asked Amira. Miss Garner took a large notebook from her desk. In the archive, each reader had to write their name, the date and the time. She read the last four lines: "On Monday, Ms. Dunn, a student, from ten to eleven. On Wednesday, Mr. Cole, a historian, from two to three. On Thursday, Mr. Pike, a builder, from twelve to one. On Friday, nobody."

"The page was cut after Mr. Blake's diary was last checked on Monday morning," Miss Garner said, "because I always look at every page when readers leave. On Wednesday, Mr. Cole sat next to my desk all the time, and I watched him. On Thursday, I went out for lunch at twelve, and I came back at half past twelve."
"So on Thursday, between twelve and half past," said Leo slowly, "the only person in this room was a reader."
"Yes," said Miss Garner. "Mr. Pike was alone."
ch.clue: On Thursday, I went out for lunch at twelve
ch.q: Who had the best chance to cut the page?
o: Mr. Cole, who sat next to the librarian's desk
Mr. Pike, who was alone while the librarian was at lunch
Miss Garner, who checked every page
Nobody, because the archive was closed on Friday
Ms. Dunn, the student who came on Monday
ch.hint: Kütüphaneci hangi ziyaretçiyi hep gözetlemiş, hangi gün yemeğe çıkmış? O sırada odada kim yalnız kalmış?
ch.why: Perşembe günü kütüphaneci öğle yemeğine çıkmıştı ve o sırada odada yalnızca Bay Pike vardı.

text: Mr. Pike came to the archive that afternoon with a friendly smile and a roll of plans under his arm. "I? Cut a page? I only read about old buildings," he said. "I am planning twenty new houses in Stonebridge, you see. I wanted to know what the land was like in the past."

"Which land?" Amira asked. Mr. Pike opened his plans on the table. They showed a field near the river, with twenty small squares drawn on it. "Long Field," he said. "A beautiful place. Flat and green. My houses will be the first on that side of the town."

Leo, who was standing behind him, read the title of the plans aloud: "Pike Homes. Long Field. Twenty new houses by the river." He turned to Amira. "Dr. Kent, Mr. Blake's diary is about the great flood of 1830."

"Yes," said Amira thoughtfully. "A page about a flood could be a very expensive page for a man who wants to sell houses next to a river. If a book says that a field floods, nobody will buy a house there."
Mr. Pike's smile became smaller.
ch.clue: Twenty new houses by the river
ch.q: Why might Mr. Pike want that page to disappear?
o: It said that the river was dry in 1830
It showed that the church was very old
It described the first houses in Stonebridge
It could show that his building land floods
It listed the owners of Long Field
ch.hint: Bay Pike evleri nereye yapmak istiyor ve kesilen sayfa hangi olayı anlatıyor? İkisini birleştir.
ch.why: Pike nehir kenarındaki Long Field'a ev yapacaktı; sayfa, sel olayını anlatıyordu ve arazinin sel altında kaldığını kanıtlayabilirdi.

text: "Even if the page is gone," said Amira, "the flood is not." In the town museum there was a drawer full of old newspaper cuttings. Leo and Amira searched for an hour. At last Leo found a thin yellow paper, folded into four. It was a copy of the Stonebridge Gazette from 1831. The headline said: The Great Flood. An article, written by Mr. Blake himself, had been printed in it.

Amira read it aloud in the archive. "On the third night of the rain, the river rose and covered Long Field up to the wall of the church. Eleven houses were lost, and three families were taken to the schoolroom." She looked at Mr. Pike. "The field you want to build on was under the water. The same field, the same river, nearly two hundred years ago."
Mr. Pike looked at the floor for a long time. "I did not hurt the diary for money," he said finally, in a tired voice. "I was afraid. I had put all my savings into the plans."
"The truth is cheaper than a flood," said Amira, kindly but firmly.
ch.clue: covered Long Field up to the wall of the church
ch.q: What does the old newspaper copy prove?
o: Long Field was flooded in 1830, as the missing page said
The church was built on Long Field in 1831
Mr. Blake never wrote about a flood
The flood destroyed only the museum
Mr. Pike had read the article before
ch.hint: Gazete kupüründe sel hangi araziyi kapladığını yazıyor? Bu bilgi, kesilen sayfanın içeriğiyle nasıl bağlantılı?
ch.why: Gazete, selin Long Field'ı kilise duvarına kadar kapladığını yazıyordu; kesilen sayfadaki bilgi doğru çıktı.

outro: Sayfanın kopyası belediyeye teslim edildi ve yeni evlerin planı yeniden yapıldı. Amira, Leo'ya şunu söyledi: yazılı bir kaydı yok etmek, o olayı unutturmaz; yalnızca başka kayıtları aramamıza neden olur.

title: The Slow Freezer
hero: Bilim insanı Dr. Ilan Voss ve asistanı Dana
intro: Dana, dondurucuya koyduğu birkaç fincan suyun beklenenden farklı hızlarda donduğunu fark etti. Dr. Ilan Voss ile asistanı Dana, tuzun ve şekerin donmayı nasıl etkilediğini ve sonucun neden karıştığını araştırıyor.

text: It was a cold Monday, and Dr. Ilan Voss was drinking his tea when his assistant Dana burst into the lab. "Ilan, you must see this," she said. "I put four cups of liquid in the freezer last night. Look at them now."

Ilan followed her. The freezer was a big white box with a thermometer on the door. It showed minus five degrees. Inside were four plastic cups, each with a label. Cup A was full of plain water, and it was completely frozen, like a small block of ice. Cup B had salty water. It was still liquid, with only a few small ice crystals on the top. Cup C had sugar water, and it was half frozen, soft like a slush. Cup D also had plain water, but its label said: Top shelf, near the door. It was almost liquid.
"Same freezer," said Dana. "Same amount of liquid in every cup. But they are not the same at all."
Ilan looked at the four cups for a long time. "Interesting," he said. "Let us begin with the cups that are easiest to compare. A and B."
ch.clue: Cup B had salty water
ch.q: What is different about Cup B compared with Cup A?
o: Cup B had salt in the water
Cup B had a plastic lid
Cup B was much colder at the start
Cup B was on a different shelf
Cup B had less liquid in it
ch.hint: Etiketlere bak: A fincanında sade su, B fincanında ne var? Dana'nın "aynı dondurucu, aynı miktar" demesini de hesaba kat.
ch.why: A fincanı sade suydu, B fincanında tuzlu su vardı; aralarındaki fark tuzdu.

text: "Salt keeps water liquid at a lower temperature," Ilan explained. "That is why we put salt on the roads in winter. So salty water freezes later than plain water. Cup B is easy to explain, and Cup C also fits. Sugar does the same thing, only not as strongly."
"But what about Cup D?" asked Dana. "It is plain water, like Cup A. It should be frozen, but it is almost liquid."

Ilan went to the freezer again and looked at the thermometer more carefully. There was a second small thermometer, in the corner, on the top shelf next to the door. He bent down and read it aloud. "Minus one degree," he said. "The big one on the door says minus five. But this little one, on the top shelf, says minus one. The top shelf near the door is much warmer."
"Because every time we open the door, the warm air from the room goes in," said Dana. "And it stays on the top."
"Exactly," said Ilan. "Water freezes below zero. At minus one, it freezes very slowly."
ch.clue: on the top shelf next to the door
ch.q: Why did the plain water in Cup D freeze so slowly?
o: The cup was made of different plastic
There was less water in that cup
That shelf was warmer than the rest of the freezer
The water in that cup was salty
Dana forgot to close the freezer door
ch.hint: Kapının yanındaki üst rafta küçük termometre kaç dereceyi gösteriyor ve su sıfırın altında ne kadar hızlı donar? Kapı açıldığında içeri ne girer?
ch.why: Kapıya yakın üst raf daha sıcaktı (eksi bir derece); orada su çok yavaş donuyordu.

text: Dana took the four cups out and put them on the table. "So the result is mixed," she said. "Cup B was slow because of the salt. Cup C was slow because of the sugar. But Cup D was slow because of the shelf. If I had not looked at the labels, I would have said that the cup itself was strange."

"That is the trouble," said Ilan. "We wanted to find the effect of salt and sugar. But we changed more than one thing at the same time. Cup D was different in a second way, which was the place. If Cup B and Cup C had been on the warm shelf too, we would never know which reason was stronger."

He drew four small boxes on the white board and wrote the word shelf under each. "To compare fairly, only one thing may change," he said. "Everything else must be the same: the amount of liquid, the temperature, the place."
Dana wrote it in her notebook: Only the liquid changes. Everything else is the same. Then she looked at Ilan and smiled. "Tomorrow, then, we start again."
ch.clue: only one thing may change
ch.q: What should Ilan do to make the experiment fair?
o: Use bigger cups for the sugar water
Put the cups in the freezer for a longer time
Use only salty water in every cup
Open the door more often to check the cups
Put all the cups on the same shelf and change only the liquid
ch.hint: Adil bir karşılaştırmada yalnızca bir şey değişmeli. Fincanlar farklı rafta olursa neyi yanlış yorumlarız?
ch.why: Tüm fincanlar aynı rafa konmalı ve yalnızca sıvı farklı olmalıydı; böylece sonuç tek bir nedene bağlanabilirdi.

text: The next morning, the freezer was empty and clean. Dana arranged the four cups in a perfect row on the middle shelf, far from the door, where the temperature was exactly minus five degrees. She poured the same amount of liquid into each one: plain water in A, salty water in B, sugar water in C, and plain water again in D. Each cup was the same plastic, the same size, and had the same lid.

At lunchtime, the cups were checked. Cup A was a solid white block. Cup D, plain water too, was exactly the same as Cup A. Cup C, with sugar, was only half frozen. Cup B, with salt, was still almost completely liquid.
Dana laughed. "A and D are twins now!" she said. "And the shelf was really the problem."
"Now the experiment tells us one clear story," said Ilan. "Plain water freezes first, sugar water later, and salt water last. And when two cups hold the same liquid, they freeze in the same time."
ch.clue: A and D are twins now
ch.q: What does the second experiment show about the earlier mistake?
o: The thermometer on the door was broken
The shelf, not the cup, had slowed down Cup D
The plastic of Cup D was a different kind
Cup D was filled with sugar water by mistake
Cups should never be put in the freezer
ch.hint: A ve D artık aynı sonucu veriyor. Bu ikisi arasındaki tek fark ilk denemede neydi ve ikinci denemede ne değişti?
ch.why: İkinci denemede A ve D aynı sürede dondu; ilk seferki yavaşlığın nedeni raf yeriydi, fincan değildi.

outro: Deney bu kez adil bir şekilde tekrarlandı ve sonuçlar net çıktı. Ilan, deney defterinin ilk sayfasına şunu yazdı: aynı koşullarda yapılmayan bir karşılaştırma, bir karşılaştırma değildir.

title: The School Rumour
hero: Muhabir Jonas Reid ve fotoğrafçı Ellie
intro: Kasabada Hill Okulu'nun haziranda kapanacağı söyleniyor. Sosyal medyada binlerce kişi bu haberi paylaştı ve anneler babalar çok telaşlı. Muhabir Jonas Reid ile fotoğrafçı Ellie, söylentinin nereden çıktığını ve gerçeğin ne olduğunu bulmaya çalışıyor.

text: On Tuesday morning, the phones at the Kingsbridge Daily did not stop ringing. Parents wanted to know if it was true that Hill School would close in June. Jonas Reid put the phone down and opened the town's Facebook page. The post with the rumour had been shared more than four hundred times. It was written by a man called Mr. Reed, and it said: Terrible news! Hill School will close in June. A friend of the mayor told me. Please sign our protest now!
Under the post, hundreds of people had written angry comments. Some of them wanted to march to the Town Hall on Friday. A mother had written: I will never send my child to another school.

Jonas read it twice, slowly. Ellie, who was looking at the screen over his shoulder, tapped it with her finger. "He does not say where he heard it, and he does not show any paper," she said. "He says that a friend of the mayor told him."
"Exactly," said Jonas. "That is not a source, it is a story about a story. Let us find the real one."
ch.clue: A friend of the mayor told me
ch.q: What is the weakest point of the Facebook post?
o: It was posted on a Tuesday morning
It repeats something heard from a friend, with no document
It was written by a man who has a child at the school
It was shared by too many people in the town
It uses too many angry words in the title
ch.hint: Bay Reed haberi nereden duyduğunu söylüyor ve herhangi bir belge gösteriyor mu? Bir haberin güvenilir olması için ne gerekir?
ch.why: Gönderi, "belediye başkanının bir arkadaşı söyledi" diyordu ama hiçbir belge göstermiyordu; kaynak ikinci elden bir söyleniydi.

text: Jonas phoned the Town Hall and asked to speak to the press officer. A calm woman named Mrs. Lowe answered. "The council has not discussed closing Hill School," she said. "Not today, not this year. But I know why you are calling. Half of the town has phoned me this morning."

"Is there a meeting?" asked Jonas. "Yes," said Mrs. Lowe. "The council meets on Thursday evening. The agenda is public. It is pinned on the notice board outside the Town Hall, and you can read it yourself. It has nine points. They are not very exciting. Most of them are about roads and rubbish."

"And nothing about the school?" Jonas asked carefully. "I did not say that," said Mrs. Lowe, and she laughed. "There is a small point about the school area. Go and read it, and then tell me what you think. I have to run now."
Jonas put the phone down and looked at Ellie. "She did not say yes, and she did not say no. She said: read the paper," he said. "Let us take our cameras."
ch.clue: The agenda is public
ch.q: What did Mrs. Lowe tell Jonas to do?
o: Phone the mayor to ask about the school
Ask Mr. Reed for his friend's name
Wait for the council meeting on Thursday
Read the public agenda on the notice board
Write an article before Thursday evening
ch.hint: Basın sorumlusu nerede ve hangi belgeyi okumasını önerdi? "Evet de demedi, hayır da demedi" cümlesi neyi anlatıyor?
ch.why: Mrs. Lowe, Belediye binasının önündeki panoda asılı olan herkese açık gündemi okumasını söyledi.

text: The notice board stood outside the Town Hall, between a poster for a dance class and a lost-cat notice. Ellie photographed the whole page, and Jonas read it aloud, line by line. Point one was the budget for the park. Point two was a new bin at the market. Point three was the repair of Church Street.

"Point four," he read, and stopped. "School Area: closure of the Main Street bus stop near Hill School, from the first of June. Pupils will use the new stop on Hill Road." He read the line a second time. "Closure of the stop," he repeated.
Ellie leaned closer. "So the council will close a bus stop, not a school," she said.

"Somebody saw 'Hill School' and the word 'closure' on the same line," said Jonas, "and the rest of the story made itself. That is how rumours work. People do not read all the words. They read the scary ones. And a friend of a friend repeats them."
Ellie smiled. "A whole town in panic because of a bus stop," she said. "I will take a photo of it."
ch.clue: closure of the Main Street bus stop
ch.q: How did the rumour about the school probably start?
o: Someone read "closure" next to "Hill School" and misunderstood
Mr. Reed made up the story to get attention
The mayor told his friend that the school was poor
The newspaper printed the wrong agenda last week
The council secretly planned to close the school
ch.hint: Gündemin dördüncü maddesi tam olarak neyin kapanacağını söylüyor? Hangi iki kelime yan yana gelince yanlış anlama çıkmış olabilir?
ch.why: Gündem maddesi, okulun değil okul yakınındaki otobüs durağının kapanacağını söylüyordu; "kapanış" kelimesi yanlış anlaşıldı.

text: Back in the office, Mrs. Cole, the editor, asked Jonas for three possible headlines for the front page. He wrote them on a sheet of paper and read them aloud. The first one said: Hill School to close in June. The second said: Council denies all rumours about school. The third was longer and more careful. It said that the council was going to close a bus stop near Hill School, that the school itself would stay open, and that pupils would use a new stop on Hill Road.

"The first is wrong," said Mrs. Cole. "The second is vague. It would only make people more nervous." She tapped the third. "This one answers every parent's question. It says what is true, and it says it simply."
Ellie added a photo of the bus stop with the old yellow sign, and a second photo of the notice board. "Photos prove it," she said.
Mr. Reed called that afternoon to say he was sorry. "I only wanted to protect our children," he said. Jonas answered gently, "Next time, please read the paper first."
ch.clue: the school itself would stay open
ch.q: Which headline gives the most accurate information?
o: Council denies everything about Hill School
Hill School to close in June, say angry parents
Council to close a bus stop near Hill School; school stays open
Mr. Reed starts a protest at the Town Hall
Town votes against the new bus stop on Hill Road
ch.hint: Doğru başlık, söylentiyi düzeltmeli ve tam olarak ne kapanıyor, ne açık kalıyor, öğrenciler nereyi kullanacak sorularını yanıtlamalı.
ch.why: Doğru başlık, okulun açık kaldığını ve yalnızca bir otobüs durağının kapandığını açıkça söyleyen cümleydi.

outro: Gazete ertesi gün doğru haberi yayımladı: okul açık kalıyor, yalnızca bir otobüs durağı kapanıyor. Jonas, bir söylentiyi durdurmanın en iyi yolunun belgeye bakmak olduğunu bir kez daha gördü.

title: The Empty Nest
hero: Park korucusu Wren Calder ve köpeği Bracken
intro: Kayalıktaki nadir bir kuşun yuvası bir sabah boş bulundu. Yumurtalar kaybolmuş. Park korucusu Wren Calder ile köpeği Bracken, yumurtaları kimin aldığını anlamak için küçük işaretlere bakıyor.

text: The Red Cliff rose over the sea like a wall, grey and brown, and the wind blew very strongly. On a narrow ledge, about ten metres above the beach, a rare bird called the shelduck had built its nest. Ranger Wren Calder had been checking it every morning for two weeks, with a pair of binoculars.

On Wednesday, the nest was empty. Wren stood on the beach with her dog Bracken and looked up, and she knew at once. The nest was still there, a soft round bowl of grass and feathers. But the four white eggs that had lain in it yesterday were gone.

She climbed up carefully with a rope, until she could see inside. The nest was clean and undamaged. Not a single piece of shell lay in it, and not one drop of egg stained the grass. Near the edge she found one small black feather, and nothing else.
"So," she said to Bracken, who was waiting below, "the thief did not break the eggs here. He took them whole and carried them away."
ch.clue: Not a single piece of shell lay in it
ch.q: What does the clean nest without any shell tell Wren?
o: The eggs broke and fell into the sea
A storm blew the eggs out of the nest
The thief carried the eggs away whole
The mother bird ate the eggs herself
The eggs hatched and the chicks flew away
ch.hint: Yuvada kırık kabuk ya da yumurta lekesi var mı? Bu durumda yumurtalar yuvadan nasıl alınmış olmalı?
ch.why: Yuvada ne kabuk parçası ne de yumurta lekesi vardı; hırsız yumurtaları bütün olarak götürmüştü.

text: Back on the beach, Wren studied the ground below the cliff. The sand was damp and smooth after the night tide, and it would show any animal's footprints very clearly. She walked from one end of the cliff to the other, and Bracken followed with his nose down. They found the prints of seagulls, of Bracken himself, and of an early walker with a small dog. There were no prints of a fox.

"A fox would love eggs," said Wren, "and there are plenty of foxes in these hills. But a fox cannot climb a straight cliff for ten metres. Even if it could, it would leave dirt and scratches on the rock."

She went back to the cliff and looked at the rock under the ledge with her magnifying glass. It was perfectly clean. No scratches, no hair, no earth. "A fox is not our thief," she said finally. "Whoever took the eggs arrived from above or from the air, and left in the same way."
Bracken looked at the sky as if he agreed.
ch.clue: a fox cannot climb a straight cliff
ch.q: Which animal is the least likely thief?
o: A large hawk
An owl
A crow
A gull
A fox
ch.hint: Tilki yumurtaları sever, ama kayalığın dibindeki kumda ya da kayanın üzerinde onun izi var mı? Dümdüz bir kayalığa tırmanabilir mi?
ch.why: Kumda tilki izi yoktu ve kaya temizdi; tilki düz kayalığa tırmanamazdı, hırsız havadan gelmişti.

text: Wren had one more tool. Two weeks earlier she had fixed a small camera on a rock near the nest. It took a picture every time something moved. She took the memory card out and put it into her laptop. There were hundreds of pictures of grass and wind. Then, in the grey morning light, one clear picture appeared: 6:10 a.m.

A large black bird stood on the edge of the nest. It had a grey patch on its neck and a thick, strong beak. In the next picture, taken one second later, it flew away with something white in its beak. In the third picture, the nest was empty. The time stamp said 6:11.

"A hooded crow," said Wren, enlarging the picture. "Those grey feathers are very clear. They are clever birds, and they love eggs." Then she looked at the picture before the crow's arrival, taken at 5:58. In that photo, the mother shelduck was leaving the nest and flying toward the sea, to find food.
"The crow waited," she said. "As soon as the mother went away, it came."
ch.clue: A large black bird stood on the edge of the nest
ch.q: Which animal took the eggs, according to the camera?
o: A small hawk
A hooded crow
A shelduck
A fox
A seagull
ch.hint: Kameranın 6:10'daki fotoğrafında yuvanın kenarında hangi kuş var? Boynundaki gri leke ve kalın gaga hangi hayvanı anlatıyor?
ch.why: Fotoğrafta boynunda gri leke olan, kalın gagalı siyah bir karga yumurtaları götürürken görülüyordu.

text: In April, the mother shelduck laid four new eggs on the same ledge. Wren was worried. The crow was still in the area, and it knew exactly where the nest was. She checked the camera pictures again and wrote a short list in her notebook: 5:58, the mother leaves the nest. 6:10, the crow arrives. Twelve minutes later, the eggs are gone. Every morning, the mother left to feed for about twenty minutes.

"The only moment of danger is the time when the nest is alone," Wren said to the young volunteer who was helping her. "We cannot stop the mother from eating. And we cannot stop the crow from being a crow."

"So what can we do?" asked the volunteer. Wren looked at the nest for a long time. "We can make the nest hard to reach," she said. "A light green net, over the top of it, with a small hole at the side. The mother is small, and she can pass through. The crow is big, and it cannot."
The next morning the crow arrived again at 6:10. It walked around the net, pushed it with its beak, and flew away angry.
ch.clue: the mother left to feed for about twenty minutes
ch.q: What is the best way to protect the new eggs?
o: A loud radio near the nest all morning
Moving the eggs to a nest on the beach
Taking the mother bird to a safe room
A net with a hole only big enough for the mother
Feeding the crow so that it forgets the eggs
ch.hint: Tehlike, yuva yalnız kaldığı yaklaşık yirmi dakikada ortaya çıkıyor. Hem anne kuşun girip çıkabileceği hem de büyük karganın giremeyeceği bir çözüm düşün.
ch.why: Yuvayı, yalnızca küçük anne kuşun geçebileceği bir delik bırakan ağla kapatmak karganın erişimini engelliyordu.

outro: Yuvaya bir koruma ağı gerildi ve bir sonraki yumurtalar güvenle çatladı. Wren, kuş gözlem defterine şunu yazdı: bir canlıyı korumak için önce onu kimin tehdit ettiğini bilmek gerekir.

title: The Silent Alarm
hero: Küratör Hugo Laurent ve güvenlik görevlisi Mina
intro: Müzedeki ünlü altın sikke, vitrinden kayboldu. Alarm ise hiç çalmadı. Küratör Hugo Laurent ile güvenlik görevlisi Mina, alarmın neden sustuğunu ve sikkenin nerede olduğunu bulmaya çalışıyor.

text: On Monday morning, Mina arrived at the museum and walked to her favourite room as usual. In the middle of it, under a spotlight, stood a glass case, and in the case there should have been the museum's greatest treasure: the Golden Lion, a small coin of pure gold, two thousand years old.
The case was empty. The glass was clean, the lock was closed and the red cloth where the coin usually lay was still there, with a round shape in the middle of it. But the coin was gone.

Mina ran to the control room and looked at the alarm panel, a small grey box on the wall with a keypad and a screen. She expected a long list of red warnings. Instead, the screen said, in calm green letters: Alarm OFF 11:50 p.m. – 12:10 a.m. User code accepted. Everything else was normal. Nobody had broken a window. No door had opened by force.
"The alarm did not fail," Mina said to herself. "It was switched off on purpose, by somebody who knew the code."
ch.clue: User code accepted
ch.q: What does the alarm panel tell Mina?
o: A thief broke the glass and the alarm
The alarm was broken by a power cut
The alarm was never turned on that night
Someone who knew the code turned off the alarm
The panel is old and shows a wrong time
ch.hint: Panelde "kod kabul edildi" yazıyor ve hiçbir pencere kırılmamış. Alarmın susmasının en mantıklı nedeni ne olabilir?
ch.why: Ekranda 11:50-12:10 arasında alarmın kapatıldığı ve kodun kabul edildiği yazıyordu; kodu bilen biri alarmı kapatmıştı.

text: Hugo Laurent arrived with a tired face and a cup of coffee. He listened to Mina and read the panel. "Who knows the alarm code?" he asked. Mina counted slowly. "I changed it last Friday," she said. "I told only two people: you, and Mr. Pell, the museum manager. I wrote it nowhere."

"And the cleaner, Mr. Okoro?" Hugo asked. "He comes at six in the morning, when the alarm is already off," said Mina. "He never needed the code, so I did not give it to him. And I remember that he told me not to give it."

Hugo put down his cup. "Then it was used by you, by me or by Mr. Pell," he said. "I was at home with my family. You were at home, too, and you did not leave the house until six. So there is only one name left."
Mina looked at him. "Mr. Pell?"
"I do not say he is a thief," said Hugo carefully. "But let us ask him why his code was used at ten to midnight."
ch.clue: I changed it last Friday
ch.q: Who could have used the code on Sunday night?
o: Hugo, Mina or Mr. Pell
Every visitor who came on Sunday
Nobody, because the code was secret
Only Mr. Okoro, the cleaner
Only Mina, who changed the code
ch.hint: Mina kodu yalnızca kime vermiş ve temizlikçiye neden vermemiş? Kodu bilen kişi sayısını bul.
ch.why: Mina kodu yalnızca Hugo'ya ve müdür Pell'e vermişti; kodu bilenler bu üç kişiydi.

text: Mr. Pell, a short man with a neat grey moustache, was in his office, drinking tea. When Hugo and Mina walked in, he did not look surprised. "Ah, you want to know about the coin," he said. "Yes, I turned off the alarm at ten to twelve. I came back after the concert dinner."

"You came to the museum at midnight?" said Mina, shocked. "To move the Golden Lion?" Mr. Pell nodded. "The insurance company is coming this morning to photograph it. They asked me to prepare it. I took it out of the case and put it in the safe, so that the photographer can use the good light of the safe room. I left a note under the case, as I always do. Did you not see it?"

Mina ran back to the room and knelt beside the glass case. Under the red cloth, folded in four, there was a small white paper. It said: The Golden Lion is in the safe for insurance photographs. Back at 10 a.m. M. Pell. She had not lifted the cloth.
"I did not see it," she said, laughing and blushing at the same time.
ch.clue: The Golden Lion is in the safe
ch.q: Where is the Golden Lion?
o: At the insurance company's office
In the cleaner's room behind the café
In the museum safe, prepared for photographs
In Mr. Pell's bag, taken home for the night
In a hidden box under the museum floor
ch.hint: Pell'in bıraktığı notta sikke için ne yazıyor? Notu neden ilk bakışta görmediler?
ch.why: Not, sikkenin sigorta fotoğrafları için kasada olduğunu söylüyordu; Pell onu kasaya kaldırmıştı.

text: At ten o'clock, the photographer from the insurance company arrived, and the Golden Lion went back into its case, shining under the spotlight. The photographer took forty pictures and went away with a happy face.

Hugo called Mina, Mr. Pell and Mr. Okoro to his office. "Nobody did anything wrong in a dishonest way," he said. "But we made three small mistakes. Mr. Pell hid his note under the cloth, where it was hard to see. Mina and I did not know the plan. And the alarm panel does not tell us who turned it off."

He took a pen and wrote three new rules on a big sheet of paper. Number one: any object that is moved must be reported to the security officer before the move. Number two: the note must be put on the glass, in the open. Number three: the alarm panel must show the name of the person who used the code.
"That would have saved all of us a very nervous morning," said Mina.
Mr. Pell nodded and took the pen. "I will sign first," he said.
ch.clue: any object that is moved must be reported
ch.q: Which new rule would have prevented this problem best?
o: Close the museum on Mondays
Never let a cleaner enter the room at six
Put every treasure in the safe at night
Change the alarm code every single day
Report any move of an object to security before it happens
ch.hint: Sorunun kökü, bir eşyanın yerinin değiştirilmesinin güvenlik görevlisine haber verilmemesiydi. Bunu önleyecek kural hangisi?
ch.why: Sorun, taşınan eşyanın güvenliğe önceden bildirilmemesiydi; böyle bir kural bu sabahki paniği önlerdi.

outro: Sikke yerine kondu ve müdüre yeni bir kural yazıldı: bir eşyayı yerinden oynatan kişi, bunu herkese yazılı olarak duyuracak. Hugo, Mina'ya teşekkür etti.

title: The Colour Library
hero: Oyun testçileri Zoe ve Max
intro: Zoe ve Max bu kez "Renkli Kütüphane" adlı yeni bir kaçış odasını deniyor. Kapı kilitlendi, yeşil bir ışık yanıyor. Çıkmak için kitapların renklerini, sayıları ve odanın haritasını kullanmaları gerekiyor.

text: The door closed with a soft click, and a green light began to count down from sixty minutes. Zoe and Max were standing in a small round room. The walls were covered with shelves, and in front of them, on a wooden table, stood four books, each with a different colour: red, green, blue and yellow. A piece of paper lay open beside them.
"A poem," said Max, and read it aloud. "First comes the light of the morning sun. Then the wide sea, where the ships run. Then the leaf, in spring so new. Last of all, the apple, red as dew."

"It is a list," Zoe said, taking the books one by one. "We have to put the books in the order of the poem. The sun, the sea, the leaf and the apple. But I want to be sure about each colour before I move anything."
Max looked at the four books, then at the poem again, and slowly lifted the first one.
ch.clue: First comes the light of the morning sun
ch.q: In which order should the books be placed?
o: Blue, yellow, red, green
Yellow, green, blue, red
Green, red, yellow, blue
Red, green, blue, yellow
Yellow, blue, green, red
ch.hint: Şiirdeki her varlığı bir renkle eşleştir: güneş, deniz, yaprak, elma. Sonra şiirdeki sıraya uy.
ch.why: Şiir güneş (sarı), deniz (mavi), yaprak (yeşil), elma (kırmızı) sırasını veriyordu.

text: The books went onto the shelf, left to right, and when the last one touched the wood, a small drawer slid open with a gentle noise. In the drawer there was a metal box with a number lock, four wheels from 0 to 9. On a small card Max read: Each book has a number hidden on its back. The numbers will talk to the box.

The two friends took the books out again and turned them over. On the spine of each book, in tiny gold letters, there was a single number. The yellow book had a 3. The blue one had a 1. The green one had a 4. The red one had a 2.

"The order of the poem again?" asked Max. Zoe shook her head. "No, think. The card says that the numbers talk to the box. The box has four wheels, and the books are in the right order on the shelf now. I think we should read the numbers from left to right, exactly as the books stand."
Max put his fingers on the four wheels and waited for her to say the first number.
ch.clue: The yellow book had a 3
ch.q: What is the code for the box?
ch.hint: Kitapların rafta soldan sağa doğru hangi sırada durduğunu hatırla (önceki bölüm). Sonra her kitabın sırtındaki sayıyı o sırayla oku.
ch.why: Kitaplar sarı, mavi, yeşil, kırmızı sırasındaydı ve sırt sayıları 3, 1, 4, 2'ydi; kod 3142'ydi.

text: The box clicked and opened. Inside they found a folded map and a small compass made of brass. The map showed the room from above, like a plan. It was a circle, with the door at the bottom and a small round window at the top. At the bottom of the map there was a sentence: The key is under the lamp that stands in the east.

"East," said Max. "But which side is east?" Zoe took the brass compass from the box. She held it flat in the palm of her hand, and the needle trembled and slowly stopped. "The needle points north," she said. "And look, the window is exactly on the north side."

They both turned toward the window and looked around the room. On the right-hand side, from where they stood, there was a tall lamp with a green shade. On the left-hand side stood an identical lamp with a red shade. "Which one?" asked Max, and he looked at Zoe.
ch.clue: The key is under the lamp that stands in the east
ch.q: Where was the key hidden?
o: Behind the books on the left side of the room
Under the lamp with the red shade
Inside the compass that Zoe was holding
Under the lamp with the green shade
Under the table where the books were
ch.hint: Pusula kuzeyi gösteriyor ve pencere kuzey tarafında. Kuzeye bakan birinin sağ eli hangi yönü gösterir? Hangi lamba o tarafta?
ch.why: Pencere kuzeyde olduğu için pencereye bakan kişinin sağı doğuydu; yeşil abajurlu lamba sağdaydı ve anahtar onun altındaydı.

text: The key opened a low wooden door that Zoe had never noticed, hidden between two shelves. Behind it there was a very small room, and in the middle of it, a steel door with a keypad and two digits on the screen: _ _. Above the keypad, a short message was written in white chalk: Add the books on the red shelf to the chairs in the room. Two digits only.

"The red shelf," said Max. "That is the shelf with a red line. How many books?" They counted carefully. There were seven books on it, all with the same brown covers. "Seven," said Zoe. "And the chairs?" They looked around the round room and the tiny room, and counted: one, two, three. "Three chairs."

"Seven books and three chairs," said Max, and looked at the keypad. It waited for two digits, with a small cursor blinking on the screen. The clock on the wall said four minutes, and neither of them was laughing now.
ch.clue: Add the books on the red shelf to the chairs
ch.q: Which two digits open the last door?
ch.hint: Mesaj iki şeyi toplamanı söylüyor: kırmızı raftaki kitaplar ve sandalyeler. Her birinin sayısını bul ve topla.
ch.why: Kırmızı rafta yedi kitap, odalarda üç sandalye vardı; yedi artı üç ondur.

outro: Kapı açıldı ve Zoe ile Max bir kez daha birlikte çıktı. Zoe, Max'e gülümsedi: iyi bir bulmaca, her ipucunu kullandırır.

title: The Wrong Platform
hero: Havalimanı görevlisi Dara Mills ve stajyer Sam
intro: Bir istasyonda yolcu Mr. Ortiz, trenini kaçırdı çünkü ekranda yazan peron ile hoparlörden duyduğu peron farklıydı. Görevli Dara Mills ile stajyer Sam, hatanın nasıl olduğunu ve Mr. Ortiz'in toplantısına yetişip yetişemeyeceğini araştırıyor.

text: Mr. Ortiz arrived at Northgate Station at five to nine in the morning, with a black suitcase and a worried face. He had to be in Leeds before half past twelve for an important job meeting. He looked at the big board above the hall. It said: 09:05, Leeds, Platform 6.

He walked quickly to Platform 6 and sat down on a bench, breathing hard. At 9:03, a voice came from the speaker above his head. "Attention, please. The 9:05 train to Leeds will leave from Platform 4." Mr. Ortiz did not hear it, because a bus was passing in the street. At 9:05, a long white train left Platform 4, and Mr. Ortiz watched the empty tracks in front of him.
He ran to the information desk, where Dara Mills, the officer, was drinking coffee next to her trainee Sam. "The board told me Platform 6," he said, almost shouting. "I trusted the board!"
"Please sit down," said Dara kindly. "We will find out what happened."
ch.clue: Leeds, Platform 6
ch.q: Why did Mr. Ortiz miss the train?
o: The board and the announcement gave different platforms
He went to the wrong city, Leeds
The train left earlier than the planned time
He arrived at the station too late for the train
He did not buy a ticket for the train
ch.hint: Büyük ekran peron altıyı gösteriyordu, hoparlör ise başka bir peron söyledi. Mr. Ortiz neye güvendi ve neyi duymadı?
ch.why: Ekranda altıncı peron yazıyordu, anons ise dördüncü perondan kalkacağını söylemişti; Mr. Ortiz ekrana güvenmişti.

text: Dara opened the station's computer log, a long list of times and messages. Sam looked over her shoulder. "Here it is," she said. "At 8:45 the system received the usual plan: Leeds train, Platform 6. At 9:00, the staff received a change from the signal room: the Leeds train must use Platform 4, because of a broken door on Platform 6. And at 9:02, somebody typed the change into the system."
"So the change was made two minutes after the board had shown the old plan," said Sam. "But then the board should have changed, too."

"It should have," said Dara. "But the board did not show Platform 4 at any time. Look at the last line of the log. It says: Change saved to Computer 2." She looked at Sam. "The announcement went through, because that is read from this desk. But the board did not change."
Sam looked at the line again. "Computer 2?" he said slowly. "Dara, I think that is not the board's computer."
ch.clue: Change saved to Computer 2
ch.q: What happened to the platform change?
o: The change was typed twice on the same computer
The change was cancelled by the signal room
The change reached the speaker but not the board
The change arrived at 9:20, after the train left
The change reached the board but not the speaker
ch.hint: Kayıtta değişiklik ne zaman girilmiş ve nereye kaydedilmiş? Anons masadan okunuyor; ekran ise başka bir bilgisayara bağlı olabilir.
ch.why: Değişiklik anons için iletilmişti ama ekranı yöneten bilgisayara kaydedilmemişti.

text: In the staff room there were two computers on the same desk, almost identical. Each had a small yellow sticker on the screen. The sticker on the left one said: Computer 1: Board link. The sticker on the right one said: Computer 2: Announcements.

Sam turned red, from the neck to the ears. "I did it," he said softly. "At two minutes past nine, the signal room phoned, and I typed the change. I was in a hurry, and I used the first computer that was free."
"And the free one was Computer 2," said Dara.

"Yes," said Sam. "I did not read the stickers. I am so sorry, Mr. Ortiz would have caught his train if..." Dara put her hand on his shoulder. "Sam, look at me. You made a mistake, but the system made it very easy to make. Two computers, two stickers, and the same desk. It will happen again with another trainee, unless we change something."
She looked at the two computers. "A system must be safe for people who are tired and in a hurry," she said.
ch.clue: I used the first computer that was free
ch.q: What went wrong with the platform change?
o: Sam forgot to phone the signal room
The board computer was turned off
Dara did not read the log in time
The signal room sent the wrong platform
Sam typed the change on the wrong computer
ch.hint: Çıkartmalar hangi bilgisayarın neyi yönettiğini söylüyor? Sam değişikliği hangi bilgisayarda yazdı?
ch.why: Sam değişikliği ekranı yöneten bilgisayara değil, anonsların yapıldığı ikinci bilgisayara yazmıştı.

text: Dara first solved the problem for Mr. Ortiz. She checked the timetable on the wall. "The next train to Leeds leaves at 10:20 from Platform 2," she said. "It arrives at 12:05. Your meeting is at half past twelve, and the office is only fifteen minutes from the station by taxi."

Mr. Ortiz counted slowly. "A quarter past twelve at the earliest," he said, "and that gives me fifteen minutes before the meeting." Dara nodded. "And of course, the ticket is free, as an apology. Sam will walk with you to the platform, and he will check the platform number twice, on the board and on the speaker."
Sam smiled for the first time. "I promise," he said.

Before they left, Dara took a pen and wrote two new notes: one for the left computer and one for the right one. In large red letters they said: Platform changes: ALWAYS type on Computer 1 first. "Now it is almost impossible to make the same mistake," she said.
ch.clue: arrives at 12:05
ch.q: Will Mr. Ortiz arrive at his meeting on time?
o: Yes, but only if he runs to the station
Yes, he will arrive about fifteen minutes early
It is impossible to say from the story
No, he will arrive after the meeting begins
No, because the next train is full
ch.hint: Tren saat kaçta Leeds'e varıyor, taksiyle ofise gitmek ne kadar sürüyor ve toplantı saat kaçta? Süreleri topla ve karşılaştır.
ch.why: Tren 12:05'te varıyordu, taksiyle on beş dakika sürecekti; toplantıdan yaklaşık on beş dakika önce ofisinde olacaktı.

outro: Bilgisayarlar etiketlendi ve Mr. Ortiz toplantıya yetişti. Dara, Sam'e şunu söyledi: bir hatayı düzeltmek iyidir, ama bir daha olmasını engellemek daha iyidir.

title: The Forged Ticket
hero: Dedektif Edmund Crane ve yardımcısı Tess
intro: Royal Hall'daki büyük konserde aynı koltuk için iki kişi bilet gösteriyor. Biri sahte olmalı. Dedektif Edmund Crane ile yardımcısı Tess, sahte bileti ve onu üreten kişiyi bulmak için konser salonuna geliyor.

text: It was seven o'clock on Friday evening, and the great hall of the Royal Hall was full of music and laughter. But at the door of Row C, there was a problem. Mr. Lane, a tall man in a grey suit, was holding a ticket for seat C12. Next to him stood Ms. Cho, a young woman in a red coat, with a ticket for the same seat, C12.
"It is my seat," said Mr. Lane, quietly but firmly. "It is mine," said Ms. Cho, nearly crying. "I paid forty pounds."

Edmund Crane and Tess had come to listen to the concert, but now they stood between the two. The doorman, Mr. Boyd, took both tickets and explained to the detectives. "Every genuine ticket has a secret mark," he said. "If you tilt it under the light, a tiny silver star appears in the corner. The Royal Hall has used this mark for years."

Crane held Mr. Lane's ticket under the lamp and turned it slowly. A tiny silver star shone in the corner. Then he did the same with Ms. Cho's ticket. The corner stayed flat and plain, with only a painted silver spot.
"Well," said Crane. "That is a beginning."
ch.clue: a tiny silver star appears in the corner
ch.q: Which ticket is probably fake, and why?
o: Mr. Lane's, because it has a silver star
Ms. Cho's, because it has no star when tilted
Both are fake, because the seat is the same
Neither is fake, because both cost money
Ms. Cho's, because she wears a red coat
ch.hint: Doorman gerçek biletlerin ışığa tutulunca ne gösterdiğini anlatıyor. Hangi biletin köşesinde bu işaret görünüyor, hangisinde sadece düz bir leke var?
ch.why: Gerçek biletlerde ışığa tutulunca gümüş yıldız görünüyordu; Ms. Cho'nun biletinde yalnızca boyanmış bir leke vardı.

text: "I did not buy my ticket from the box office," Ms. Cho admitted. "A man was selling tickets outside the station. He said the concert was nearly full, and he had a few extra ones. I thought I was lucky."

Crane asked Mr. Boyd to show him the box office list for that evening. It was a single sheet of paper, with a neat title: Friday concert, 400 seats. Each ticket had a number, starting at 0001. Mr. Boyd explained that the Hall printed exactly four hundred tickets for each concert and that the last number was always 0400.
Crane looked at the fake ticket again. In the top corner, in small black numbers, it said: No. 0412.
"Twelve more than the last real number," said Tess. "A forger is a very clever person, but he forgot to count."
Crane smiled. "He copied the style of the ticket well, but he did not know how many tickets existed. Someone who knew would have chosen a number between one and four hundred."
ch.q: What proves that Ms. Cho's ticket is not a real Royal Hall ticket?
o: It does not show the name of the concert
Its number is lower than the first ticket
It was sold outside and not in the Hall
Its number is higher than the last real ticket
It was printed on very thin paper
ch.hint: O akşam için kaç bilet basılmış ve son numara kaç? Sahte biletin numarasıyla karşılaştır.
ch.why: O gece yalnızca 400 bilet basılmıştı; sahte biletin numarası 0412'ydi, yani gerçek olamazdı.

text: "A fake ticket needs paper, a printer and a way to cut it," said Crane. "Let me look at the edge." He asked Ms. Cho for a magnifying glass, and she, a little surprised, borrowed one from the cloakroom. Crane studied the edge of the false ticket for a long time. On the left side, near the corner, there was a very tiny notch, shaped like a small half moon.

"Real tickets are cut by the big paper cutter in the box office," said Mr. Boyd. "That machine has a small damaged place in the blade. Every ticket it cuts gets the same notch. I have noticed it for years, but nobody cares."
He took out a real ticket from his pocket, Mr. Lane's. On its left side, near the corner, the same tiny half moon.
"So the fake was cut by the same machine," said Crane quietly. "That means that the forger had access to the box office."
"But only two people work there," said Mr. Boyd. "Ms. Park, who has been here for twenty years. And Ed, our new student helper."
ch.clue: a very tiny notch, shaped like a small half moon
ch.q: What does the notch on the fake ticket tell Crane?
o: The fake was cut in the box office of the Hall
The fake was cut by Ms. Cho with scissors
The fake was printed in another city
The fake was made a long time ago
The fake was cut with the same blade as Mr. Lane's
ch.hint: Gerçek biletlerin kenarındaki küçük hilal çentik nereden geliyor? Sahte biletin de aynı çentiği taşıması ne anlama gelir?
ch.why: Çentik, gişedeki kâğıt kesicinin kusurlu bıçağından geliyordu; sahte bilet de gişede kesilmişti.

text: "Ms. Cho," said Crane gently, "can you describe the man who sold you the ticket?" The young woman closed her eyes. "Young, with a green scarf," she said. "He counted the money with his left hand, and he held the ticket with his right. I remember because it looked a little strange to me."

Crane and Tess walked to the box office. Ms. Park, a calm woman with silver hair, was counting coins, and she wrote the total in a book. She held the pen in her right hand. "I have worked here for twenty years," she said. "I never use green. I do not like green."

The second person sat in the corner, a nervous boy of twenty with a scarf round his neck. It was dark green. When Crane asked him about the paper cutter, he picked up a pair of scissors to cut a piece of paper, and he held them in his left hand.
"Ed," said Crane, "I think you have something to tell us."
The boy's face turned white, then red. "I only wanted to make a little extra money," he whispered.
ch.clue: He counted the money with his left hand
ch.q: Why does Crane think Ed made the fake tickets?
o: Ed was nervous when he met the two detectives
Ed had a better printer than Ms. Park
Ed is left-handed, wears a green scarf and works in the box office
Ed was the only person who knew about the star mark
Ed sold the tickets to Mr. Lane and Ms. Cho
ch.hint: Ms. Cho satıcının hangi elini kullandığını ve boynunda ne taktığını söylemişti. Gişedeki iki kişiyi bu iki ayrıntıyla karşılaştır.
ch.why: Satıcı solaklı, yeşil atkılıydı ve gişede çalışan Ed'in de aynı özellikleri vardı; Ms. Park ise sağlaklıydı ve yeşil sevmiyordu.

outro: Sahte biletleri yazdıran stajyer işten çıkarıldı ve Ms. Cho parasını geri aldı. Crane, Tess'e şunu dedi: sahtecilik, orijinal şeyi iyi bilen birinden gelir.

title: The Chicken Salad
hero: Genç doktor Mara Quinn ve hemşire Joe
intro: Çarşamba günü hastanenin üçüncü koğuşundaki beş hastanın midesi bozuldu. Doktor Mara Quinn ile hemşire Joe, hastaların ortak noktasını bulup hastalığa neyin neden olduğunu ve nasıl önlenebileceğini araştırıyor.

text: On Wednesday evening, nurse Joe came to the doctors' room with a worried face. "Doctor Quinn, five patients in Ward 3 have a bad stomach," he said. "They all began to feel sick between two and four o'clock. Fever, pain, and some of them cannot keep water down."

Mara went to the ward and looked at every bed. Mr. Hale, Mrs. Ingram, Mr. Frost, Ms. Kaya and Mr. Doyle. All of them looked tired and pale, but none was in danger. There were also three other patients in the ward, who felt perfectly well: Mr. Gray, Mrs. Stone and Mr. Ahmed.

"Today is a normal day," Mara said. "Same ward, same air, same visitors. So what did the five patients do that the three did not?" Joe held up the ward lunch list. On it were the names of all eight patients and their meals. Mr. Gray had pasta and a fruit salad. Mrs. Stone had soup and bread. Mr. Ahmed was not allowed to eat before an operation.
The five sick patients all had the same meal: chicken salad with bread.
"That cannot be a coincidence," said Mara.
ch.clue: The five sick patients all had the same meal
ch.q: What do the five sick patients have in common?
o: They all had the same visitors at midday
They all were older than seventy years
They all ate the chicken salad for lunch
They all slept in the same part of the ward
They all took the same medicine that morning
ch.hint: Hasta olanların yemek listelerine, sağlam kalanlarınkiyle birlikte bak. Beş hastanın ortak yaptığı ve diğer üç kişinin yapmadığı şey ne?
ch.why: Beş hastanın hepsi öğle yemeğinde tavuk salatası yemişti; sağlam kalan üçü yememişti.

text: Mara walked to the hospital kitchen with Joe. The head cook, Mr. Ruiz, was a calm man in a white hat. "Yes, the chicken salad was made at ten o'clock," he said proudly. "Fresh chicken, fresh vegetables. We always cook it carefully."

"And what happened after ten?" Mara asked. Mr. Ruiz pointed to a long steel table next to the oven. "The big bowl stayed here," he said. "The delivery truck was late, and the staff were very busy. We began to serve at one o'clock. Three hours later, I put it on the trays."

Mara looked at the table, then at the oven just beside it. The oven was warm, and the air around it was warm, too. She asked Mr. Ruiz to bring the kitchen thermometer, and she put it next to the bowl. It showed twenty-eight degrees.
"This is not a fridge," she said. "Chicken salad must be kept cold, below five degrees. After three hours at twenty-eight, bacteria grow very fast, even if everything was fresh at ten."
Mr. Ruiz looked down. "I did not think it was dangerous," he said softly.
ch.clue: It showed twenty-eight degrees
ch.q: Why did the chicken salad make the patients ill?
o: The chicken was old when it arrived at the kitchen
The salad was cooked for too many minutes
The cook did not wash the vegetables with water
The bowl was too dirty from the day before
It stayed for hours in a warm place and bacteria grew
ch.hint: Salata saat onda hazırlanmış ve servis saat birde başlamış. Bu üç saat boyunca kasenin durduğu yerin sıcaklığı kaç derece?
ch.why: Salata üç saat boyunca fırının yanındaki sıcak masada beklemişti; bakteriler sıcak ortamda hızla çoğalır.

text: "There is still one problem," Joe said, reading the lunch list again. "Mr. Doyle is sick, and his name is on the chicken salad list. But look at this: Mr. Gray, who ate the fruit salad, is well, and Mr. Ahmed, who did not eat, is well. There is one more name I have not checked, Mrs. Stone. She had soup and bread. She is fine, too."

"Which is exactly what we expect," said Mara. "So who is the problem?" Joe turned the page. At the bottom of the list there was a nineth line that he had not read: Mr. Ward, Bed 9, chicken salad. "Mr. Ward ate the chicken salad, but he is not sick," he said.

They went to see Mr. Ward, a sleepy old man with a big white moustache. "My salad?" he said, smiling. "I did not eat it at lunch. My daughter brought me a big sandwich at noon, and I was full. The nurse put my salad in my small fridge for later. I ate it at six, after it had been cold for hours."
"A cold salad is a safe salad," said Mara, and she wrote it down.
ch.clue: I ate it at six, after it had been cold for hours
ch.q: Why is Mr. Ward not sick, although he ate the chicken salad?
o: His salad came from another kitchen
His salad was kept cold in a fridge until he ate it
He is stronger than the other patients
His salad had less chicken than the others
He ate a sandwich before and after the salad
ch.hint: Mr. Ward salatayı öğlen mi yemiş? Salatası öğleden akşama kadar nerede durmuş? Bunu diğer hastaların salatasıyla karşılaştır.
ch.why: Mr. Ward'ın salatası akşam altıya kadar soğuk bir buzdolabında durmuştu; soğuk ortam bakterilerin çoğalmasını önler.

text: That evening, Mara called a short meeting in the hospital kitchen. The head cook, two kitchen helpers, Joe and the hospital manager stood around the steel table. Nobody was angry. Mara took a pen and wrote three possible rules on a piece of paper.

"One: always cook the chicken for longer," she read. "Two: wash the bowls with very hot water every hour. Three: keep cold food in the fridge until the moment it is served, and write the time on every bowl."

"The first rule does not help," said Mr. Ruiz after thinking for a moment. "The chicken was cooked well. The problem was the long wait at twenty-eight degrees." The manager nodded. "And the second rule is good, but it does not solve the real problem."

"Then the third rule is the one," said Mara. "From tomorrow, nothing cold stays on the table for more than twenty minutes. If the delivery truck is late, we serve later, but we do not leave the salad next to the oven."
Mr. Ruiz took the paper, folded it and put it carefully into his white hat.
ch.clue: keep cold food in the fridge until the moment it is served
ch.q: Which new rule would solve the main problem?
o: Serve lunch earlier than before
Wash the bowls with very hot water
Add more salt to the salad
Keep cold food in the fridge until it is served
Cook the chicken for twice as long
ch.hint: Asıl sorun, soğuk yemeğin saatlerce sıcak bir ortamda kalmasıydı. Bu sorunu doğrudan çözen kural hangisi?
ch.why: Asıl sorun soğuk salatanın sıcakta beklemesiydi; çözüm, onu servis anına kadar buzdolabında tutmaktı.

outro: Mutfağın kuralları yeniden yazıldı ve soğuk yiyecekler artık buzdolabında tutuluyor. Mara, Joe'ya şunu söyledi: hastalığın nedenini bulmak, bir sonraki hastalığı önlemenin en güvenli yoludur.

title: The Echo from the Moon
hero: Komutan Noor Hale ve mühendis Pip
intro: Aurora istasyonunun radyosu, birkaç dakikada bir tuhaf bir "HELLO" sinyali alıyor. Ekip heyecanlı: bir uzaylı mı? Komutan Noor Hale ile mühendis Pip, sinyalin zamanlamasına bakarak onu çözmeye çalışıyor.

text: At lunch, the whole crew of the Aurora space station was floating around the table, and Eli was telling a very long story about a pizza. Suddenly the speaker on the wall made a sound. It was a thin, high voice, full of noise. It said: "Hello... hello." Then it stopped.
Everybody was quiet. "That is not from Earth," whispered Dr. Sato. "Nobody on Earth speaks like that." Eli's eyes were as big as plates. "It is an alien," he said. "I knew it!"

Commander Noor Hale smiled but did not answer. She went to the control room and opened the radio record. The strange word had appeared fourteen times that morning. The first time was at 8:00, then 8:07, then 8:14. Every seven minutes, to the second, like a clock.
Pip looked at the numbers over her shoulder. "Seven minutes," he said. "Aliens would not be so punctual."

"No," Noor said. "Something regular is much more likely to be a machine than a visitor. But we have to prove it." She took a notebook, and wrote the first question: What do we send every seven minutes?
ch.clue: Every seven minutes, to the second
ch.q: Why does Noor not believe that it is an alien?
o: Eli told a long story about pizza
The voice sounds too thin and too high
The signal has appeared only fourteen times
The signal arrives with perfect regularity, like a machine
Nobody at the table knew the word
ch.hint: Sinyal sabah 8:00, 8:07, 8:14'te gelmiş. Bu düzenlilik canlı bir varlıktan mı, yoksa bir makineden mi daha çok beklenir?
ch.why: Sinyal tam yedi dakikada bir geliyordu; bu kadar düzenli bir şey bir makineden ya da otomatik bir sistemden gelir.

text: Pip opened the station's own radio log, and Noor placed it next to the record of the strange signal. Every seven minutes, the station's computer sent a short test message to Mission Control. The message was the same every time: a voice that said "Hello", to check that the system was alive.

"Look at the times," said Noor. The test message left the station at exactly 8:00:00. The strange answer arrived at 8:00:02.6. At 8:07:00 the next test message left, and at 8:07:02.6 the strange signal arrived. Every time, the same delay: two point six seconds.

"Light moves very fast, three hundred thousand kilometres every second," said Pip, writing on a screen. "The Moon is about three hundred and ninety thousand kilometres from Earth. So light takes one point three seconds to reach it."
"And one point three seconds to come back," said Noor. "One point three plus one point three. Two point six."
They looked at each other. "The signal goes to the Moon, hits it, and returns to us," said Pip slowly. "We are hearing our own voice."
ch.clue: two point six seconds
ch.q: What explains the delay of two point six seconds?
o: The signal travels to the Moon and back to the station
The radio needs time to start every morning
The computer is slow when it is cold
Mission Control answers after counting to ten
The signal travels from Mars to the station
ch.hint: Işık Ay'a kaç saniyede gider? Gidiş ve dönüş süresini topla ve 2,6 saniyeyle karşılaştır.
ch.why: Işık Ay'a 1,3 saniyede ulaşır; gidiş dönüş 2,6 saniye eder, sinyal Ay'dan yansıyıp geri dönüyordu.

text: "It is a very good idea," said Noor, "but we must test it. A good idea is not a fact." She went to the radio desk and changed the test message. Instead of 'Hello', she recorded a different sentence in her own voice: "Aurora to Mission Control, good morning." Then she pressed the button.

The crew waited in the control room with their eyes on the clock, and nobody said a word. The test message left at 8:14:00. At 8:14:02.6, the loudspeaker made a small click, and a thin, high, noisy voice said: "Aurora to Mission Control, good morning."
Dr. Sato opened his mouth. Eli, who had been sure about the alien for two hours, laughed so hard that he floated up to the ceiling.
"Of course," said Pip. "The echo repeats whatever we send. An alien would not repeat my commander's sentences so politely."
Noor smiled, pleased. "That is the proof," she said. "When the answer changes exactly as the question changes, we are listening to ourselves."
ch.clue: Aurora to Mission Control, good morning
ch.q: Why does the new test prove that the signal is an echo?
o: The new message was sent by Mission Control
The new message arrived earlier than the old one
The strange voice repeated the new message exactly
The strange voice became louder than before
The strange voice answered with a new word
ch.hint: Noor mesajı değiştirince tuhaf ses ne söyledi? Değişen soruya aynı şekilde değişen cevap neyi gösterir?
ch.why: Mesaj değişince yankı da aynı değişikliği tekrarladı; bu, sinyalin kendi sesleri olduğunu kanıtlıyordu.

text: In the evening, Noor gave a short talk to the crew. "I am proud of all of you," she said, "especially of Eli, who found the signal first." Eli took a bow in the air. "Today we learned something important. Let me write it as a short list."

She wrote on the board: One, a signal every seven minutes. Two, a delay of two point six seconds. Three, the echo repeats a new message. "Three ordinary facts," she said, "and one extraordinary story. Which of the two is more likely to be true?"
"The ordinary one," said Dr. Sato. Noor nodded. "In science, we always begin with the simplest explanation that fits all the facts. We do not forget aliens. But we do not choose them first, either."
Pip raised his hand. "May I ask a question? Is there anything in our facts that proves that no alien exists?"
"Not at all," said Noor with a smile. "Only that this particular signal was not from one."
ch.clue: one extraordinary story
ch.q: Which sentence best explains Noor's way of thinking?
o: Never believe any strange signal from space
Always choose the most exciting explanation
Ask the youngest crew member for his opinion
Wait for Earth to explain every unusual noise
First choose the simplest explanation that fits all the facts
ch.hint: Noor üç sıradan olguyu ve bir sıra dışı hikâyeyi karşılaştırıyor. Bilimde önce hangi tür açıklamaya bakılır?
ch.why: Noor, bütün olgulara uyan en basit açıklamayı önce seçmek gerektiğini söylüyordu.

outro: Sinyalin kendi sesleri olduğu anlaşıldı ve herkes gülerek yemek masasına döndü. Noor, günlüğüne şunu yazdı: sıradışı bir ipucu bulunca önce en sıradan açıklamayı dene.

title: The Roman Coin
hero: Arkeolog Dr. Amira Kent ve öğrencisi Leo
intro: Bir çiftçi tarlasında iki eski sikke buldu ve ikisinin de Roma dönemine ait olduğunu düşünüyor. Dr. Amira Kent ile öğrencisi Leo, hangisinin gerçek, hangisinin kopya olduğunu anlamaya çalışıyor.

text: The farmer, Mr. Hallam, put two coins on a white cloth in the university laboratory. He was a big, shy man in a muddy coat, and he looked as if he was afraid to breathe. "I found them in the north field," he said. "I was ploughing. They were just lying there, in the earth. I think they are Roman."

Dr. Amira Kent and her student Leo bent over the table. The first coin, which they called Coin A, was perfectly round and bright, golden-brown like new bread. Its edge was smooth, with a thin line all around. The portrait of an emperor was sharp, and each letter was clear.

The second coin, Coin B, was very different. It was dark and uneven, a little too thick on one side and a little too thin on the other. The portrait was worn, and the letters were hard to read. Its edge was rough, with small marks where something had hit it.

"Which one is real?" asked Mr. Hallam. Amira smiled. "Most people think the beautiful one," she said. "But Roman coins were not made by machines. They were made by hand, one at a time, with a hammer."
ch.clue: Roman coins were not made by machines
ch.q: Which coin looks more like a hand-made Roman coin?
o: Coin B, because it is darker than Coin A
Coin A, because the portrait is clear
Both, because they were found together
Coin A, because it is bright and perfectly round
Coin B, because it is uneven and has hammer marks
ch.hint: Amira Roma sikkelerinin nasıl yapıldığını söylüyor: elle, çekiçle. Elle yapılan bir sikke hangi görünüşte olurdu: kusursuz yuvarlak mı, düzensiz mi?
ch.why: Roma sikkeleri çekiçle elle basılırdı; düzensiz ve çekiç izli olan B sikkesi buna daha çok benziyordu.

text: Leo took a soft brush and carefully cleaned the surface of Coin B under a bright lamp. A little brown dust fell onto the cloth. Then, under the magnifying glass, he looked at the deep places between the letters. There was green and black earth packed in them. Some of the dirt was so hard that it looked like a part of the metal itself.
"This soil has been here for a very long time," said Amira. "Metal changes slowly when it lies under the ground. It forms a thin green crust. You cannot make it in a day."

Then they examined Coin A with the same glass. Between its letters there was only clean, shiny metal. There was no earth, no green crust. In one place, near the edge, Leo found something strange: very fine parallel scratches, all in the same direction, like the marks of a modern tool.
"Coin A has been cleaned very well," he said. "Too well."
"A coin that spent eighteen hundred years in the ground would not look like this," said Amira. "Not even after a good wash."
ch.clue: green and black earth packed in them
ch.q: What do the earth and the green crust on Coin B show?
o: Coin B was cleaned in the laboratory
Coin B lay in the ground for a very long time
Coin B was painted green to look old
Coin B was kept in a museum for years
Coin B was made last year from new metal
ch.hint: Sikkenin harflerinin arasında hangi malzeme var ve metal toprak altında uzun süre kalınca ne olur? Bunu hızlıca yapmak mümkün mü?
ch.why: B sikkesinin harflerinde sertleşmiş toprak ve yeşil bir kabuk vardı; bunlar ancak çok uzun süre toprakta kalmakla oluşur.

text: Leo turned Coin A over, and on the back, under the lamp, he noticed something odd. In the corner there was a little rectangle that was slightly lighter than the rest of the surface. He rubbed it gently with his finger, and a thin piece of dry glue fell onto the cloth. "It looks as if a sticker was here," he said.
Amira put the coin under the magnifying glass again. Near the glue, there were four very small letters, almost invisible: M.A.D.E. And after a space, another group, even smaller: IN CHINA.
"Roman emperors did not export to China," said Amira, trying not to laugh. "This coin was made in a factory, probably as a souvenir, and sold in a museum gift shop."

Mr. Hallam went red to the ears. "My grandson must have lost it," he said at last. "He loves coins. He often walks in my fields with a metal detector, and he carries a few souvenirs in his pocket. He must have dropped it there."
"So the second coin is only a toy," said Leo. "And it fell on top of the real one."
ch.clue: a little rectangle that was slightly lighter
ch.q: How did the modern coin end up in the field?
o: A Roman soldier left it there on purpose
Mr. Hallam bought it at a market to trick them
Leo found it in the museum shop
Mr. Hallam's grandson lost it from his pocket
Amira put it in the field for the test
ch.hint: Sikkenin arkasındaki etiket izi ve küçük yazı neyi gösteriyor? Çiftçi torununun sikkelerle ilgili hangi alışkanlığından bahsediyor?
ch.why: Sikkenin arkasında hediyelik eşya etiketi izi ve "made in" yazısı vardı; torun cebinden düşürmüştü.

text: Amira sent Coin B to the museum laboratory, where an expert cleaned it very slowly, with a small wooden stick and a drop of water. After three weeks, the portrait became clearer. It showed the face of an emperor with a short beard and a strong nose, and the Latin letters around it said: HADRIANUS AUG.

The expert called Amira on the phone. "It is real," she said. "It is a silver denarius of the Emperor Hadrian, struck around the year one hundred and twenty. We have a few of them, but none as well preserved. Please thank Mr. Hallam."

Amira told him the news in the field, where he was ploughing again. "It is yours, in a way," she said. "But the law says that finds like this belong to the nation. If you give it to the museum, your name will be on the label."
Mr. Hallam took off his cap and held it in both hands. "I would be very proud," he said, "if my name stood beside an emperor."
The next summer, in a glass case in the City Museum, a small card said: Found by Mr. Hallam, North Field.
ch.clue: HADRIANUS AUG
ch.q: What proves that Coin B is a real Roman coin?
o: The expert found Hadrian's name and judged it a real denarius
It was darker and older than the souvenir coin
The farmer said that he found it in a field
The museum offered a lot of money for it
It was found near a Roman road
ch.hint: Uzman temizlikten sonra sikkenin üzerinde hangi yazıyı ve hangi imparatoru buldu? Bu bilgi sikkenin gerçek olduğuna nasıl bir kanıt oluşturur?
ch.why: Temizlenen sikkede Hadrianus'un adı çıktı ve uzman bunun gerçek bir Roma gümüş denarius'u olduğunu belirledi.

outro: Gerçek sikke müzeye bağışlandı ve çiftçinin torunu kopyayı ödül olarak aldı. Amira, Leo'ya şunu söyledi: eski bir şeyin gerçek olup olmadığını, onun yaşadığı yolculuğa bakarak anlayabilirsin.

title: The Bread That Stayed Fresh
hero: Bilim insanı Dr. Ilan Voss ve asistanı Dana
intro: Dana, evden getirdiği ekmek dilimlerinin neden farklı hızlarda küflendiğini merak ediyor. Dr. Ilan Voss ile asistanı Dana, küfün büyümesi için hangi koşulların gerektiğini bir deneyle bulmaya çalışıyor.

text: On Monday, Dana arrived at the laboratory with a bag of bread and a bright idea. "My grandmother always says that bread goes bad faster in a plastic bag," she said. "Is it true? Let's test it, Ilan."

Dr. Ilan Voss liked the idea at once. They took four slices of the same bread, from the same loaf, and put them in four different places. Slice 1 went into a plastic bag, on a warm shelf near the radiator. Slice 2 went into a plastic bag in the fridge. Slice 3 stayed on an open plate, on the table. Slice 4 went into a glass jar with a lid, together with a small packet of dry silica, the little white bag that comes in new shoes.
Dana wrote a label for each slice and the date: Monday. "How long do we wait?" she asked. "One week," said Ilan. "Every day, we will look at the slices, take a photo and write what we see."
On Wednesday, Slice 1 already had a few dark green spots. On Thursday, it was covered with soft grey fur. The other three looked exactly as before.
ch.clue: a plastic bag, on a warm shelf near the radiator
ch.q: Which slice developed mould first?
o: Slice 1, in a bag on a warm shelf
All four slices at the same time
Slice 4, in a jar with silica
Slice 3, on an open plate on the table
Slice 2, in a bag in the fridge
ch.hint: Her dilimin nerede ve hangi koşulda tutulduğunu karşılaştır. Çarşamba ve perşembe günü yeşil lekeler hangi dilimde görülmüş?
ch.why: İlk küflenen dilim, kalorifer yanındaki sıcak rafta, poşet içinde bekleyen Dilim 1 oldu.

text: After a week, the four slices stood in a row on Dana's desk. Slice 1 was now a soft grey and green mess that smelled strongly. Slice 3, on the open plate, had a few small spots at the edge. Slice 2, from the fridge, was a little hard but completely clean. Dana lifted it carefully with tongs. "No mould at all," she said, surprised. "Even after seven days in the bag."

"The bag is the same as Slice 1's," said Ilan. "The slice is the same. The bread is the same. Only the temperature is different." He took a notebook and wrote two lines: Warm and bag: mould in three days. Cold and bag: no mould after seven days.
"So the bag is not the real problem," Dana said slowly. "My grandmother was a little wrong. The bag only keeps in the water. The heat is the thing that helps the mould to grow."
"We have learned something about warmth," said Ilan. "But I am not sure what the bag does yet. Let us look at Slice 4, in the jar."
ch.clue: No mould at all
ch.q: What does Slice 2 show about mould?
o: A fridge makes mould disappear completely
Plastic bags always stop mould from growing
Cold temperature slows the growth of mould
Mould only grows on slices that are warm and open
Bread in the fridge cannot become hard
ch.hint: Dilim 1 ve Dilim 2 aynı poşette ve aynı ekmekten. Aralarındaki tek fark ne ve sonuçlar nasıl?
ch.why: Dilim 2 de poşetteydi ama buzdolabındaydı ve küflenmedi; düşük sıcaklık küf oluşumunu yavaşlatıyor.

text: Slice 4 was the strangest of all. It lay in the glass jar with the small packet of silica, completely dry and golden, hard as a biscuit. Dana unscrewed the lid, and a faint smell of toast came out. There was no mould anywhere, not a single spot, though the jar had stood on the desk at room temperature for a whole week.

"Room temperature," Dana repeated. "Not cold, not hot. And still no mould." Ilan smiled. "What is different about the jar?" Dana looked at it carefully. "The jar is closed, but so is the bag. The difference is the silica. It takes the water out of the air. The bread is completely dry."
"And Slice 3, on the open plate, has only a few spots," said Ilan. "The air dries it a little."

He wrote on the white board: Mould needs three things: food, warmth and water. Then he drew a small triangle and wrote the three words at its three corners. "Take away just one of them, and the mould stops."
Dana put the jar on the shelf, proud. "The bread was the food, the room was warm," she said. "But without water, nothing happened."
ch.clue: It takes the water out of the air
ch.q: What does Slice 4 show about mould?
o: Mould appears only in plastic bags
Mould grows best inside a glass jar
Room temperature always stops mould
Silica gives the bread a special taste
Mould needs water, and dry bread does not grow it
ch.hint: Kavanozdaki dilim oda sıcaklığındaydı ama küflenmedi. Silika paketi ne yapıyor ve ekmek bu sayede nasıl bir hâle geliyor?
ch.why: Silika havadaki nemi aldığı için Dilim 4 kuru kaldı ve küflenmedi; küf için su gerekir.

text: On Friday, Ilan and Dana wrote a short note for the whole laboratory, to go on the kitchen wall. It was a good example of how to turn an experiment into advice. "Three slices tell the same story, and the fourth slice tells it from the other side," Ilan said. "Warmth and water make mould. Cold or dryness stop it."

Dana wrote three possible storage tips on a sheet of paper and read them aloud. One said: Keep bread in a warm, closed bag for a better taste. The second said: Put bread in a cool, dry place and use it within a few days. The third said: Put bread in the sun to dry it quickly.
"The first tip is exactly what made Slice 1 grow mould," said Ilan. "And the third one sounds dry, but the sun also brings warmth, and sometimes steam under the plastic."

"So the second one," said Dana. She pinned it on the wall with a green pin. Under it, in smaller letters, she added her grandmother's name. "She was almost right," she said. "She only forgot to mention the radiator."
ch.clue: Warmth and water make mould
ch.q: What is the best way to store bread, according to the experiment?
o: On an open plate in the sunlight
In a cool, dry place and use it quickly
In a wet cloth inside a drawer
In a warm plastic bag near a radiator
