In a closed bag with some water
ch.hint: Küfün büyümesi için hangi iki koşul önemliydi? Bunları ortadan kaldıran saklama yöntemini seç.
ch.why: Küf ısı ve neme bağlıydı; serin ve kuru bir yerde saklamak ikisini de azaltır.

outro: Ekmeğin ömrünü uzatmak için pratik bir kural bulundu: serin ve kuru yerde sakla. Ilan, Dana'ya şunu söyledi: bir şeyin neden olduğunu anlamak için, onu bir kez de olmasın diye denemek gerekir.

title: Fifty Five-Star Reviews
hero: Muhabir Jonas Reid ve fotoğrafçı Ellie
intro: Yeni açılan bir restoranın internet sayfasında bir günde elli tane beş yıldızlı yorum çıktı. Okurlar şüpheli. Muhabir Jonas Reid ile fotoğrafçı Ellie, yorumların gerçek olup olmadığını araştırıyor.

text: On Thursday morning, a reader named Mrs. Farrow came into the office of the Kingsbridge Daily with a folded paper. "Have you seen the page of Luigi's?" she asked, a little angry. "It is a new restaurant in Mill Street. Yesterday it had no reviews at all. Today it has fifty-two, and every one has five stars."

Jonas Reid opened the page on his computer. The restaurant had a picture of a big plate of pasta, and below it there was a long list of reviews, each with a smiling face and five bright yellow stars. He scrolled down slowly. Ellie leaned over his shoulder, drinking a mug of coffee.
"They all look very happy," she said. "But is that normal for a restaurant that opened only two days ago?"

Jonas clicked on the dates. "Everything was posted yesterday between four and six in the afternoon," he said. "Fifty-two reviews in two hours. And when we opened the page this morning, there were still none from real customers who had eaten there at lunch."
"Two hours," said Ellie. "That is one review every two minutes."
ch.clue: Fifty-two reviews in two hours
ch.q: What makes the reviews look suspicious at first?
o: The restaurant has pictures of pasta on its page
Fifty-two reviews appeared in only two hours
Every review has a smiling face and five stars
Mrs. Farrow was angry when she arrived
The restaurant opened only two days before
ch.hint: Yorumların hepsi hangi saat aralığında yazılmış? İki saatte elli iki yorum, normal bir restoran için ne kadar olası?
ch.why: Elli iki yorum yalnızca iki saat içinde yazılmıştı; yeni açılmış bir restoran için bu çok garipti.

text: Ellie copied the first ten reviews and pasted them into a document, one under the other. She and Jonas read them slowly. They were short and friendly. The first said: Best pasta in town! The sauce is magic, and the waiter was lovely. The fourth said: Best pasta in the whole town! Magic sauce, lovely waiter. The seventh said: The sauce is magic. Best pasta in town. Lovely waiter.
"These are not ten different people," said Ellie. "These are one person who wrote the same sentence ten times, and changed a word here and there."

Jonas highlighted the three words that came again and again: magic, lovely and best. "Real customers write about different things," he said. "One talks about the price, another about the dessert, another about the music. A third complains that the soup was cold. Real reviews are messy."
"These are perfect," said Ellie. "And perfect is suspicious." Jonas looked at the clock. "Let us see the names of the people. Maybe they have more to tell us."
ch.clue: Best pasta in town! The sauce is magic, and the waiter was lovely
ch.q: What does the similarity of the reviews suggest?
o: They were all written by Mrs. Farrow
They were written in a hurry after a good meal
They were written by customers from the same family
They were probably written by one person or copied
They were written by the waiters on that evening
ch.hint: Ilk ve dördüncü ve yedinci yorumlara bak: kelimeler neredeyse aynı ve yalnızca sıraları değişmiş. Gerçek müşteriler böyle mi yazar?
ch.why: Yorumlarda aynı üç kelime ve aynı cümleler tekrar ediyordu; bunları tek bir kişinin yazmış ya da kopyalamış olması çok olasıydı.

text: Jonas clicked on the little round pictures beside the names. Every reviewer had a profile photo: a smiling young woman on a beach, an old man with a dog, a family at a picnic. They looked like perfectly normal people. But when he opened the information about the accounts, he found something unusual: all fifty-two had been created in the same week, only five days before the restaurant opened.

Ellie took one of the photos, the young woman on the beach, and dragged it into an image search engine. In a few seconds, the screen showed a long list. The same young woman, on the same beach, smiled in an advertisement for a bank, on the cover of a travel magazine, and on a website that sold free pictures to anybody.
"She is a stock photo," Ellie said. "She is not a customer of Luigi's. She is a person from a picture shop." She tried the old man with the dog. The same result.
"Fifty-two new accounts, fifty-two borrowed faces," said Jonas. "Someone created a crowd that does not exist."
ch.clue: all fifty-two had been created in the same week
ch.q: What do the profile photos and the new accounts show?
o: The reviewers were not real customers but invented accounts
The reviewers were friends of the owner of the restaurant
The reviewers worked for the bank in the advertisement
The reviewers were from different cities in the country
The reviewers had visited the restaurant in the same week
ch.hint: Hesapların hepsi ne zaman açılmış ve profil fotoğrafları başka nerede kullanılıyor? Bu iki bilgi birlikte neyi gösterir?
ch.why: Hesapların hepsi aynı hafta açılmıştı ve fotoğraflar başka yerlerde reklam olarak kullanılıyordu; yorumcular gerçek müşteri değildi.

text: Jonas and Ellie walked to Mill Street and found Luigi, the owner, polishing a glass behind the counter. He was a round man in a white apron, and when he saw the notebook in Jonas's hand, his smile disappeared.

"I did not write the reviews myself," he said at once. "A man phoned me last month. His company is called StarBoost. He said that new restaurants never get customers without good reviews. For thirty pounds, he would write fifty nice reviews on opening day. I paid, and I did not ask questions. I did not want to cheat. I just wanted people to come."

"Did it work?" asked Ellie. Luigi looked at the empty tables around him. "Yesterday I had four customers," he said. "Three of them were Mrs. Farrow's neighbours, who came to see the pasta of the fifty-two stars. They were not very happy."
Jonas put down his pen. "Mr. Luigi," he said gently, "one honest review is worth more than fifty bought ones. If you cook well, your customers will tell the town for free."
Luigi sighed. "Please write that, too," he said.
ch.clue: he would write fifty nice reviews on opening day
ch.q: How did the fake reviews appear on the restaurant's page?
o: The owner wrote them himself during the night
The customers wrote them after a free dinner
The owner paid a company to write them
A bank wrote them to help the restaurant
The newspaper asked Mrs. Farrow to write them
ch.hint: Luigi, sahte yorumların nereden geldiğini kendisi anlatıyor. Kimi aradığını, ne için para ödediğini ve kime ödediğini hatırla.
ch.why: Luigi, yorumlar için StarBoost adlı şirkete otuz pound ödediğini itiraf etti.

outro: Gazetenin haberi yayımlandı ve restoran sahibi yorumları sildi. Jonas, defterine şunu yazdı: gerçek bir insanın sesi, bir fotokopiye benzemez.

title: The Dry River
hero: Park korucusu Wren Calder ve köpeği Bracken
intro: Köyün yanından geçen nehir bir sabah neredeyse tamamen kurudu. Dağda ise yağmur yağıyor. Park korucusu Wren Calder ile köpeği Bracken, suyun neden köye ulaşmadığını bulmak için nehri yukarı doğru takip ediyor.

text: On Monday morning, the villagers of Little Combe woke up to an unusual silence. The river, which usually ran under the old stone bridge with a loud, cheerful noise, had almost stopped. A few small pools of water lay among the round stones, and the fish in them were swimming in circles. A woman with a bucket stood on the bridge and shook her head.
Ranger Wren Calder walked down from the bridge with her dog Bracken and looked carefully at the river bed. The stones were wet but not covered. The sun was warm, and the air smelled of mud.

"It did not rain here this week," she said. "But it rained in the mountains on Friday and on Saturday, a lot. I saw the black clouds myself. So the water should be here. There should be even more of it than usual."

Bracken sniffed the air, whining softly. Wren pointed up the valley, where the river came down from the hills. "Water does not disappear," she said. "If it is not here, then it is stopped somewhere above us. Let us find where."
ch.clue: it rained in the mountains on Friday and on Saturday
ch.q: What does Wren conclude from the rain in the mountains?
o: The fish in the river drank all the water
The river was dried up by the hot sun
The water is blocked somewhere above the village
The rain fell only on the bridge area
The villagers took the water for their gardens
ch.hint: Dağda cuma ve cumartesi çok yağmur yağmış. Normalde nehirde daha fazla su olması gerekirken kuru olması neye işaret eder?
ch.why: Dağda yağmur yağdığı hâlde nehir kuruydu; su yukarıda bir yerde tutuluyor olmalıydı.

text: After an hour's walk, the path became steep and the valley narrow. The air grew cooler, and the trees were closer together. Bracken ran ahead, and Wren followed, with her eyes on the ground and on the river bank.

At the bend of the stream, she stopped. On both sides of the water, at the edge of the wood, were the stumps of several small trees. They were as thick as her arm, and each one ended in a point, like a sharpened pencil. Around them lay pale white chips of wood, clean and fresh, on the dark earth.

"No saw made these," she said, kneeling to touch the cut. "Look at the marks. Two parallel lines, as if somebody used big front teeth." She measured the distance between the lines with her fingers: about as wide as her thumb.
She looked up and across the water. On the opposite bank, a smooth path of flattened grass led from the trees down to the stream, as if something heavy had dragged branches there again and again.
"Beavers," she said softly. "Beavers have been working here."
ch.clue: each one ended in a point, like a sharpened pencil
ch.q: Which animal cut the trees?
o: Rabbits
Foxes
Deer
Wild boar
Beavers
ch.hint: Kesilmiş gövdelerin ucu nasıl görünüyor ve etrafta ne var? İki paralel diş izi ve sivri uç hangi hayvanı çağrıştırır?
ch.why: Gövdeler kalem ucu gibi sivriydi ve iki paralel diş izi vardı; bunlar kunduzların işiydi.

text: A little farther up, the stream ended in a wall. It was a long, low dam of branches, stones and thick mud, as high as Wren's chest, stretching from one bank to the other. The water in front of it was deep and dark and quiet, with small bubbles floating on top. Below it, the river bed was almost dry.

"A beaver family built this," said Wren. "They want a quiet pool to build their home in the middle, away from foxes. The water behind the dam is their protection. And it is also the reason why the village has no water."

She put her hand on the top of the dam. A very thin thread of water ran over the branches. It was almost nothing. "Beavers build a dam so well that nothing can pass," she said. "Not even a little river."
Bracken barked at a round shape in the pool, which dived with a loud splash and disappeared. A flat, brown tail slapped the water twice.
"That is the owner," said Wren, smiling. "I do not think he wants to move."
ch.clue: a long, low dam of branches, stones and thick mud
ch.q: Why does the village have no water?
o: The rain stopped before it reached the hills
The beavers' dam holds back the river water
The river has found a new path under the ground
The trees took the water from the stream
The beavers drank all the river water
ch.hint: Dam hangi malzemeden yapılmış ve suyun çoğu şimdi nerede? Barajın alt tarafındaki nehir yatağı neden kuru?
ch.why: Kunduzların barajı suyu tutuyordu; baraj nehri neredeyse tamamen kapatmıştı ve köye su gitmiyordu.

text: That evening, Wren called a meeting in the village hall. Fifty people sat on wooden chairs, and some of them were not happy. "Let us break the dam," said a farmer. "Those animals are a problem." Another man agreed. "We need our water."

Wren raised her hand. "Beavers are protected by law, and they help nature," she said calmly. "Their ponds filter the water and hold it back in dry months. If we destroy the dam, they will simply build another in a week. I have a better idea."

She had brought a drawing. It showed a long plastic pipe passing through the dam, with its upper end under the water and its lower end below the dam. "The pipe lets some water run through all the time," she explained, "but the pool stays deep enough for the beavers. They do not notice the pipe. It is cheap, and the village gets its river back."
The farmer looked at the drawing for a long time. "Will it work?" he asked. "Yes," said Wren. "It has worked in many other places."
ch.clue: The pipe lets some water run through all the time
ch.q: What is Wren's solution to the problem?
o: Bring water to the village in big trucks
Build a second dam higher in the hills
Remove the dam and move the beavers away
Put a pipe through the dam so water can pass
Dig a new river around the village
ch.hint: Wren barajı yıkmak istemiyor. Hem kunduzların havuzunu koruyan hem de köye su akmasını sağlayan çözüm hangisi?
ch.why: Wren, barajın içinden geçen bir boruyla suyun akmasını ve kunduzların yuvasının korunmasını sağlamayı önerdi.

outro: Barajın içine bir boru yerleştirildi ve nehir yeniden akmaya başladı. Wren, defterine şunu yazdı: doğada bir çözüm bulmak için, onu yapan canlıyı yok etmeye gerek yoktur.

title: The Moving Mummy
hero: Küratör Hugo Laurent ve güvenlik görevlisi Mina
intro: Müzenin Mısır salonunda bir mumya sandığının kapağı gece kımıldamış. Mina bunun bir hayalet olduğunu söylüyor, ama Küratör Hugo Laurent buna inanmıyor. İkisi toz izlerine ve kamera kayıtlarına bakıyor.

text: On Tuesday morning, Mina opened the Egyptian Room as usual. The room was dark and cool, and the old walls were covered with strange paintings of birds and boats. In the middle, on a low wooden stand, lay the golden coffin of a priestess, three thousand years old, with a heavy lid.
Mina stopped at the door. Yesterday, the lid had been exactly in line with the coffin. Today, it was slightly turned, and one corner was ten centimetres out of place.

She ran to the control room and checked the alarm record. Nothing. The doors had not opened, and the windows were closed. The camera in the corridor had seen nobody. "Then it moved by itself," she whispered, and she crossed her arms over her chest. In a few minutes, she was sitting in Hugo's office with her heart beating fast.
"A ghost," she said. "The priestess wants to go home."
Hugo took off his glasses. He did not laugh, because Mina was serious. "Let us not decide too fast," he said. "A ghost would not explain why the alarm did not ring. Let us go and look at the floor."
ch.clue: Nothing. The doors had not opened
ch.q: What does the alarm record tell Mina and Hugo?
o: The alarm was broken for the whole night
A thief opened the windows at midnight
Several visitors came in after closing time
Nobody entered the room during the night
The doors were left open by the cleaner
ch.hint: Alarm kaydında ne yazıyor? Kapılar açılmış mı, pencereler, koridor kamerası ne görmüş? Hugo neden hayalet açıklamasını yeterli bulmuyor?
ch.why: Alarm kaydında kapıların açılmadığı ve kameranın kimseyi görmediği yazıyordu; gece kimse içeri girmemişti.

text: The floor of the Egyptian Room was covered with a thin layer of pale dust, because the museum used a special dry floor, with sand in it, to match the walls. Hugo knelt next to the stand, switched on his torch and held it very low, so that the light ran across the floor.

"Look," he said. "No footprints. Nobody walked here. But there are other marks." In the dust, around the stand, he could see a long curved line, like the edge of a half moon, and next to it, a series of small round shapes, each about the size of a coin, in pairs.
"Those are not feet," said Mina, who had followed him. "They are too regular. And too round."
"They are wheels," said Hugo, measuring with his hand. "Two small wheels, side by side, on a thing about thirty centimetres wide. It went along the wall, turned round the stand, and left."
Mina bent down and looked at the curved line. "Something round came into the room during the night," she said slowly. "And it was not a ghost. It was a machine."
ch.clue: a series of small round shapes, each about the size of a coin
ch.q: What made the marks in the dust?
o: Something with small wheels, not a person
A broom pushed by the night cleaner
Water dripping from the ceiling
An animal that had entered the museum
A visitor wearing very small shoes
ch.hint: Tozda ayak izi yok ama küçük yuvarlak şekiller ve eğri bir çizgi var. Bunlar bacak izlerine mi, tekerleklere mi benziyor?
ch.why: Tozda ayak izi yoktu; çiftler hâlinde küçük yuvarlak izler vardı ve bunlar tekerlek izleriydi.

text: "A machine of thirty centimetres, with two small wheels," Hugo repeated. Then he laughed, and his face lit up. "Mina, what does the museum buy every spring to keep the floors clean?" Mina's eyes opened wide. "Dusty," she said. "The little round robot. But he cleans the corridors, not the Egyptian Room!"

They went to the cleaning cupboard, where the robot was sleeping on its small charging station. On the wall above it, there was a paper with the programme. Hugo read it aloud: Monday to Friday, 2:00 to 2:30 a.m.: Corridor A and Egyptian Room. "The Egyptian Room is in his programme since the spring," he said. "Nobody remembered."
On the back of the robot, he found a little piece of golden paint, sticking to the soft rubber border. It was exactly the same shade as the coffin lid. "That is our ghost's fingerprint," said Hugo.
Mina sat down on a chair and started to laugh. She could not stop for a minute. "The priestess wanted to go home," she said, wiping her eyes, "and the robot pushed her coffin!"
ch.clue: Corridor A and Egyptian Room
ch.q: Why did the robot enter the Egyptian Room?
o: Hugo wanted to test the robot
It was looking for its charging station
It was programmed to clean there at 2 a.m.
The alarm told it to enter the room
Mina sent it there by mistake that night
ch.hint: Robotun temizlik programında hangi bölgeler ve hangi saatler yazıyor? Mısır salonu o listede var mı?
ch.why: Robotun programında gece 2:00-2:30 arasında Koridor A ve Mısır salonu yazıyordu; oraya temizlik için girmişti.

text: Hugo and Mina walked to the Egyptian Room one more time and looked at the low stand where the coffin lay. It was a light wooden table, with thin legs, and the robot had hit one of the legs with its round body. "The stand is too light," said Hugo. "Three thousand years of history on a table made of cheap wood."

Mina wrote down three ideas on a card. The first was to turn off the robot for good, so that no machine would ever bump into the stand again. The second was to put a heavy base under the coffin and mark the area of the stand as a place where the robot must not go. The third was to move the coffin to another room.

"The first idea is not good," said Hugo. "We need the robot for the long corridors. The third is a lot of work and does not solve the problem for other objects. I choose the second. Strong base, and a no-go zone in the robot's programme."
"One heavy table and one small change on the screen," said Mina. "That is all it takes to keep a priestess in her place."
ch.clue: the robot had hit one of the legs
ch.q: Which solution is best for the museum?
o: Move the coffin to a different room of the museum
Ask the night guard to watch the Egyptian Room
Put a larger lid on top of the coffin
Turn off the cleaning robot for good
Make the stand heavy and keep the robot out of that area
ch.hint: Robot koridorlar için gerekli, sehpa ise çok hafif. Hem robotu çalıştırmaya devam eden hem de sandığı koruyan çözüm hangisi?
ch.why: Sağlam bir taban koymak ve robotun o bölgeye girmesini engellemek, hem temizliği sürdürüyor hem sandığı koruyordu.

outro: Standın altına bir kilit takıldı ve temizlik robotu başka bir bölgeye gönderildi. Hugo, Mina'ya gülümsedi: bir sorunun cevabı bazen en küçük yuvarlak izde saklıdır.

title: The Wrong Labels
hero: Oyun testçileri Zoe ve Max
intro: Zoe ve Max'in bu kez önünde yanlış etiketli üç kutu, günler üzerine bir bilmece ve bir sayı dizisi var. Her bulmacanın cevabı bir sonrakini açıyor ve çıkış kapısına yaklaşıyorlar.

text: The door closed behind them, and a soft blue light began to count down: 60:00. Zoe and Max stood in a small room with a long wooden table. On the table there were three boxes in a row. Each box had a label, and each label had a word.

The first box said: Apples. The second said: Oranges. The third said: Apples and Oranges. Next to the boxes, a paper with a short message lay in the light: All the labels are wrong. You may take out only one fruit, from only one box. Then you must put every label in the right place.
"All three labels are wrong," Max said slowly. "So the box that says 'Apples' does not have only apples. And the box that says 'Oranges' does not have only oranges."
"We may take out only one fruit," said Zoe. "So we must choose the box very carefully. Which one will tell us the most?"
Max looked at the three labels, one by one, for a long time.
ch.clue: All the labels are wrong
ch.q: From which box should Zoe and Max take the fruit?
o: The box labelled Apples
None, because they must not touch the boxes
The box labelled Oranges
Any box, because all are the same
The box labelled Apples and Oranges
ch.hint: Her etiket yanlış olduğuna göre, "Elma ve Portakal" etiketli kutuda karışık meyve olabilir mi? O kutuda ne bulunur?
ch.why: Etiketler yanlıştı; "Elma ve Portakal" etiketli kutu karışık olamazdı, yalnızca tek tür içermeliydi.

text: Max opened the third box and took out a fruit. It was a bright red apple. "So this box has only apples," he said. "Then the 'Oranges' box must be the mixed one, because its label is wrong, and it cannot have only apples. And the 'Apples' box must have only oranges." Zoe put the labels in the new places, and the three boxes clicked one after another. A small door opened in the wall, and a piece of paper dropped to the table.
On it was a very short riddle: The day after tomorrow is Friday. What number day of the week is today, if Monday is number 1?
Zoe read it twice. "Counting days is like going down a ladder," she said. "Let us start at Friday and go down." Max took out a pen and began to write the names of the days on the back of his hand.
ch.clue: The day after tomorrow is Friday
ch.q: What number day of the week is today?
ch.hint: Bugünden iki gün sonra cuma ise bugün haftanın hangi günü olur? Pazartesi 1 ise o günün numarası kaç?
ch.why: Bugünden iki gün sonra cuma ise bugün çarşambadır; pazartesi 1 olduğuna göre çarşamba 3'tür.

text: The number 3 opened a small cupboard with a screen and a keyboard. On the screen there was a row of numbers: 2, 4, 8, 16, and then a blank. Under the row, a sentence said: Type the next number. Then the first two digits of the exit code will appear.

"Two, four, eight, sixteen," said Zoe. "It goes up quickly." Max looked at it for a long moment. "Four is two plus two. Eight is four plus four. Sixteen is eight plus eight." He counted on his fingers and nodded. "Every number is the number before it, doubled."
Zoe's fingers waited over the keyboard. "There is a number that fits," she said. "I can feel it." The little clock above the screen said 17:30, and neither of them wanted to make a mistake.

Next to the row of numbers, there was a small drawing of a ladder with arrows going upward, and every arrow was longer than the one before. Max looked at it and smiled. "The designer of this room likes to give us a little help," he said, "but only a little."
ch.clue: Every number is the number before it, doubled
ch.q: What is the next number in the row 2, 4, 8, 16?
ch.hint: Dizideki her sayı bir öncekinin iki katı. 16'nın iki katı kaç eder?
ch.why: Her sayı bir öncekinin iki katıydı; 16'nın iki katı 32'dir.

text: Zoe typed the next number, and the screen turned green. Two big digits appeared on it: 4 and 7. "The first two digits of the exit code," said Max, and wrote them on his hand with a pen. "There must be more. The paper said 'first two digits'."

Max looked around the room again, this time more slowly. He had been so busy with the boxes and the numbers that he had not read the walls. Behind the table, a large frame held a long poem in tiny letters. Under it, someone had written in pencil: Two lines hold the end of the code. The tallest letters speak.

Zoe stepped closer. Most of the letters in the poem were small, but in the last two lines a few were slightly larger, as if they had been written with a heavier hand. She read them aloud, one by one, and noticed that they were not letters but two digits: a big 1 at the start of the first of the two lines, and a big 9 at the start of the last line.
"One and nine," she said, "and the first two digits were four and seven."

Max walked to the heavy door, and Zoe read the digits aloud, one by one, while he typed them on the keypad. A green light flashed. The lock opened with a deep, friendly sound, and a cool wind from the corridor touched their faces.
"Eight minutes left," Zoe said. "Not bad for two people who started with three wrong labels."
ch.clue: The tallest letters speak
ch.q: What is the full exit code?
ch.hint: Kodun ilk iki hanesi 4 ve 7. Son iki satırın başındaki büyük harflerin gösterdiği rakamlar sırayla neler ve onları nereye eklemelisin?
ch.why: İlk iki hane 4 ve 7, şiirdeki büyük rakamlar 1 ve 9'du; tam kod 4719'du.

outro: Zoe ve Max kapıdan çıkıp birbirine el çırptı. Oda sahibi şöyle dedi: iyi bir bulmaca, doğru cevabı bulmaktan çok doğru soruyu sormayı öğretir.

title: The Hotel Mix-up
hero: Havalimanı görevlisi Dara Mills ve stajyer Sam
intro: Mr. ve Mrs. Brown, otele varınca odalarının olmadığını öğrendi: otel rezervasyonlarını hiç bulamıyor. Havalimanı görevlisi Dara Mills ile stajyer Sam, rezervasyonun nerede kaybolduğunu ve çiftin akşama kadar doğru oteli bulup bulamayacağını araştırıyor.

text: At half past five on Friday afternoon, an older couple stood at the Sea View Hotel in Bournemouth, tired after a long flight. Mr. and Mrs. Brown had booked a double room with a sea view for the weekend, for their fortieth wedding anniversary. The young receptionist searched her screen for a long time. "I am so sorry," she said at last. "I cannot find a booking under the name Brown."

"But we have the confirmation," said Mrs. Brown, and took a piece of paper from her bag. It was a printout of an email, with a big green logo. It said: Dear Mr. and Mrs. Brown, your booking at Sea View Hotel is confirmed. Check-in: Friday. Check-out: Monday. Two nights, double room. Thank you for choosing us.

The receptionist read it twice. "It says Sea View Hotel, but there is no address, only the name," she said. She picked up the phone. "I will call the airport information desk. The officer there is very good with problems."
A few minutes later, Dara Mills answered, with her young trainee Sam beside her. "Please read me the confirmation number," she said.
ch.clue: there is no address, only the name
ch.q: What is unusual about the confirmation?
o: It gives the name of the hotel but no address
It was printed on very old paper
It does not have the name of the guests
It does not show the dates of the stay
It is written in a foreign language
ch.hint: Resepsiyonist onay belgesini iki kez okuyor. Belgenin üzerinde otelin adı var ama bir şey eksik: otelin nerede olduğunu gösteren bir bilgi.
ch.why: Onay mektubunda yalnızca otelin adı vardı, adres yoktu; bu yüzden iki otel karışmış olabilirdi.

text: Sam opened the airline's hotel database on the computer and typed the name of the hotel. He frowned. "Dara," he said, "there are two Sea View Hotels in the country. One is in Bournemouth. The other is in Brighton, on the opposite side of the coast."
Dara asked the receptionist to read the email address printed at the top of the confirmation. "It says: bookings at seaview-brighton dot com," she read slowly. "Oh no."

"So the booking was made at the Brighton hotel," said Sam. "The Browns arrived at the wrong one. The Bournemouth hotel has a very similar name, and the green logo is identical, because both belong to the same old family company."

Dara nodded. "Mr. and Mrs. Brown," she said into the phone, "your room is waiting for you, but not in Bournemouth. It is in Brighton, about a hundred and forty kilometres away. It is a very easy mistake to make. Many people make it every year."
There was a silence at the other end. Then a small, tired laugh. "Forty years," said Mrs. Brown, "and we still manage to find new adventures."
ch.clue: bookings at seaview-brighton dot com
ch.q: Where is the Browns' booking?
o: There is no booking anywhere
At the airport hotel near the runway
In the Sea View Hotel in Brighton
In the Sea View Hotel in Bournemouth
In a third hotel with another name
ch.hint: E-posta adresi hangi şehre işaret ediyor? Browns hangi otele gitmiş ve iki otelin ortak yanı ne?
ch.why: Onayın e-posta adresi Brighton'daki otele aitti; çift yanlışlıkla Bournemouth'taki aynı adlı otele gitmişti.

text: "We must decide quickly," said Dara. "It is now twenty minutes to six. The hotel in Brighton keeps rooms until midnight, and after that they give them to other guests." Sam spread a printout of the timetable on the desk.

"There are three possible ways," he said. "First, a taxi. About two hours and a half, if the roads are empty, but on a Friday evening it will take three hours. Second, the bus: it leaves Bournemouth at a quarter past seven, and it takes four hours, with two changes. Third, the train. The last direct train leaves at 8:10 and arrives in Brighton at ten thirty."

Dara looked at the clock on the wall. "The Browns are in the hotel, a ten-minute walk from the station. If they leave now, they can easily catch the 8:10 train, and they will arrive at half past ten, with an hour and a half to spare before midnight."
Mrs. Brown, listening on the phone, said, "The train, please, dear. We are too old for a taxi at night."
ch.clue: arrives in Brighton at ten thirty
ch.q: Which way will bring the Browns to Brighton before midnight, comfortably?
o: A taxi in heavy Friday evening traffic
Staying at the Bournemouth hotel until midnight
The 7:15 bus with two changes on the way
Walking to the station and waiting for the morning train
The 8:10 direct train, arriving at 10:30
ch.hint: Her yolculuğun ne kadar sürdüğünü ve saat kaçta varıldığını hesapla. Gece yarısından önce rahatça varan yol hangisi?
ch.why: 8:10 treni 10:30'da Brighton'a varıyordu ve gece yarısından bir buçuk saat önce yetişiyordu; taksi ve otobüs çok yavaştı.

text: At twenty past ten, a quiet knock came at the door of the airport office. It was the end of Dara's shift, but when she opened it, she found Mr. and Mrs. Brown outside, in their travel clothes, holding two small suitcases. They had come by train to Brighton, and then, for some reason, a taxi had brought them here, to the airport, instead of the hotel.

"We were curious," said Mr. Brown, smiling shyly. "We wanted to see the people who helped us. And we have a small gift." He held a box of chocolates, tied with a blue ribbon, with the words: Sea View Hotel, Brighton. Thank you from the Browns.
"The receptionist in Brighton gave us a room with the best sea view in the whole house," said Mrs. Brown. "She said it was an apology from the family company."
Sam, who was putting away the timetables, looked up. "Dara," he said, "I have a question. How can a hotel prevent this kind of mistake?"
Dara thought for a moment. "Write the address on every confirmation," she said. "A name is not enough."
ch.clue: Write the address on every confirmation
ch.q: How can hotels avoid this kind of mix-up?
o: By changing the name of one of the hotels
By writing the full address on every confirmation
By asking guests to arrive earlier in the day
By giving every hotel the same green logo
By sending confirmations only by telephone
ch.hint: Karışıklığın nedeni iki otelin aynı ada sahip olması ve onayda adres bulunmamasıydı. Bunu önlemek için en doğrudan çözüm ne olur?
ch.why: Sorun belgede adres olmamasıydı; her onay mektubuna tam adres yazılması bu karışıklığı önlerdi.

outro: Çift gece yarısından önce doğru otele ulaştı ve ertesi sabah erken kalkıp denize baktı. Dara, Sam'e şunu söyledi: iki yer aynı ismi taşıyabilir, bu yüzden adrese de bakmak gerekir.

title: The Pianist's Alibi
hero: Dedektif Edmund Crane ve yardımcısı Tess
intro: Koleksiyoncu Mr. Vance'in malikânesinde bir yıldönümü balosu sırasında çalışma odasındaki kasa boşaltıldı. Bütün misafirler piyanistin müziğini dinliyordu. Dedektif Edmund Crane ile yardımcısı Tess, herkesin bir mazeretinin olduğu bir geceyi çözmeye çalışıyor.

text: Vance Hall stood on a hill above the village, its windows shining with candlelight, and the sound of a piano floated across the gardens. It was the fortieth wedding anniversary of Mr. and Mrs. Vance, and nearly sixty guests had come to celebrate. At a quarter to eleven, in the middle of a waltz, a maid screamed upstairs.

When Edmund Crane and Tess arrived an hour later, the study door was open and the whole family was standing in the corridor. The room was small and dark, with leather chairs and a large painting of a ship. Behind the painting, the wall safe stood open. Mr. Vance's collection of diamonds, worth more than the house, was gone.

Crane studied the safe without touching it. "There are no scratches around the lock," he said. "Nobody forced it. Someone turned the combination, correctly, on the first attempt." On the desk, a small carriage clock lay on its side, its glass broken, its hands stopped at 10:40. A porcelain vase had fallen from the shelf and lay in pieces on the carpet. And on the carpet, between the window and the safe, there was a line of dried mud, as if somebody had walked in from the garden in wet shoes.
Tess whispered, "Whoever did it knew the numbers."
ch.clue: Nobody forced it
ch.q: What does the undamaged lock suggest about the thief?
o: The thief broke the lock and then repaired it
Whoever opened the safe already knew the combination
The safe had been left open by Mr. Vance earlier
A professional opened the safe with special tools
The diamonds were taken out through the window
ch.hint: Kasanın kilidi çevresinde çizik yok ve kombinasyon ilk denemede doğru girilmiş. Bu durum, kasayı açan kişi hakkında ne söyler?
ch.why: Kilit zorlanmamıştı; kasayı açan kişi kombinasyonu önceden biliyordu.

text: Crane began with the guests. In the great hall, the pianist, a thin young man called Elias Marsh, was packing his music. Everyone agreed that he had played the whole evening, with a short pause at eight. "I played from nine thirty until eleven without a stop," he said calmly. "Ask anybody."

They did. Mrs. Vance, the host's wife, said she had danced to his music. A retired colonel remembered that the pianist had not left the piano once, because he had asked the pianist to play his favourite song. The butler, Mr. Grimes, had stood by the piano with a tray all evening. The niece, Clara, had turned the pages for him.
"Then he cannot be the thief," said Tess. "He was playing at the time."

Crane did not answer. He turned to the music teacher among the guests, a quiet lady with silver hair. "Madam, you have a trained ear," he said. "Did you notice anything unusual?" She hesitated. "In the waltz, there is a difficult bar where the pianist usually plays a wrong note. A tiny mistake, a half-tone too low, but very characteristic. I heard it at a quarter to ten. And I heard exactly the same mistake, in exactly the same place, at twenty-five to eleven."
"The same mistake twice?" Crane said softly. "A human being almost never repeats a mistake so exactly."
ch.clue: exactly the same mistake, in exactly the same place
ch.q: What might the identical mistake in the waltz show?
o: The pianist was nervous and played carelessly all evening
The waltz was written with a mistake in the music
Two different pianists played the same piece that evening
The music at 10:35 may have been a recording, not live playing
The music teacher had the wrong time on her watch
ch.hint: Müzik öğretmeni aynı küçük hatayı iki farklı saatte duymuş. Bir insanın aynı hatayı bire bir aynı yerde tekrarlaması ne kadar olasıdır?
ch.why: Aynı hata iki kez birebir aynı yerde duyulmuştu; bu, ikinci seferde bir kayıt çalındığını düşündürüyordu.

text: Crane walked to the piano and looked at it carefully. It was a grand piano, black and polished, standing in the middle of the room, and behind it, between the wall and the heavy curtain, there was a narrow space where nobody had looked. He pushed the curtain aside. On the floor lay a small black speaker, connected by a thin wire to a box with a single red button. A label on the box said: Looped recording, 40 minutes. Repeats until stopped.

"The pianist played live until about ten," said Crane quietly. "Then he started this box, and the music continued, with a loud applause in between. The guests heard the piano, because the speaker was hidden behind the real one. And while the recording was playing, he was free."
Elias Marsh, standing in the doorway with the music under his arm, was very pale. "It is a normal tool for a pianist," he said. "I use a recording when I need to rest my hands. Every musician does."
"Perhaps," said Crane. "But a musician does not need to rest his hands for twenty-five minutes while the family safe is opened. And he does not need to hide the box."
Tess looked at the clock on the wall. It said ten past eleven.
ch.clue: Looped recording, 40 minutes
ch.q: How did the pianist's apparent alibi work?
o: A hidden recording kept playing while he was away from the piano
The pianist asked another musician to play for him
The guests were not listening to the piano at all
The butler stopped the music at ten o'clock
The pianist played two pianos at the same time
ch.hint: Piyanonun arkasındaki perdenin ardında ne bulundu ve etiketinde ne yazıyor? Misafirler müziği duyarken piyanist aslında ne yapabilirdi?
ch.why: Piyanonun arkasına gizlenmiş bir kayıt cihazı müziği sürdürüyordu; piyanist o sırada çalışma odasında olabilirdi.

text: "The recording explains how he left," said Tess, "but not how he opened the safe. Nobody forced it. The thief knew the numbers." They went back to Mr. Vance, who was sitting in the library with his head in his hands. Crane asked him the question carefully. "Sir, what is the combination of your safe?"
Mr. Vance looked up. "Three-one, zero-seven, five-eight," he said. "The date I met my wife. The thirty-first of July, nineteen fifty-eight. I told it to nobody except Margaret and my lawyer."

Crane turned to Mrs. Vance. "Madam, the pianist played a special piece this evening, at the colonel's request. Do you remember the title?" Mrs. Vance smiled sadly. "Every anniversary, Elias plays our song. It is called 'The Thirty-First of July'. Mr. Vance wrote the words himself many years ago, and the title is on the front of every programme. It is also printed on the invitation card."

The pianist, standing at the door, did not move. Crane looked at him for a long moment. "The title is a date," he said. "And the combination is the same date, with the year. You did not need to ask for the number, Mr. Marsh. It was on the programme in your hands."
ch.clue: The Thirty-First of July
ch.q: How could Elias Marsh have guessed the combination of the safe?
o: The lawyer gave the number to the guests by mistake
The butler wrote the numbers on the music sheet
The song's title, printed everywhere, was the date used as the code
He had watched Mr. Vance open the safe before
Mrs. Vance told him the combination at the party
ch.hint: Mr. Vance kombinasyonun ne olduğunu söylüyor ve Mrs. Vance özel şarkının adını veriyor. Bu iki bilgi arasında nasıl bir bağlantı var?
ch.why: Şarkının adı (31 Temmuz) kombinasyondaki tarihle aynıydı ve program kartlarında basılıydı; piyanist sayıyı kolayca tahmin edebilirdi.

outro: Elias ertesi sabah polise teslim oldu ve elmaslar Vance'in kasasına geri döndü. Crane eldivenlerini giyerken şunu söyledi: bir mazeret ne kadar kusursuzsa, onun nasıl kurulduğuna o kadar dikkatle bakmak gerekir.

title: The Stuck Key
hero: Genç doktor Mara Quinn ve hemşire Joe
intro: Gece vardiyasında Mr. Oates'in kalp monitörü alarm verdi. Kandaki potasyum tehlikeli derecede yüksekti. Doktor Mara Quinn ile hemşire Joe, hastaya yanlış dozda ilaç verilmesine neden olan şeyi ve aynı hatanın başkalarını da tehlikeye atıp atmadığını araştırıyor.

text: At three in the morning, the heart monitor above Mr. Oates's bed began to scream. Doctor Mara Quinn ran into Room 4 of the intensive care ward with Nurse Joe at her heels. The patient, a sixty-year-old man recovering from heart surgery, was awake but weak, and his heart rhythm was irregular on the screen.

Mara looked at the numbers from the blood test taken an hour earlier. The potassium level was 7.2, far higher than the safe limit of 5.0. "Potassium is a salt that the heart needs," she said quickly, "but too much of it can stop a heart. Give him calcium at once, and call the laboratory for a second test."

When the calcium began to work, and the rhythm on the screen became more regular, Mara stood back and breathed. "Joe," she said, "what has he been receiving?" Joe read from the chart: "Because his potassium was a little low after the operation, the night doctor ordered a slow potassium infusion, ten millilitres per hour, to run until morning. The pump was started at eleven o'clock."
Mara frowned. "Ten millilitres per hour is a very small amount. It should not do this in four hours."
Joe looked at the pump, and then at her. "Doctor, can you check the pump yourself?"
ch.clue: ten millilitres per hour
ch.q: What is the puzzle Mara faces?
o: The patient had been allergic to the calcium injection
The pump was started too early in the evening
The ordered dose was small, yet the potassium is dangerously high
The laboratory test gave a wrong number by mistake
The patient received no potassium at all during the night
ch.hint: Hekim hastaya hangi dozda ve ne kadar süreyle potasyum verilmesini istemiş? Verilmesi gereken miktar ile ölçülen seviye arasındaki çelişkiye dikkat et.
ch.why: Planlanan doz çok düşüktü ama potasyum seviyesi çok yüksekti; pompada bir şeylerin ters gittiği anlaşılıyordu.

text: The infusion pump stood beside the bed, a grey machine the size of a shoe box, with a small screen and a keypad. Mara pressed a button to open the log, and the screen showed a list of events with exact times. She read them one by one. At 23:02 the rate had been entered by a nurse, whose initials were R.P. The rate was 100 ml/h.
"A hundred," she said. "Not ten. Ten times too fast, for four hours."

Joe checked the nurse's schedule. R.P. was Rita Park, a very experienced nurse who had been working for fifteen years. "Rita does not make mistakes like that," he said. "She told me this morning that she is always careful with potassium."

Mara looked at the keypad. It had ten numbers and, below them, a small key with a dot. "If you want to enter ten point zero, you press one, zero, and then the dot key, and then zero again," she said slowly. "But if the dot key does not work, the pump understands one, zero, zero. A hundred."
She pressed the dot key. Nothing appeared on the screen. She pressed it again, harder. The key moved slowly, like a button in a very old radio.
ch.clue: The rate was 100 ml/h
ch.q: What happened to the infusion rate?
o: It was set ten times lower than ordered
It was stopped by the pump after one hour
It was changed by the night doctor at midnight
It was correct, but the potassium bag was wrong
It was set ten times higher than ordered
ch.hint: Günlükte hemşire hangi hızı girmiş ve doktor hangi hızı istemişti? İkisini karşılaştır.
ch.why: Doktor 10 ml/saat istemişti ama pompada 100 ml/saat kayıtlıydı; hız on kat fazlaydı.

text: Joe called the engineering department the next morning, and a technician named Mr. Dunmore came to look at the pump. He tested the keypad with a small tool and nodded. "The dot key is worn out," he said. "Probably the spring is weak. It works only when you press it very hard. A tired nurse in the middle of the night will not notice."

Mara asked him how long the problem had existed. "Two weeks," said Mr. Dunmore. "I saw the report myself. Look." He opened a file on his computer. A note from a nurse in Ward 2, dated fourteen days earlier, said: The pump in Room 4 has a sticky dot key. Please repair or replace. Under it, someone from engineering had written: Low priority. Wait for next service in March.
"Low priority," Mara repeated. "For a machine that controls the dose of potassium."

Mr. Dunmore shrugged, uncomfortable. "The report was classified as 'comfort'. Because the key was working, only slowly. Nobody thought of a patient. We have eighty pumps of this kind in the hospital, and about half of them are old."
Mara thought, and her voice became quiet. "Then Rita did not make the mistake alone," she said. "The system let it happen."
ch.clue: Low priority. Wait for next service in March
ch.q: Why was the dangerous pump still in use?
o: The pump had been repaired only the day before
A repair request had been classified as low priority
The hospital had no technicians for pumps
The nurse had not reported the faulty key
The doctor had refused to change the pump
ch.hint: İki hafta önce bir hemşire arızayı bildirmiş. Mühendislik bölümü bu rapora nasıl bir öncelik vermiş ve neden?
ch.why: Arıza raporu "düşük öncelik" olarak sınıflandırılmış ve mart bakımına bırakılmıştı.

text: In the afternoon, Mara called a meeting with the director of nursing, Mr. Dunmore and the pharmacist. She put the Room 4 pump on the table, with a note that said Dot key faulty. "This is the problem we found," she said. "But I do not want to talk only about this one. If the report was classified as low priority, other reports may be classified the same way. And other pumps may have worn keys. We have forty patients on infusions this morning."

The director of nursing looked at the list. "Which of them should we check first?" she asked. The pharmacist raised her hand. "I have a suggestion," she said. "We have seen that the danger is greatest when the decimal point matters. These are drugs with small doses, where a missing dot makes a tenfold error: potassium, insulin and some heart drugs. We should begin with the pumps that are delivering those drugs to patients right now."
"And then the others, in order," said Mara. "By risk, not by age."
"I will have all eighty tested by tomorrow evening," said Mr. Dunmore, and wrote it on his hand.
Mara looked at Joe, who stood by the door. "Next time, a report like this gets an answer in one day."
ch.clue: a missing dot makes a tenfold error
ch.q: Which pumps should be checked first?
o: Those in rooms where the patients are asleep
Those that have never been repaired before
Those that are the oldest in the whole hospital
Those delivering potassium, insulin and other small-dose drugs
Those in the wards with the fewest nurses
ch.hint: Eksik nokta en çok hangi ilaçlarda on kat hataya yol açıyor? Eczacının önerisine dikkat et: risk yaşa göre değil, doza göre belirleniyor.
ch.why: Küçük dozlu ilaçlarda (potasyum, insülin, bazı kalp ilaçları) eksik bir nokta on kat hataya yol açtığı için bu pompalar önce kontrol edilmeliydi.

outro: Pompalar kontrol edildi, bozuk tuşlar değiştirildi ve bakım raporlarına yanıt verme süresi kısaltıldı. Mara şunu söyledi: bir hata bir insana ait olabilir, ama aynı hata ikinci kez olursa sistem hatalıdır.

title: The Vanishing Water
hero: Komutan Noor Hale ve mühendis Pip
intro: Aurora istasyonunun su deposundaki seviye her gün yüzde birkaç düşüyor. Ne bir sızıntı ne de bir kaçak görülüyor. Komutan Noor Hale ile mühendis Pip, suyun nereye gittiğini bulmak zorunda, çünkü ikmal gemisi yedi hafta sonra gelecek.

text: On the fortieth day of the mission, Commander Noor Hale sat in the control room of the Aurora with the water report open in front of her. The main water tank had held two thousand litres on the day they left Earth. Now, on the screen, the little blue bar showed seventy-one percent. It had lost about three percent every day for the last nine days.

"The crew drinks, washes and cooks," said Pip, the engineer, leaning on the wall, "and the recycling machine returns most of it to the tank. The normal loss is less than half a percent a day. Three percent is far too much."

"So we have a leak," said Noor. Pip shook his head. "That is the first thing I checked. We have moisture sensors on every pipe and under every tank. They are all dry. I also looked at the valves, the pump and the outside hatches. Not a drop. And a leak into space would have been noticed in the pressure readings."
"Then where is the water going?" asked Noor. "Water does not simply vanish."
Pip scratched the back of his neck. "At the current rate, the tank will be empty in twenty-four days. The supply ship comes in forty-nine."
Noor stood up. "Then we have less than a month to find out what is going on."
ch.clue: They are all dry
ch.q: What have the engineers established so far?
o: The water was spilled when the tank was filled
The tank was only half full on the first day
The crew has used much more water than planned
There is no sign of a leak, yet the water level keeps falling
The recycling machine is making too much water
ch.hint: Pip nemi kontrol etti ve ne buldu? Sensörler, vanalar ve basınç ne diyor? Su kaybı hakkında kesin olan şey nedir?
ch.why: Sensörler ve vanalar kuruydu, basınçta da sorun yoktu; yine de depo seviyesi düşüyordu.

text: Noor decided to look at the problem from a different side. She floated through the station, module by module, with a small tablet, and she wrote down every strange thing she saw. In the kitchen, a thin film of water ran down the wall near the cold pipe. In the sleeping quarters, the window glass was covered with tiny drops, and one of the crew had to wipe it every morning to see the stars. Eli complained that his towel never dried, however long he left it.

At the end of the round, she opened the environment report on the tablet. It showed the humidity of the air, as a percentage, for each module. The normal level on the station was about forty-five percent. Today, in the kitchen, it was sixty-eight. In the sleeping quarters, sixty-four. In the laboratory, seventy.
"Humidity," she said to herself. "The air is full of water."

She looked at the graph for the last two weeks. The humidity had been rising slowly, day after day, in perfect mirror to the falling line of the water tank. When the water level went down by three percent, the humidity went up by three points.
Noor sat very still. "Pip," she said into the radio, "come and look at this graph."
ch.clue: The humidity had been rising slowly
ch.q: What does the humidity graph suggest about the lost water?
o: The water is now in the air of the station as vapour
The sensors are measuring the wrong modules
The crew is breathing out more water than before
The water has frozen inside the outside pipes
The humidity is rising because the tank is leaking
ch.hint: Su deposu düşerken havanın nemi hangi yönde ve ne oranda değişmiş? İki grafiği yan yana düşün.
ch.why: Depodaki su azaldıkça havadaki nem aynı oranda artıyordu; su buhar olarak istasyonun havasına karışmıştı.

text: Pip arrived in a minute, and Noor showed him the two lines. He studied them for a long time without a word, and then he smiled slowly. "That is good news, in a way," he said. "The water is not lost. It is only in the wrong place. On the Aurora, we do not have rain or a river to take the humidity away. We have the cabin air system. Its job is to cool the air, so that the vapour turns into drops, and the drops are collected and sent back to the tank."
"And that has stopped," said Noor. "Why?"

Pip opened the maintenance file on the tablet and pressed the button for the history of alarms. It showed one message from nine days ago, on a Tuesday: Condenser filter blocked. Condenser reduced to 10 percent for protection. Please replace the filter. The message had been marked as read, but not as done.
"Nine days," Noor said. "The same day the water began to fall."

Pip nodded. "The system protected itself and almost stopped collecting water. All the time, the crew was breathing, sweating and cooking, and the vapour had nowhere to go. It went to the windows, the walls and the towels."
ch.clue: Condenser reduced to 10 percent for protection
ch.q: Why has the water been missing from the tank?
o: The crew has been drinking from the emergency supply
The tank has a crack that is invisible to the sensors
The condenser was nearly off, so vapour was not returned
The water pump is sending water out of the station
The cold pipe in the kitchen is leaking vapour
ch.hint: Alarm kaydı dokuz gün önce hangi mesajı vermiş ve yoğuşturucu hangi duruma geçmiş? Bu, su damlalarının tanka dönmesini nasıl etkiler?
ch.why: Filtre tıkandığı için yoğuşturucu %10'a düşmüştü; nem toplanıp tanka geri gönderilemiyordu.

text: The spare filters were stored in a green box in the maintenance module. Pip took one, and in thirty minutes he had removed the old filter, a grey and slimy piece of metal, and put the new one in its place. The condenser woke up with a low hum, and the little light on its side turned from amber to green.
"Now we wait," said Pip. "If we are right, two things must happen. The humidity in the air should go down. And the water level in the tank should stop falling, and then rise."

They watched the screen for a whole day. By evening, the humidity in the kitchen had dropped from sixty-eight to sixty. After two days, the windows were clear, and Eli's towel was dry for the first time in a week. On the third day, Noor opened the water report again. The blue bar had moved. It showed seventy-six percent, five points higher than before.
"The water came home," said Pip, grinning.
Noor wrote in her log: The water was never lost. It changed shape. Then she looked up. "From now on, the filter report gets read by two people, and the second person signs when it is done."
ch.clue: humidity in the air should go down
ch.q: What is the best evidence that the repair worked?
o: The condenser made a low and regular noise
The old filter was grey and slimy when removed
The crew felt less tired after the repair
The little light on the machine turned green
Humidity fell and the tank level began to rise again
ch.hint: Onarımdan sonra iki şey beklenmişti. Bu iki şeyin gerçekten olduğunu hangi ölçümler gösteriyor?
ch.why: Hem nem azaldı hem de depo seviyesi yükseldi; bu iki ölçüm onarımın işe yaradığını doğruladı.

outro: Filtre değiştirildi, nem yeniden düştü ve depo yeniden dolmaya başladı. Noor, günlüğüne şunu yazdı: bir şey kaybolmuş görünüyorsa, belki yalnızca başka bir biçime girmiştir.

title: The Wreck off the Cape
hero: Arkeolog Dr. Amira Kent ve öğrencisi Leo
intro: Deniz dibinde bulunan bir batık geminin kimliği belli değil. Arkeolog Dr. Amira Kent ile öğrencisi Leo, tahta parçalarına, sikkelere ve topların biçimine bakarak geminin ne zaman battığını ve hangi gemi olduğunu bulmaya çalışıyor.

text: The research boat rocked gently above Cape Harrow, where fishermen had been catching old iron and broken pottery in their nets for many years. Three weeks earlier, a team of divers had found the reason: a wooden ship, lying on its side in twelve metres of water, half covered with sand and shells. Now Dr. Amira Kent sat at a small table on the deck with her student Leo, looking at a plastic tray full of dark, wet pieces of wood.

"Oak," she said, holding one piece up to the light. "The best wood for ships in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. And look at the end." She pointed at the grain, where thin circles lay one inside the other like the rings of a target. "Each ring is one year of the tree's life. A wet year makes a wide ring, a dry year makes a narrow one. The pattern of wide and narrow rings is like a signature. We can compare it with a database of trees from known dates."

Leo took a photograph through a magnifying glass and sent it to the laboratory. The answer came back in an hour. The outermost ring, the last year of growth before the tree was cut down, was dated 1639.
"So the tree was cut in 1639," said Leo. "Does that tell us when the ship sank?"
"Not exactly," said Amira. "But it tells us something important about the earliest possible date."
ch.clue: the earliest possible date
ch.q: What does the date of the last tree ring tell Amira?
o: The ship sank exactly in the year 1639
The ship was repaired every year after 1639
The ship was built from wood of several centuries
The ship was already old when the tree was cut
The ship was built after 1639, so it cannot have sunk earlier
ch.hint: Ağacın dış halkası kesildiği yılı gösterir. Bu ağaçtan yapılan bir gemi, o yıldan önce var olabilir mi?
ch.why: Meşe 1639'da kesilmişti; gemi bundan sonra yapılabilirdi ve dolayısıyla daha önce batmış olamazdı.

text: In the next days, the divers brought up more finds: a bronze bell with half of its letters missing, three iron cannons covered with shells, a broken clay jar, and a small leather bag with forty-one silver coins stuck together like a lump. Leo cleaned the coins patiently in a bath of warm water, one by one, with a toothbrush. Each coin had a year written on one side.
He made a list in his notebook. Most of the coins were dated 1624, 1628 or 1631. Some of them were from 1635 and 1638. One coin, almost perfectly clean, was dated 1641. And there was nothing later.

"Forty-one coins in a purse," said Amira, "from many different years. The purse belonged to somebody who had been collecting money for a long time. A sailor, or an officer, perhaps. The newest coin in a purse is a very useful clue. Can you tell me why?"
Leo frowned. "Because the owner could not have a coin that did not exist yet," he said slowly. "So the purse must have been closed in 1641, or later."
"Exactly," said Amira. "A purse can be older than its oldest coin. It cannot be older than its newest."
She laid the purse next to the oak sample. "Two witnesses, and they agree."
ch.clue: A purse can be older than its oldest coin
ch.q: What does the coin dated 1641 tell Amira and Leo?
o: The ship sank before the year 1641
The ship sank in 1641 or later
The owner of the purse was born in 1641
The ship was built about the year 1641
The coins were made on the ship itself
ch.hint: Kesenin içindeki en yeni sikke hangi yılda basılmış? Sahibi, henüz basılmamış bir sikkeyi cebinde taşıyabilir miydi?
ch.why: En yeni sikke 1641'e aitti; kese en erken 1641'de kapanmış olabilirdi, yani gemi 1641 ya da daha sonra batmıştı.

text: The bell was the best piece of all. It was a small bronze bell, about as big as a bucket, and it hung from a beam in the ship's front part. Over the years, the sea had eaten some of its letters, but when Leo washed it for three days and brushed the surface carefully, a few of them appeared again, deep in the metal. He copied them in his notebook, leaving spaces for the missing ones: SAN RAF . . . L. . . 164.

"San Raf..." said Leo. "San Rafael?" Amira smiled. "That is my guess, too. San Rafael was a common name for Spanish ships. But 'San Rafael' is only a guess, and there were dozens of ships with the name."
She asked him to look at the date. "One, six, four, and then a blank," she said. "The last digit is gone. It could be 1640, 1641 and so on. But we already know something from the coins and the wood."

"Not before 1641," said Leo, and wrote it down. Then he looked at the clock. "Dr. Kent, the library in the port keeps records of lost ships, doesn't it? Can we ask them for ships called San Rafael that sank near here?"
"Let us do it," said Amira. "Facts from the sea, and facts from the archive. When they meet, we may have a name."
ch.clue: SAN RAF . . . L. . . 164
ch.q: What can the team now say about the ship's name?
o: It was surely the Santa Maria from 1492
It was probably a ship of the Roman Empire
It had no name written anywhere on it
It probably began with San Rafael, and the date started with 164
It sank in a year ending with 0
ch.hint: Zilin üzerindeki harflerden hangi bölümler okunabilmiş? Hangi isim ve yıl önerisiyle ilerleyebilirler?
ch.why: Zilde "SAN RAF..." ve "164..." okunabiliyordu; gemi büyük olasılıkla San Rafael adındaydı ve tarih 164 ile başlıyordu.

text: The port archive was a long, quiet room in the old customs house. A woman in glasses, the archivist, brought them three heavy books bound in leather. "These are the lists of ships lost in Cape Harrow Bay between 1640 and 1660," she said. "There are eleven of them. Only three are called San Rafael."

Leo read the entries aloud. The first San Rafael had sunk in 1640 during a storm in October, with all its cargo of wine. The second had been burned in 1652 in a battle, and the cargo was sugar and cloth. The third one was lost in 1643: the book said, in a clerk's very careful handwriting, that it had been carrying iron cannons and a purse of money for the soldiers, and that it had struck the rocks at the Cape in the night.

"1640 is too early," said Amira at once. "That is before the oldest possible date for our ship. The one from 1652 was burned in a battle, and burned ships look very different. We found no charcoal at all. And there is only one that carried iron cannons, a purse of coins, and hit these rocks."
"The San Rafael of 1643," said Leo, and his voice shook a little. "We have found her."
ch.clue: iron cannons and a purse of money for the soldiers
ch.q: Why is the San Rafael of 1643 the best match?
o: It fits the date limit, the cargo and the place
It carried wine, like the broken clay jar
It was burned in battle, as the wood shows
It is the only ship with a bell on board
It sank earlier than all the other ships
ch.hint: Üç San Rafael'den birinin tarihi çok erken, birinin batış şekli bulguya uymuyor. Üçüncüsünün kargosu ve battığı yer batıkta bulunanlarla nasıl örtüşüyor?
ch.why: 1643'teki San Rafael hem tarih sınırına (1641'den sonra) hem demir toplara hem de kayalıklarda batmış olmasına uyuyordu.

outro: Batığın kaydı arşive girdi ve geminin mürettebatının adları ilk kez bir müzede yazıldı. Amira, Leo'ya şunu dedi: bir belgenin tarihi onun en erken olabileceği tarihtir, en geç olabileceği tarih değil.

title: The Dirty Bottles
hero: Bilim insanı Dr. Ilan Voss ve asistanı Dana
intro: Nehirden toplanan on su örneğinin üçünde zararlı bakteri çıktı ve kasaba paniğe kapıldı. Dr. Ilan Voss ile asistanı Dana, nehrin gerçekten kirli olup olmadığını, yoksa kirlenmenin şişelerden mi geldiğini anlamaya çalışıyor.

text: On Monday morning, the mayor of Riverbend phoned the university in a state of panic. "Three of your ten water samples contain dangerous bacteria," he said. "The newspaper is already asking if the river is poisoned. Do you want me to close the beach?"

Dr. Ilan Voss put down the phone and called his assistant. Dana had collected the ten water samples the week before at different places along the river, from the old stone bridge to the waterfall. She had labelled each plastic bottle with a number from 1 to 10 and a code for the place. Now Ilan had the results from the test on his desk. Samples 2, 5 and 9 were positive: each one contained more than two hundred bacteria in a small amount of water. The other seven were clean.

"Three positives out of ten," said Dana, upset. "Does it mean the whole river is dirty?" Ilan looked at the sheet with the map of the river and the places where she had collected each sample. "Not necessarily," he said. "A result is just a number. Before we tell the mayor to close the beach, we must understand why these three, and not the others."
He took a marker and began to draw a table on the white board with three columns: where, when, and who.
ch.clue: Samples 2, 5 and 9 were positive
ch.q: Why does Ilan not want to close the beach at once?
o: He wants to understand why only three samples were positive
He does not trust the weather forecast for the week
He wants to wait for the newspaper to write first
He thinks the mayor has no right to ask
He believes that the river is certainly clean
ch.hint: Üç numune pozitif, yedisi temiz. Ilan sonuçları hemen kamuoyuna açıklamak yerine neden önce örneklerin nedenini araştırmak istiyor?
ch.why: Yalnızca üç örnek pozitifti; Ilan önce bunun nedenini anlamak istiyordu, çünkü tek başına bir sonuç yeterli değildi.

text: They filled the table together, using Dana's field notes. For each sample they wrote the place, the time of day and the bottle box from which it came. The ten bottles had been carried in two white boxes: Box A, with bottles 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 10, and Box B, with bottles 2, 5 and 9. Dana had collected samples at different places, some near the town and some in the wild upper valley, at different hours.

Ilan stood back and studied the board for a long time. "Is there a pattern in the place?" he asked. "Sample 2 is from the old bridge, sample 5 is from the middle of the forest, and sample 9 is from the waterfall. Three different places."

"And the time of day?" Dana read the notes. "Two in the morning, one in the afternoon. No pattern." She frowned, then looked at the last column. "But look at the boxes. All three positives, 2, 5 and 9, are in Box B. And all seven clean ones are in Box A."
Ilan wrote a large B on the board and circled it. "Now that," he said, "is a pattern. The bacteria do not follow the river. They follow the box."
ch.clue: All three positives, 2, 5 and 9, are in Box B
ch.q: What pattern do the results follow?
o: All the positive samples came from near the town
All the positive samples came from the same place
All the positive samples came from the same box of bottles
All the positive samples were taken in the morning
All the positive samples were collected by the same person
ch.hint: Yer ve saat ile örnekler arasında bir bağ yok. Peki taşıma kutusu açısından bakınca pozitif örnekler nasıl bir ortak özellik gösteriyor?
ch.why: Üç pozitif örneğin hepsi B kutusundaydı ve yedi temiz örneğin hepsi A kutusundaydı; sonuçlar nehri değil kutuyu izliyordu.

text: "What is special about Box B?" Ilan asked. Dana thought. "I washed the bottles in the lab, before the trip," she said. "I always put them in the big dishwasher in the corridor. But the dishwasher is old, and it is not big enough, so I washed them in two rounds. Box A was washed in the morning. Box B was washed in the second round, in the afternoon."

They went to the corridor and looked at the machine. It was a grey steel box with a small display. Ilan opened the manual and found the page about the temperature. "To kill bacteria, the final wash must reach seventy degrees," he read. "Let us see what the log says."

He pressed a button. A list of numbers appeared on the screen, with the date of each wash and the final temperature. Dana read the line from last Thursday morning: seventy-one degrees. Then the next line, last Thursday afternoon: forty-three.
"Forty-three," said Ilan. "The second wash did not heat up. Perhaps the water tank was empty again, or the heater has a fault. The bottles of Box B were washed, but they were not made clean."
"So the bacteria were already in the bottles," whispered Dana, "before I put a drop of river water in them."
ch.clue: forty-three
ch.q: What probably contaminated the bottles of Box B?
o: The river water was poured in too slowly
The boxes were left open in the sun on the trip
The bottles in Box B were older than the others
The dishwasher cleaned the bottles with too much soap
The second wash was not hot enough to kill bacteria
ch.hint: Makinenin günlüğündeki iki yıkama sıcaklığını karşılaştır: sabahki ve öğleden sonraki. Bakterileri öldürmek için kaç derece gerekiyordu?
ch.why: İkinci yıkama yalnızca 43 dereceye ulaşmıştı; bakterileri öldürmek için 70 derece gerekiyordu.

text: "It is a good theory," said Ilan, "but a theory is not a proof. Dana, I want a control test." He explained it slowly. "We take a few bottles from the same Box B, which we have not used. We fill them with sterile water, from our own clean source, which is free of bacteria. Then we test them, exactly as we tested the river samples. If the bottles are guilty, the sterile water will turn positive. If the river is the problem, the sterile water will stay clean."

Dana prepared six bottles from Box B and six from Box A, all filled with the same clean, sterile water. After two days in the incubator, they looked at the dishes under the lamp. The six bottles from Box A were clean, as clear as glass. In four out of the six bottles from Box B, small white spots had appeared.

"Sterile water," said Dana, "and it has bacteria." Ilan nodded. "Sterile before we poured it, dirty after the bottle." He picked up the phone. "Mr. Mayor, you can keep the beach open. The river is fine. The problem was in our washing machine."
"And my washing," said Dana quietly. "I should have checked the temperature."
ch.clue: sterile water
ch.q: What proves that the river was not the source of the bacteria?
o: The mayor said that the river looked clean
Sterile water also became positive in the Box B bottles
The seven clean samples came from the river
The three positive samples had a different smell
The newspaper printed a new map of the river
ch.hint: Kontrol deneyinde steril su kullanıldı. Steril su Kutu B şişelerinde bakteri gösterdiyse, bakterinin kaynağı sence nerede?
ch.why: Steril su B kutusundaki şişelerde de bakterili çıktı; bakteri şişelerdeydi, nehirde değil.

outro: Nehir temiz çıktı ve kasaba rahat bir nefes aldı. Ilan, laboratuvarın panosuna büyük harflerle şunu yazdı: bir sonuç ancak kontrol deneyiyle birlikte anlam taşır.

title: The Missing Half Sentence
hero: Muhabir Jonas Reid ve fotoğrafçı Ellie
intro: Gazetenin ön sayfasında belediye meclisi üyesi Councillor Hart'ın yeni yola karşı olduğunu söyleyen bir alıntı yayımlandı. Hart sinirli bir mektup yazıp böyle bir şey söylemediğini bildirdi. Muhabir Jonas Reid ile fotoğrafçı Ellie, hangi cümlenin nasıl yayımlandığını araştırıyor.

text: The letter arrived on Wednesday morning, written on thick cream paper in a firm hand. Councillor Margaret Hart, who had represented the town for eleven years, did not use many words. "On Tuesday," she wrote, "your front page claimed that I said, and I quote, 'I will not support the new road.' I never told your reporter that I opposed the road. If it is not corrected, my lawyer will write to you."
Jonas Reid read it twice and placed it on the editor's desk. Mrs. Cole raised an eyebrow. "She is not a woman who exaggerates," she said. "Is it possible that our reporter invented the quote?"
"Kit does not invent things," said Jonas. "He is young, but he is careful. I have worked with him for two years. Let us look at his notes."

The notebook was small and brown, held together with a rubber band. Kit had interviewed the councillor on Monday afternoon, in the corridor outside the council chamber, and he had written the interview in neat shorthand. He had also recorded the conversation on his phone, as he always did, in case of doubt. Jonas found the page for Monday and pressed his finger on a line. The line was underlined twice. It said: Hart: will not support the new road...
After the three dots, the writing continued for the rest of the line.
ch.clue: I will not support the new road
ch.q: What is the first thing Jonas must do to settle the argument?
o: Print a correction before he knows what happened
Check what Councillor Hart actually said in the recording and notes
Phone Councillor Hart's lawyer to explain the case
Ask the reporter to apologise to the councillor at once
Ask Mrs. Cole to decide who is right
ch.hint: Hart, sözlerinin yanlış aktarıldığını söylüyor, muhabir ise not ve ses kaydı tutmuş. Bir tartışmayı çözmeden önce hangi kanıta bakmak en mantıklıdır?
ch.why: Jonas'ın ilk işi, Hart'ın gerçekte ne söylediğini muhabirin notlarından ve ses kaydından kontrol etmekti.

text: Kit was waiting in the office, nervous, with his phone in his hand. "I have the audio," he said. "I never delete them." They put on a pair of headphones and listened together, passing them back and forth. The recording was noisy, full of footsteps and the buzz of a vending machine, but Councillor Hart's voice was perfectly clear.

At minute three and twenty seconds, Kit said, "So, do you support the new road?" There was a short pause, and then the councillor answered: "I will not support the new road if the money comes out of the school budget. I would support it, gladly, if we can find the money somewhere else. The road is needed, but the children come first."

Jonas stopped the recording and wrote the sentence on a sheet of paper, word for word. Then he laid next to it the front page of Tuesday's newspaper. It said, in large letters, under a photograph of the councillor: 'I will not support the new road', says Hart. He read the printed sentence and the recorded one slowly, two times, and pointed with his pencil at a word.
"Look," he said, almost to himself, "the first six words are exactly the same."
ch.clue: if the money comes out of the school budget
ch.q: What is the difference between the recorded answer and the printed quote?
o: The printed quote uses different words in the first half
There is no difference, because both say the same
The printed quote changes the councillor's opinion of schools
The printed quote leaves out the condition about the school budget
The printed quote adds a sentence that Hart never said
ch.hint: Kayıtta Hart cümleyi nasıl bitiriyor? Gazetedeki alıntı hangi kelimelerde sona eriyor? İkisini kelime kelime karşılaştır.
ch.why: Kayıtta Hart, yola "okul bütçesinden para çıkarsa" karşı olduğunu söylüyordu; gazetedeki alıntı bu koşulu içermiyordu.

text: Kit insisted that he had not shortened the sentence. "I wrote the whole quote in my story," he said. "I sent it at four. I can show you the file." He opened the story on the computer, and Jonas found the sentence in the original: the full answer of the councillor, including the school budget and the children. It had thirty-seven words.

"Then somebody cut it after you," said Jonas. He opened the page system, where every change was recorded with the name of the editor and the time. At 5:48 p.m., the page editor, Mr. Barlow, had written a short message to the reporters: Front page is too long by forty words. I will trim quotes to fit. No time to check with writers. The first quote that he had changed was the quote of Councillor Hart. The new version had only nine words, and the history showed the precise moment of the cut: 5:52 p.m.

Mr. Barlow, a tired man with a pencil behind his ear, did not deny it. "The printing machines start at six," he said, "and the page was too long. I thought the quote was clear without the end. I did not think it would change the meaning."
Kit looked at the floor. "I did not know," he said quietly.
ch.clue: No time to check with writers
ch.q: Who shortened the quote, and why?
o: The page editor, because the front page was too long
The printers, because their machines broke down
The reporter, because he wanted a stronger headline
Mrs. Cole, because she disliked the road
The councillor, because she changed her mind
ch.hint: Sayfa sisteminin kaydında hangi saatte ve kimin adıyla bir kısaltma yapılmış? Neden yapıldığını yazan mesajda ne yazıyor?
ch.why: Sayfa editörü Mr. Barlow, ön sayfa kırk kelime fazla uzun olduğu için alıntıyı kısaltmış ve muhabirlere sormamıştı.

text: That afternoon, Mrs. Cole called the whole editorial team into her office. She did not shout. She laid the three documents on the table: the councillor's letter, the recording and the page history. "Everybody did something reasonable, and the result was a mistake," she said. "Kit recorded and wrote correctly. Mr. Barlow was in a hurry. I allowed a rule that nobody could change a quote without a check. Today that stops."

She wrote three possible corrections on a card, and read them aloud. The first said that the paper regretted its error and that Councillor Hart was in favour of the road. The second said that the paper printed an incomplete quote, and then gave the whole sentence, adding that Councillor Hart would support the road if the school budget remained untouched. The third was only a short line at the bottom of page two: A quote on Tuesday's front page was shortened.

"The first is wrong again," said Jonas, "because she did not say she was in favour. The third is too small. Nobody will notice it." Mrs. Cole nodded and took a pen. "Then we choose the second, on the front page, in the same place."
Councillor Hart read it the next morning and phoned the editor. "Thank you," she said simply. "That is exactly what I said."
ch.clue: the whole sentence
ch.q: Which correction is the most accurate and fair?
o: The one that removes the old article from the website
The one that says Hart is in favour of the road
The one that prints the full sentence and Hart's condition
The one that only mentions a shortened quote on page two
The one that blames the reporter for the mistake
ch.hint: Doğru düzeltme, Hart'ın gerçekte ne söylediğini tam olarak vermeli ve ne eksik ne fazla olmalı. Hangi düzeltme bunu yapıyor?
ch.why: İkinci düzeltme tam cümleyi ve Hart'ın koşulunu veriyordu; ilki Hart'ın sözlerini yeniden çarpıtıyor, üçüncüsü fark edilemeyecek kadar küçüktü.

outro: Gazete tam cümleyi yayımlayarak düzeltme yaptı ve Hart ile okurlardan özür diledi. Jonas, redaksiyon masasına şunu yazdı: kısaltılan bir cümle, bazen farklı bir cümledir.

title: The Quiet Pond
hero: Park korucusu Wren Calder ve köpeği Bracken
intro: Bir çiftliğin göletinde onlarca balık ölü bulundu. Çiftçi birilerinin gölete zehir attığını düşünüyor. Park korucusu Wren Calder ile köpeği Bracken, suyu ölçerek ve izleri okuyarak gerçeği bulmaya çalışıyor.

text: At six in the morning, Farmer Rowan phoned the park office in a trembling voice. "Somebody has poisoned my pond," he said. "There are dead fish everywhere. Please come before the foxes do."

Ranger Wren Calder arrived in half an hour with her dog Bracken and a box of measuring tools. The pond lay behind the old barn, about fifty metres across, grey and still in the morning mist. Dozens of fish floated near the shore, their silver bellies up. Wren counted them quickly: carp and tench, some of them as long as her forearm. The water was thick and green, like pea soup, and the shore smelled of rotten leaves.

She walked slowly round the edge. In the shallow places, among the reeds, small fish no bigger than a finger darted in the water, quite lively. Frogs sat on the stones and watched her. At the far end, a pair of ducks paddled calmly, as if nothing had happened.

"If someone had poured poison," Wren said, thinking aloud, "the ducks, the frogs and the little fish would have died as well. Poison usually does not choose by size." She opened her toolbox and took out a small bottle of test liquid. "Let us start with the numbers."
ch.clue: small fish no bigger than a finger darted in the water
ch.q: Why does Wren doubt that the pond was poisoned?
o: The farmer had no reason to protect the pond
The fish died during the morning, not during the night
Small fish, frogs and ducks were unharmed, while only large fish died
