The water was green, which is a sign of good health
The pond smelled of rotten leaves, not of chemicals
ch.hint: Ölü balıklar nasıl, canlı kalanlar neler? Zehir genellikle büyüklüğe göre seçim yapar mı? Gölette kimler hâlâ sağlıklı?
ch.why: Küçük balıklar, kurbağalar ve ördekler sağlamdı, yalnızca büyük balıklar ölmüştü; bu bir zehirlenme için olağandışıydı.

text: Wren worked quickly. First, she tested the acidity of the water, dipping a paper strip into the pond. It turned a pale yellow-green that matched the number 7.2, the usual level for a healthy pond. Then she checked for traces of the chemicals that farmers use against pests. The result was zero.

"Not poison," she said. "Now the oxygen." She took out a small metal meter on a long wire and lowered it into the water. The number on its screen moved slowly and stopped: 1.8. "A healthy pond has more than six milligrams of oxygen in every litre," she explained to the farmer, who was standing behind her with his cap in his hands. "Large fish need a lot. Small fish, frogs and insects can survive on very little. At 1.8, the big carp are suffocating."

She wrote the time, six forty, in her notebook, and then came back in the afternoon to measure again. By three o'clock, in the bright sun, the same meter showed eleven. "Eleven," she said. "So much oxygen in the afternoon, and almost none at dawn. The pond breathes in a cycle. It loses oxygen in the night and gains it in the day."
The farmer frowned. "Ponds do not breathe," he said. Wren smiled. "This one does. And I think I know who is doing the breathing."
ch.clue: By three o'clock, in the bright sun, the same meter showed eleven
ch.q: What do the two oxygen readings show?
o: Oxygen stays the same at every hour of the day
Oxygen is controlled by the temperature of the barn
Oxygen is highest at dawn and lowest in the afternoon
Oxygen is much lower at the shore than in the middle
Oxygen drops during the night and rises again in the sunshine
ch.hint: Sabah 6:40'ta ve öğleden sonra 3'te ölçülen oksijen değerlerini karşılaştır. Gün içinde göletin oksijeni nasıl değişiyor?
ch.why: Sabah oksijen çok düşüktü (1,8) ve güneşli öğleden sonra çok yüksekti (11); oksijen geceleri düşüyor, gündüz artıyordu.

text: "Who is doing the breathing?" asked the farmer. Wren pointed at the green water. "Algae. Millions of tiny plants, floating everywhere. In the daytime, they use sunlight and make oxygen, the way every plant does. But at night, without light, they take oxygen from the water, like we do when we breathe. If there are only a few algae, the pond can easily survive the night. But if the pond is full of them, as this one is, they can use all the oxygen before dawn. The big fish die first."

"But why so many algae this year?" asked the farmer. "Last summer, the pond was clear." Wren looked up the slope, where a field of young wheat ran down to the edge of the pond. A narrow ditch, still wet, ran along the border of the field and ended in the water.

She followed it with Bracken. The ditch was full of brown water, and on the bank, small white grains lay scattered, like salt. She picked one up and tasted nothing, only dust. "Fertiliser," she said. "When did you spread it?"
"Last Tuesday," said the farmer slowly. "And on Sunday it rained very hard. The whole slope was running with water."
Wren looked at the brown line that led from the field to the pond. "Then I think I have found the food of your algae," she said.
ch.clue: small white grains lay scattered
ch.q: Why did so many algae grow in the pond?
o: The ducks had brought algae from another lake
Fertiliser from the field washed into the pond with the rain
The barn walls had dropped paint into the water
The summer was hotter than the previous summer
The farmer had put too many fish into the pond
ch.hint: Çiftçi gübreyi ne zaman serpti ve pazar günü ne oldu? Hendek tarlayı nereye bağlıyor?
ch.why: Gübre tarlaya salı günü serpilmişti ve pazar günkü yağmur onu hendekle göle taşımıştı; gübre alglerin besiniydi.

text: Over a cup of coffee in the farm kitchen, Wren laid out the problem in simple words. "It was not poison and it was not a crime," she said. "The fertiliser did what it is made to do. It made plants grow, only the wrong plants, in the wrong place. If nothing changes, the same thing will happen next spring."

Farmer Rowan scratched his head. "I do not want to lose my wheat, and I do not want to lose my fish. What can I do?" Wren drew three small pictures on the back of an envelope. In the first, she drew a pump with a tube in the pond. In the second, a new fence around it. In the third, a green stripe of long grass between the field and the water.

"The pump adds air, but only when it is running, and it costs a lot of electricity," she said. "The fence keeps animals out, and that is no problem here. The grass strip, five or six metres wide, would catch the water from the field before it reaches the pond. The roots hold the fertiliser and use it. It costs almost nothing."
The farmer looked at the third picture for a long time. "A strip of grass," he said. "And I always thought I was wasting that corner."
ch.clue: a green stripe of long grass between the field and the water
ch.q: Which solution addresses the cause of the problem?
o: A pump to add air to the water all day long
A new ditch to carry more water to the pond
More large fish to eat the algae in the water
A strip of long grass to stop fertiliser reaching the pond
A fence around the pond to keep animals away
ch.hint: Sorun, gübrenin göle taşınması. Bunu kaynağında durduran, ucuz ve doğal çözüm hangisi?
ch.why: Tarla ile gölet arasına bir çim şeridi koymak, gübrenin göle ulaşmasını kökünden engelliyordu.

outro: Gölet kısa sürede yeniden canlandı ve çiftçi tarlanın kenarına bir çim şeridi ekledi. Wren, defterine şunu yazdı: doğada suçlu aramadan önce, ölçümlere sormak gerekir.

title: The Restored Masterpiece
hero: Küratör Hugo Laurent ve güvenlik görevlisi Mina
intro: Müzenin 1650 tarihli Hollandalı ressam tablosunda laboratuvar testi modern bir boya buldu. Gazeteler tablonun sahte olduğunu yazmaya başladı. Küratör Hugo Laurent ile güvenlik görevlisi Mina, tablonun gerçekte ne olduğunu araştırıyor.

text: The Lacemaker's Window had hung in the Dutch Room of the City Museum for forty years. It showed a young woman in a dark dress, sitting by a window with a pillow of white thread on her knees, in the soft light of a winter afternoon. The label said: Dutch School, 1650. Everybody in the town knew and loved it.

On Monday morning, Hugo Laurent opened an envelope from the laboratory of the university, and his face went pale. The report was short and polite. As a part of a routine study, the scientists had analysed tiny samples of paint from fifteen places in the picture. In twelve of them, the pigments were typical of the seventeenth century: lead white, red earth and a blue made from crushed stone. But in three samples, the scientists found titanium white.

"Titanium white," Hugo read aloud to Mina, who had come into his office with two cups of tea. "The report says that this pigment was not made until the year 1921. It is bright and very pure, and painters began to use it in the twentieth century."
Mina put the cups down. "In a picture painted in 1650?" she asked. "Then the newspapers are right. It is a fake."
Hugo did not answer at once. "Three samples out of fifteen," he said slowly. "Before I say anything, I want to see where they are."
ch.clue: titanium white
ch.q: Why is the presence of titanium white a problem for the painting?
o: The pigment is poisonous to anyone who touches it
The pigment is too expensive for a Dutch painter
The pigment was forbidden in the seventeenth century
The pigment did not exist until 1921, long after 1650
The pigment was used only in modern buildings
ch.hint: Raporda titanyum beyazının ne zaman icat edildiği yazıyor. 1650 tarihli bir tabloda bu boyanın bulunması neden şüpheli?
ch.why: Titanyum beyazı ancak 1921'den sonra kullanılabiliyordu; 1650'de yapılan bir tabloda bulunmaması gerekirdi.

text: Hugo asked the laboratory for a map of the samples. It arrived in the afternoon: a photograph of the painting, covered with fifteen small red circles, each with a number. Three of them, numbers 4, 9 and 12, had a green line around them. Hugo spread it on the table, and Mina stood beside him.

"Number 4," he said, "is on the woman's left sleeve, in the white of the lace. Number 9 is in the window, a bit of white in the corner of the glass. And number 12 is at the bottom of the picture, on the floor, a pale patch of light." He looked at the map for a long time. "These three spots are all very small. And they are all in the places where the picture was damaged."

"How do you know?" asked Mina. Hugo pointed at the photograph. "Look at the surface. In these places, you can see tiny cracks, or a slightly different colour. In the lace, there is a small round loss. In the window, a long thin scratch. The paint has fallen off, and somebody repaired it."

"And the other twelve samples?" said Mina. "Those are all old," said Hugo. "Every one of them, from the face, the dress, the wall, the pillow. The old paint is everywhere. The modern paint is only in the injured places."
ch.clue: In these places, you can see tiny cracks
ch.q: What does the position of the titanium white suggest?
o: Someone retouched small damaged areas with modern paint
The whole painting was made again in the twentieth century
The artist used a special white for the lace only
The laboratory made a mistake in all fifteen samples
The painting was cleaned with a chemical in the museum
ch.hint: Titanyum beyazı hangi yerlerde bulundu: tablonun tamamında mı, yoksa yalnızca çatlak, kayıp ve çizik gibi hasarlı bölgelerde mi?
ch.why: Modern boya yalnızca küçük, hasar görmüş yerlerde bulunmuştu; biri bu yerleri sonradan rötuşlamıştı.

text: "If it was repaired," said Mina, "there must be a record." Hugo opened a heavy grey file with the title of the painting. "Of course. The museum has kept every document since the painting came to us as a gift in 1931." He turned the pages slowly. Most of them were bills and letters, yellow and soft, but near the end he found a report written in 1953 by a conservator named Mr. Aldous.

He read aloud: "Following the fire of 1948, which damaged the east gallery, the painting suffered from heat and from water. Several small areas of paint were lost, especially on the sleeve, at the window and on the floor. The lost areas were repaired with white pigment of the most modern kind, titanium white, mixed to match the old paint. The restoration is limited to the damaged places. The original paint has not been touched."
Mina took a deep breath. "So a painter fixed it, in the fifties, and wrote it down."

"And then the papers were forgotten in a drawer for seventy years," said Hugo. "The laboratory in the university did not have the report, and nobody told them. Their results are correct. It is only that the explanation was lost."
ch.clue: titanium white, mixed to match the old paint
ch.q: Why did the laboratory find a modern pigment in an old painting?
o: The painting was a copy made after the fire in 1948
The museum painted over it when the painting arrived
A conservator in 1953 used it to repair fire damage
A visitor spilled paint on the picture in 1931
The artist added it himself when he finished the painting
ch.hint: 1953 raporunda restoratör hangi hasarları ve hangi boyayı anlatıyor? Bu bilgi laboratuvarın bulgusunu nasıl açıklıyor?
ch.why: 1953'te restoratör, 1948'deki yangının hasarını titanyum beyazıyla onarmıştı; laboratuvarın bulduğu modern boya bu rötuştu.

text: "But how do we know the rest is truly old?" said Mina. "The twelve samples say so, but twelve samples are not the whole painting." Hugo smiled. "That is a very good question. I would like a completely different test, one that does not depend on paint."

He called a colleague in the university, who studied the wood of old panels. A week later, she sent a short email: "The Lacemaker's Window is painted on an oak panel. I measured the rings in the wood, from the edge, and compared them with a database. The last ring, closest to the painted surface, dates from the year 1631. Allowing for the years a panel was usually dried before painting, I would estimate that the painting was made between 1640 and 1660."

Hugo put down his pen and sat back in his chair. "So the wood is old," he said. "The old paint is everywhere. The new paint is only in the small, damaged spots, and the report says why." He looked at Mina. "Today's newspaper says that the painting is a fake. Tomorrow's will say it is not."
"What is the correct description?" asked Mina. Hugo took a marker and a new label card.
ch.clue: The last ring, closest to the painted surface
ch.q: What is the most accurate description of the painting?
o: A modern copy made from old wood and old paint
A forgery painted completely in the year 1921
A painting whose age cannot be decided by anybody
A painting from 1948, made after the museum fire
A seventeenth-century original with small twentieth-century repairs
ch.hint: Tahta panel yaklaşık 1640-1660'lara tarihleniyor, eski boya her yerde, modern boya yalnızca onarım yerlerinde. Bu üç bilgiyi birleştiren tanım hangisi?
ch.why: Panel ve boyanın çoğu 17. yüzyıldandı; modern boya yalnızca 1953'teki küçük onarımlardan geliyordu: gerçek bir eser, küçük rötuşlarla.

outro: Tablo, bir restorasyon geçirmiş gerçek bir 17. yüzyıl eseri olarak müze kataloğuna yeniden yazıldı. Hugo, Mina'ya şunu söyledi: bir tablonun her yeri aynı yaşta olmak zorunda değildir, ama her yerinin bir hikâyesi vardır.

title: The Three Signs
hero: Oyun testçileri Zoe ve Max
intro: Zoe ve Max bu kez "Üç Kapı" adlı bir kaçış odasında. Her bulmaca bir öncekinden biraz daha zor ve süre kısıtlı. Doğru mantık yürütmek, hızlı davranmaktan daha önemli.

text: The door closed behind Zoe and Max with a heavy sound, and a large digital clock on the wall began to count: 60:00. They were standing in a narrow hall with three identical wooden doors in front of them, numbered 1, 2 and 3. On each door hung a small brass sign, and above the doors, written in white paint, was a line of instructions:
Only one door leads out. The others lead to rooms from which there is no way back. Exactly one of the three signs tells the truth.

Max read the signs aloud, one by one, and Zoe copied them into her notebook. The sign on Door 1 said: The exit is here. The sign on Door 2 said: The exit is not here. The sign on Door 3 said: The exit is not behind Door 1.

"Exactly one sign is true, and two are false," said Zoe, tapping her pen. "That is a strong rule. We can test each door in our heads. If the exit is behind a door, we can check how many of the three signs would then be true. It must be exactly one."
"We have no second chance," Max said quietly, looking at the clock. "So let us not guess. Let us check them carefully, one by one."
ch.clue: Exactly one of the three signs tells the truth
ch.q: Which door leads out?
o: Doors 1 and 3 together
It is impossible to say
Door 3
Door 1
Door 2
ch.hint: Her kapının arkasında çıkış olduğunu varsay ve üç levhadan kaçının doğru olacağını say. Yalnızca bir levha doğru olmalı.
ch.why: Çıkış 2 numaralı kapıdaysa yalnızca üçüncü levha doğrudur; 1'de iki, 3'te iki levha doğru olurdu; yalnızca 2 numara kurala uyar.

text: Behind Door 2 there was a small round room with a table and a sheet of paper. The room was warm and smelled of old wood, and a green lamp lit the table. On the paper was a table with all the letters of the alphabet, and next to each letter a number: A was 1, B was 2, C was 3, and so on, up to Z, which was 26. Under it, in large capital letters, a message said: THE CODE OF THE LOCKED BOX IS THE SUM OF THE LETTERS OF THE WORD THAT HOLDS THE EXIT.

Max read it twice. "The word that holds the exit," he said. "It must be the word on the door, the one we have just opened. Look at the brass plate above the frame." Zoe stepped back and raised the lamp. Above the doorframe, on a small plate, a single word was engraved in capitals: DOOR.

"D, O, O, R," said Zoe. She took her pencil. "D is the fourth letter, so it is four. O is the fifteenth letter. R is the eighteenth." She wrote the numbers in a column on the paper. "Two Os, don't forget."
On the table stood a little wooden box with four small wheels for a number code. Max looked at the clock. They had spent thirteen minutes, and there were forty-seven left.
ch.clue: THE SUM OF THE LETTERS OF THE WORD THAT HOLDS THE EXIT
ch.q: What is the code for the box?
ch.hint: D=4, O=15, R=18 ve kelimede iki tane O var. Harflerin sayı karşılıklarını topla.
ch.why: DOOR kelimesinde D=4, O=15, O=15, R=18; toplam 52'dir.

text: The wooden box opened with a click, and inside, on a velvet cloth, lay eight silver balls, all exactly the same size, next to a small balance scale with two flat pans. A card on the lid said: Seven of the balls weigh the same. One is a little heavier. You may use the scale only twice. Put the heavier ball in the small tray at the end of the table to open the next lock.

Zoe took the balls out of the box and arranged them on the cloth in two rows. "Eight balls and two weighings," she said. "If we put four against four, we know which group is heavier, but then we have four balls and only one weighing left. Four balls are too many for one weighing."

Max drew a picture on the paper. "What if we divide them into three groups?" he said. "Not two. For example, three here, three there, and two left aside. If we put the groups of three on the scale, either one side goes down, or the scale stays level."

"And what does each of those tell us?" asked Zoe, trying to see the whole plan. Max did not answer yet. He wrote the numbers 3, 3 and 2 on the paper and underlined them, one after another, while the clock above them moved from 41:10 to 40:55.
ch.clue: You may use the scale only twice
ch.q: How should they use the first weighing?
o: Put all eight balls on one pan of the scale
Put one ball against one and leave six aside
Weigh the box and the balls together
Put three balls against three, and leave two aside
Put four balls against four on the scale
ch.hint: Sadece iki tartım hakkın var. Dört-dört yaparsan dört topun içinde tek tartımla ağır olanı bulabilir misin? Üç gruba bölme fikrinin neden işe yaradığını düşün.
ch.why: Üç topa karşı üç top tartıp iki topu kenarda bırakmak, ilk tartımla problemi en fazla üç topa indirir ve ikinci tartım yeter.

text: The heavy ball dropped into the little tray, and a drawer slid out of the table with a long soft noise. Inside there was a last box with a round keypad of four digits, and a note on a card: To open the last door, enter the real time shown by the old clock. But beware: the clock does not tell the truth.

Max pointed to the wall. Above the exit door hung an old brass clock with a white face and thin black hands, ticking very loudly. It showed twenty-five minutes to ten. Under it, in tiny letters on a brass label, someone had engraved: This clock is twelve minutes fast. Please set your life by it, and subtract.

"The old clock says twenty-five to ten," Zoe said. "Nine thirty-five. And the label says that it runs twelve minutes ahead of the real time." She stopped. "That is an interesting kind of lie. A clock that is too fast is not a stupid clock, it is just early."
"The real time is earlier than the clock," said Max. He read the line again. "The keypad has four digits, so the hours and the minutes. I think I have the number, but I want to count it twice."
Behind them, the big digital clock showed 08:30. They had eight minutes and thirty seconds left to leave the room.
ch.clue: This clock is twelve minutes fast
ch.q: What code should they enter on the keypad?
ch.hint: Eski saat 9:35'i gösteriyor ama on iki dakika ileri. Gerçek saati bulmak için ileri giden süreyi çıkar ve dört haneli saat-dakika biçiminde yaz.
ch.why: Saat 9:35'i gösteriyordu ama 12 dakika ileriydi; gerçek saat 9:23'tü, yani kod 0923'tü.

outro: Çıkış kapısı açıldı ve oda sahibi iki arkadaşı alkışladı. Zoe, Max'e şöyle dedi: iyi bir bulmacanın en güzel yanı, cevabı bulduğunda neden hep orada olduğunu anlamaktır.

title: The Time Zone Trap
hero: Havalimanı görevlisi Dara Mills ve stajyer Sam
intro: Dubai havalimanında bir yolcu, devam uçuşunu beş saat erken geldiğini düşünerek kaçırdı. Havalimanı görevlisi Dara Mills ile stajyer Sam, zaman farklarını hesaplayarak yolcunun neden geç kaldığını ve onu ertesi günkü toplantısına ulaştırmanın yolunu arıyor.

text: It was ten o'clock in the morning at Dubai airport, and Mr. Tan stood in front of the information desk of Dara Mills with a heavy bag on his shoulder and a pale face. He was a tall man in a grey suit, about forty years old, and he was almost out of breath.

"I have missed my flight to Colombo," he said. "It left at a quarter to ten. But I am sure I was early. I arrived at the gate at five thirty-five in the morning, according to my watch, and I sat down to read. There were four hours before the plane. I fell asleep for a while, and when I woke up the gate was empty."

Dara looked at his boarding pass. It said: Dubai to Colombo, departure 09:45. "Did the gate not have a clock?" she asked. "I never looked at it," said Mr. Tan. "My watch is a good one, a gift from my wife. I trusted it."
Sam, her trainee, was reading Mr. Tan's first boarding pass at the same time, the one for the flight from London. "Sir," he said slowly, "what time zone is your watch on?"
Mr. Tan looked at his wrist and then at the large clock above the desk. The big clock said 10:05. His watch said 06:05.
ch.clue: His watch said 06:05
ch.q: What is the main reason for Mr. Tan's problem?
o: His watch was still set to London time, not Dubai time
He misread the number on his boarding pass
The airline changed the flight time without telling
His watch was broken and had stopped at 06:05
The airport clock above the desk was wrong
ch.hint: Büyük saat 10:05'i, yolcunun saati ise 06:05'i gösteriyor. İki saat arasındaki dört saatlik farkın kaynağı ne olabilir? Yolcu hangi şehirden gelmişti?
ch.why: Mr. Tan'ın saati hâlâ Londra saatindeydi; havalimanı saati Dubai saatiydi ve aralarında dört saat fark vardı.

text: Dara took a pen and drew a small diagram on a piece of paper, while Sam explained it to Mr. Tan in a gentle voice. "In winter, London is on Greenwich time, which scientists call UTC. Dubai is four hours ahead of UTC, all year round. So when it is six o'clock in London, it is already ten in Dubai."

"That is why my watch and the airport clock are four hours apart," said Mr. Tan slowly. "But I do not understand. I looked at my watch, and it said five thirty-five when I arrived at the gate. The airport clock must have said nine thirty-five."

"Exactly," said Dara. "You thought you had four hours before the flight. In reality, you had ten minutes. When you sat down, the plane was almost ready to leave. When your watch showed 05:45, the real time in Dubai was exactly the same as the flight time on your boarding pass."
She drew a circle around two numbers on her diagram: 05:45 on one side, 09:45 on the other. "Your watch told you what time it is in a city where you no longer are," she said.
Mr. Tan held his head in his hands. "Four hours," he said. "I forgot, because I slept on the plane, and the flight attendant announced the local time in the morning, when I was sleeping."
ch.clue: Dubai is four hours ahead of UTC
ch.q: At what time on Mr. Tan's watch did the flight actually leave?
ch.hint: Dubai Londra'dan dört saat ileride. Uçak Dubai saatiyle 09:45'te kalktı. O anda Londra saatine ayarlı saat kaçı gösteriyordu?
ch.why: Dubai saati Londra'dan dört saat ileri olduğu için, Dubai'de 09:45 olduğunda Londra saatindeki saat 05:45'i gösteriyordu.

text: "I am going to be very honest with you," said Dara. "The airline's rule is that a passenger who misses a flight because he reads the time wrongly must buy a new ticket. That would cost you nearly six hundred pounds."

Mr. Tan took a deep breath. "I understand. It was my mistake." But Sam was reading the boarding pass again with a frown. "Dara, look at this," he said. He turned the paper over. Under the printed flight times, in very small letters, was a line that nobody normally reads: All times shown are local times at the place of departure. Time zones may differ. Passengers are responsible for checking local time.
Dara read the line, and then she looked at Mr. Tan with new interest. "So the airline told you," she said. "In very small letters. You did not read it, and neither does anybody."
"I only look at the big numbers," Mr. Tan admitted.

"I will be honest again," said Dara. "The airline is right according to the rule. But a rule that nobody can read is a bad rule. I will talk to my manager, and I will ask whether we can rebook you free of charge, as a goodwill gesture. I cannot promise anything."
She picked up the telephone, and Sam saw her mouth move in a small smile.
ch.clue: Passengers are responsible for checking local time
ch.q: What does the small print on the ticket say?
o: The airline is responsible for all time changes
Tickets can be exchanged without any extra payment
Passengers must arrive at least four hours before departure
Flights always depart ten minutes later than printed
Times are local, and passengers must check the time zones
ch.hint: Biletin arkasındaki küçük harfli satır uçuş saatleri ve yolcunun sorumluluğu hakkında ne söylüyor? Sam bu satırı neden fark etti?
ch.why: Küçük yazı, saatlerin kalkış yerinin yerel saati olduğunu ve zaman farkını kontrol etmenin yolcunun sorumluluğu olduğunu söylüyordu.

text: The manager agreed to rebook Mr. Tan, without charge, on the next flight with free seats. Dara looked at the screen. "There are two possibilities," she said. "A flight at 14:20, which is full, and another at 18:05, with seats. The flight to Colombo takes four hours and ten minutes. And Colombo is an hour and a half ahead of Dubai."

Mr. Tan had a meeting in Colombo the next morning at ten o'clock in the city's local time. He took out a notebook and began to calculate. Sam helped him on a spare piece of paper. If the plane left at 18:05 Dubai time, it would land four hours and ten minutes later, at 22:15, still in Dubai time. In Colombo, an hour and a half ahead, the clocks would say 23:45.
"So I arrive at a quarter to midnight tonight," said Mr. Tan. "And the meeting is at ten the next morning. That is ten hours and a quarter to sleep, and to put on a clean shirt."
"Exactly," said Dara. "And please, before you board, change your watch."
Mr. Tan smiled for the first time that day, and, in front of both of them, he pressed the small button on the side of his watch.
ch.clue: an hour and a half ahead of Dubai
ch.q: At what local time will Mr. Tan arrive in Colombo?
o: 22:15 the same evening
23:45 the same evening
18:05 the same evening
02:15 the next morning
10:00 the next morning
ch.hint: Uçuş 18:05'te kalkıyor, 4 saat 10 dakika sürüyor ve Colombo Dubai'den bir buçuk saat ileride. Varış saatini Dubai saatiyle hesapla, sonra Colombo saatine çevir.
ch.why: 18:05 + 4 saat 10 dakika = 22:15 Dubai saati; Colombo bir buçuk saat ileride olduğu için varış saati 23:45'tir.

outro: Mr. Tan ertesi sabah Colombo'da toplantısına yetişti ve saatini yerel saate ayarlamayı hiç unutmadı. Dara, Sam'e şunu söyledi: zaman farkı bir yolculuğun kolay yeri değildir; en kolay şey, saati yeni yere uydurmaktır.

title: The Borrowed Code
hero: Dedektif Edmund Crane ve yardımcısı Tess
intro: Pazar sabahı erkenden Hartley Caddesi'ndeki mücevher dükkânı soyuldu. Alarm, yetkili bir kodla kapatılmış. Dedektif Edmund Crane ile yardımcısı Tess, kodu bilen üç kişiyi ve onların anlattıklarını dikkatle karşılaştırıyor.

text: Rhodes & Daughter was the finest jeweller's shop on Hartley Street, with a window of dark blue velvet and a door so heavy that two people had to push it. On Sunday morning, when the manager arrived to find the door unlocked and the cases empty, he called the police first and Edmund Crane second.

When Crane and Tess entered the shop at eight o'clock, the manager, Mr. Rhodes, a stout man with white hair, was sitting on a chair with a glass of water. "Forty thousand pounds of rings and watches," he said. "Gone in one night. And the alarm did not make a sound."

Crane looked at the alarm panel near the door. It had a screen and a keypad, and under the screen a list of events scrolled slowly. The last line said: Alarm disarmed 06:12 using manager's personal code. Before it: Alarm armed 19:03 Saturday.
"So the code was entered at twelve minutes past six," said Tess. "Nobody forced the door. The thief knew the number."

"The security company changes it on the first day of every month," said Mr. Rhodes. "This month's new code was sent to me by phone, and to my assistant Pia, so that she could open the shop in an emergency. The technician from the company, Mr. Kerr, also knows it, of course, because he programmes the panel. That is all. Three people."
Crane took out his notebook and wrote three names in a column.
ch.clue: using manager's personal code
ch.q: What can Crane conclude from the alarm record?
o: A professional thief broke the alarm system at night
Someone who knew the monthly code entered it at 6:12
The police had disarmed the alarm for their visit
The manager forgot to arm the alarm on Saturday
The alarm was never switched on on Saturday evening
ch.hint: Alarm kaydında saat kaçta ve hangi kodla devre dışı bırakıldığı yazıyor. Kapı zorlanmamış. Bu bilgiler, hırsızın koda dair neyi bildiğini düşündürür?
ch.why: Alarm 06:12'de aylık kodla kapatılmıştı ve kapı zorlanmamıştı; hırsız kodu önceden biliyordu.

text: Crane started with the manager. "Mr. Rhodes, where were you at twelve minutes past six this morning?" The jeweller took a plastic card from his pocket. "At Heathrow airport," he said. "I was catching the six-forty flight to Edinburgh for my daughter's graduation. Here is the boarding pass." It was stamped at 6:05 at the gate. Tess photographed it. "And the airport camera will have a picture of me, if you like," he added. "I was the one who spilled coffee on a police officer."

Crane smiled and made a note. The next person was Pia, a quiet young woman of twenty-two who worked at the shop on weekdays. She was waiting on the pavement outside with red eyes. "I was on the bus," she said. "Visiting my grandmother in Northgate. I take the 5:40 from the station, and it takes about forty minutes. I have the ticket." She showed a small yellow paper. The machine had stamped it at 5:43, with the code of the bus: N7.
"And your bus did not stop on the way?" asked Crane. "It stops at every village," said Pia. "We reached Northgate at twenty past six. I know, because I looked at the church clock."

Crane turned to Tess. "One alibi is stamped at an airport gate. The other is stamped on a moving bus. Neither can be in two places at once," he said quietly. "That leaves only the third name on the list."
ch.clue: It was stamped at 6:05 at the gate
ch.q: Why can Crane eliminate Mr. Rhodes and Pia?
o: Both of them said that they love their jobs very much
Both had taken the day off from the shop
Both lived many miles from Hartley Street
Their timed tickets place them far from the shop at 6:12
Both had the codes written on their personal cards
ch.hint: Müdürün biniş kartı ve Pia'nın otobüs bileti hangi saatte damgalanmış ve alarm kaç saatte kapatılmış? İki kişi aynı anda iki yerde olabilir mi?
ch.why: Rhodes 06:05'te havalimanındaydı, Pia ise 05:43'te otobüse binmişti; ikisi de 06:12'de dükkâna uzaktı.

text: Mr. Kerr, the security technician, was a calm man in his forties, with a neat blue uniform and a company badge on his chest. Crane found him in his small flat on Bridge Road, drinking tea in front of a television. When Crane told him about the robbery, Kerr listened politely and shook his head.

"Terrible," he said. "I changed the code on the first of the month, in the afternoon, when the shop was closed. Yes, I know it. But I have not touched the panel since then. And this morning I was at home, in bed, until nine. You can ask my neighbour. I do not go out on Sundays."
"You did not go out at all?" asked Crane. "Not even for a walk, or to buy a newspaper?" Kerr shook his head. "Never on Sundays."

On the way out, Tess looked at the small parking space behind the building. A white van with a blue stripe stood there, and on the door, in blue letters, was the name of the security company. She walked round it. Under the windscreen, a small black box with a green light was fixed to the dashboard, with a sticker: Fleet GPS. Please do not remove.
"Mr. Crane," she said softly, "I think this van has a very good memory."
ch.clue: Fleet GPS
ch.q: What does Tess's discovery about the van suggest?
o: The van's GPS may record where Kerr really was that morning
The van's blue stripe is the proof of the thief's identity
The van belongs to Rhodes and not to the company
The van proves that Kerr had been at work all night
The van was bought with the money from the robbery
ch.hint: Kerr "Pazar günleri hiç dışarı çıkmam" diyor. Minibüsün torpidosunda ne var ve bu cihaz sürüş geçmişi hakkında ne söyler?
ch.why: Minibüste filo GPS cihazı vardı; Kerr'in gerçekte nerede olduğunu kaydediyor olabilirdi.

text: The company's office opened on Monday morning, and its manager, after a short telephone call with the police, agreed to print the GPS record. It was a long strip of paper with times, places and speeds. Crane read it standing up, with Tess at his elbow.

"Sunday," he said. "Five fifty-two: the van leaves the parking space in Bridge Road. Six oh two: it stops in Mill Lane, which is the narrow street behind the shop. Six forty-one: it leaves Mill Lane. Six fifty-five: it returns to Bridge Road." He tapped the paper. "The van stayed for thirty-nine minutes, a hundred metres from the back door of Rhodes & Daughter. And the alarm was disarmed at 6:12, in the middle of it."
Tess looked at the report. "He said that he was in bed until nine."

"He said that he had not touched the panel," said Crane. "He did not need to touch the panel of the shop's alarm in order to know the code. He had set the code himself. Mr. Rhodes was in the air, and Pia was on the bus. Only one person who knew the number was in the street."
When the two detectives came back to Bridge Road with the police, Mr. Kerr opened the door in his dressing gown. He looked at the paper in Crane's hand. He did not need to read it.
ch.clue: The van stayed for thirty-nine minutes
ch.q: How does the GPS record expose the technician?
o: It shows that his van visited Pia's grandmother
It records the exact code that he used on the panel
It places his van near the shop when the alarm was disarmed
It proves that the van was stolen that Sunday morning
It shows that his van never left the parking space
ch.hint: Minibüs saat kaçta Mill Lane'e gitmiş, kaçta ayrılmış ve alarm hangi dakikada kapatılmış? Kerr'in söylediğiyle karşılaştır.
ch.why: GPS kaydı minibüsün 06:02-06:41 arasında dükkânın arka sokağında olduğunu gösteriyordu; alarm 06:12'de, tam o sırada kapatılmıştı.

outro: Kerr hırsızlığı itiraf etti ve mücevherler dükkâna geri döndü. Crane şunu söyledi: bir yalan, dönüp bakıldığında hep kendi saatini ele verir.

title: The Weekend Cough
hero: Genç doktor Mara Quinn ve hemşire Joe
intro: Ms. Alvarez üç aydır geçmeyen bir öksürükle polikliniğe geldi. Röntgeni ve kan tahlili normal. Doktor Mara Quinn ile hemşire Joe, öksürüğün ne zaman azaldığını ve ne zaman arttığını dinleyerek hastalığın kaynağını arıyor.

text: On a rainy Thursday afternoon, Ms. Alvarez sat in Doctor Mara Quinn's consulting room with a paper handkerchief in her hand. She was thirty-five, worked as an accountant, and had a pleasant, tired face. "I have had this cough for three months," she said. "It is dry and irritating. It is worse at night, especially when I lie down. I do not have a fever. I am not ill in any other way."

Mara listened to her chest carefully, with the cold end of her stethoscope. The breathing sounds were clear. She asked about smoking (never), about allergies (none that she knew of) and about the medicines that Ms. Alvarez took (only a vitamin tablet). Nurse Joe brought the results of the earlier examinations from her file. The chest X-ray, done a month before, was perfectly normal. The blood tests showed no infection. A test of the lung function, done last week, was within the normal range.
"I have tried three kinds of cough syrup," said Ms. Alvarez, "and two courses of antibiotics. Nothing works, and my friends say that I am a hypochondriac."

"I do not believe that for a moment," said Mara. "When a cough does not respond to treatment, and all the tests are normal, it is often caused by something in the environment. The question is: what, and where?"
ch.clue: it is often caused by something in the environment
ch.q: Why does Mara think about the patient's environment?
o: The X-ray showed some dust in the lungs
The patient told her that she lives in a damp place
Normal tests and failed treatments suggest an outside cause
The patient had never been examined by another doctor
The patient had stopped taking her vitamin tablet
ch.hint: Röntgen, kan ve solunum testleri normal; sirop ve antibiyotikler işe yaramamış. Bu tablo, hastalığın nedenini nereye bakmayı gerektirir?
ch.why: Tüm tahliller normaldi ve tedaviler işe yaramamıştı; bu durumda neden çoğu zaman çevrede aranır.

text: "Tell me about the cough, day by day," said Mara. "When is it better, and when is it worse?" Ms. Alvarez thought, and a small frown appeared on her forehead. "It is worst in the morning, when I get up, and again in the night," she said. "In the daytime, at work, it is much milder. And at weekends..."

"What happens at weekends?" asked Joe, who was writing notes. "That is the strange thing," she said. "Every second weekend I go and stay at my mother's house in the country. And I never cough there, not once, from Friday night until Sunday afternoon. But on Sunday evening, when I come home, the cough begins again. Last month I spent a whole week of holiday at the seaside. By the third day, it was almost gone. I thought that it was the sea air."

Mara asked Joe to draw a calendar on a piece of paper and to put a cross on each day when the cough was bad. A pattern appeared at once. A long line of crosses covered the working days and the days at home, with a clear gap on every weekend in the country and the whole week at the seaside.
Mara looked at it for a long time. "The cough follows you home," she said. "It does not follow you to work, and it does not follow you to the sea."
ch.clue: I never cough there, not once
ch.q: What does the pattern of the cough suggest?
o: The cause is the stress of her work as an accountant
The cause is a serious infection that comes and goes
The cause is the vitamin tablet that she takes
The cause is the sea air and the countryside
The cause is probably at home, and she coughs when she is there
ch.hint: Öksürük hangi günlerde ve nerelerde kayboluyor, nerelerde geri geliyor? Takvimdeki çarpılar hangi yerleri işaret ediyor?
ch.why: Öksürük anne evinde ve deniz kenarında geçiyor, eve dönünce başlıyordu; neden büyük olasılıkla evdeydi.

text: "Describe your flat," said Mara. "Where do you sleep? How old is the building?" Ms. Alvarez described it with a small smile. "It is a first-floor flat in an old house. I moved there four months ago. I love it. It is bright, and it has a nice bedroom, with a big old wardrobe against the north wall. The bedroom is a bit cold. The window has to stay closed in winter, because the frames are not good."

"And the wall behind the wardrobe?" asked Mara. "I have not looked," said Ms. Alvarez. "It is very heavy. But it smells a little... how can I say... like wet cardboard. I thought it was the old wood."
Joe stopped writing. "Doctor," he said, "my aunt once had the same smell, and it was mould."

Mara nodded slowly. "Mould spores are tiny, and you breathe them in at night, when you lie in the room with a closed window for eight hours. The air in a cold room next to a damp wall is perfect for them. At work and in the country house, you do not breathe them. This would fit all your symptoms, including the timing, the dry cough and the morning problems."
"But the X-ray was normal," said Ms. Alvarez. "That is also exactly what I would expect," said Mara. "An allergy irritates the airways, but it does not leave a mark on a picture."
ch.clue: like wet cardboard
ch.q: What detail in the flat supports the doctor's idea?
o: The first-floor position of the flat in the house
A cold bedroom and a wardrobe against a wall that smells damp
The bright windows that face the street
The new furniture that she bought four months ago
A heavy wardrobe made of old and strong wood
ch.hint: Yatak odasının duvarı, penceresi ve gardırop konumu hakkında ne öğreniyoruz? "Islak karton" kokusu neye işaret edebilir?
ch.why: Soğuk bir odada, gardırobun arkasındaki duvardan ıslak karton kokusu geliyordu; bu nem ve küf için ideal bir ortamdı.

text: "I do not like to treat a guess as a fact," said Mara. "We will test it in two ways." She wrote a short note and gave it to Ms. Alvarez. The first test was a small skin test, which Joe carried out the same afternoon. He placed seven tiny drops on her forearm, each with a different common allergen: pollen, house dust mite, cat hair, mould and others. After fifteen minutes, six of the places were calm. At the seventh, the one with the mould, a red, raised, itching patch had appeared.
"A positive result," said Joe, writing it down.

The second test was in her flat. Mara asked Ms. Alvarez to pull the wardrobe away from the wall and photograph the surface. The next morning, an email arrived with two pictures. The wall behind the wardrobe was covered with black and green spots, as large as a human hand, with a pale, fluffy edge.

"The skin test and the wall are two independent witnesses," said Mara. "They say the same thing. Treat the damp problem with your landlord, clean the wall professionally, keep the room warm and ventilated, and I will give you an antihistamine for the next two weeks."
Two weeks later, Ms. Alvarez returned and did not cough once during the visit.
ch.clue: a red, raised, itching patch had appeared
ch.q: What makes Mara confident that mould causes the cough?
o: The antibiotics cleared the infection at last
Ms. Alvarez's friends also had the same cough
The cough syrup finally worked for a week
A positive skin test and mould photographed behind the wardrobe
The X-ray showed some spots in the lungs
ch.hint: İki bağımsız kanıt: deri testi ve duvarın fotoğrafı. Bunlar aynı sonucu gösterdiğinde, doktor neden daha güvenle konuşabilir?
ch.why: Deri testi küfe karşı pozitifti ve gardırobun arkasındaki duvar küf lekeleriyle kaplıydı; iki bağımsız kanıt aynı sonucu gösteriyordu.

outro: Ms. Alvarez'in yatak odasındaki nem giderildi ve öksürüğü iki haftada kayboldu. Mara şunu söyledi: bir şikâyetin hangi zamanlarda arttığını dinlemek, bazen bir tahlilden daha çok şey söyler.

title: The Ninety-Minute Pulse
hero: Komutan Noor Hale ve mühendis Pip
intro: Aurora istasyonunda kabin basıncı, tam olarak 90 dakikada bir küçük bir düşüş gösteriyor. Ekip sızıntıdan korkuyor. Komutan Noor Hale ile mühendis Pip, düşüşün gerçek mi yoksa ölçüm hatası mı olduğunu anlamak için dikkatle kayıtları inceliyor.

text: Eli was the first to notice it, because he was on night duty and had nothing to do but watch the screens. "Commander," he whispered into the radio at two in the morning, "the pressure in Module B is falling. Not much, only a little, but I think it is falling every ninety minutes. It has done it four times since midnight."

Commander Noor Hale reached the control room in five minutes, still wearing her sleeping bag around her waist. She and Pip, the engineer, studied the graph on the main screen. For most of the time, the line was almost flat, at one thousand and thirteen millibars, the pressure of normal air at sea level. Then, every ninety minutes, there was a small step down of about three millibars, and a slow climb back over the next half hour.
"Three millibars is only 0.3 percent," said Pip, "but a leak would not make the pressure climb back by itself. Unless we have an unusual leak that opens and closes."

"Let us write down what we know," said Noor, and took a marker. She wrote on the white board: One. The drop happens every ninety minutes. Two. It recovers after thirty minutes. Three. It affects only Module B.
"Ninety minutes," said Pip. He looked at her. "That is a number I know very well."
ch.clue: every ninety minutes
ch.q: What is unusual about the drop in pressure?
o: It affects all the modules of the station equally
It happens only when the crew is asleep
It is so large that the alarm should have rung
It repeats regularly and then recovers by itself
It continues to fall until the air is gone
ch.hint: Eli ve Pip basınç grafiğinde ne gözlemledi? Düşüş ne sıklıkta oluyor ve sonra ne oluyor? Gerçek bir sızıntı kendiliğinden toparlanır mı?
ch.why: Basınç düzenli olarak, yaklaşık 90 dakikada bir düşüyor ve kendiliğinden geri yükseliyordu; bu gerçek bir sızıntı için tuhaftı.

text: "Ninety minutes," Pip said again. "The Aurora goes around the Earth once every ninety minutes. In each orbit, it passes through sunlight and then through the Earth's shadow. We see sixteen sunrises and sixteen sunsets every day. The time between two sunrises is..."

"Ninety minutes," said Noor. She leaned on the table. "Do the drops coincide with the sunrises?" Pip opened the orbit file and laid the two timelines one above the other. The first line was the pressure graph. The second, drawn in yellow, showed the moments when the station entered the shadow of the Earth. At 00:12, the station entered the shadow. At 00:15, the pressure dropped. At 01:42, the next shadow. At 01:45, the next drop. And so on, with a delay of exactly three minutes each time.
"Every time we move into the shadow," said Pip, "something drops. Three minutes later. It is not a coincidence."

Noor looked at the wall clock. "In the shadow, the outside temperature falls from plus one hundred and twenty degrees to minus one hundred and sixty in a few minutes. The whole hull changes. Metal contracts when it gets cold. A pipe, a valve, a gauge, a seal..."
"Or something that only appears to be a leak," said Pip, and he reached for a notebook of his own.
ch.clue: something drops. Three minutes later
ch.q: What do the two timelines show?
o: The pressure drop follows the station's entry into the Earth's shadow
The pressure drop happens whenever the antenna is turned
The pressure drop appears at the moment of every sunrise
The pressure drop is caused by the crew opening the hatches
The pressure drop starts before the shadow begins
ch.hint: Basınç grafiği ile gölgeye girme saatlerinin grafiği yan yana konunca düşüşler ne zaman oluyor: gölgeden önce mi, sonra mı? Aradaki gecikme ne kadar?
ch.why: Her gölgeye girişten tam üç dakika sonra basınç düşüyordu; düşüş yörüngenin gün-gece döngüsüyle bağlantılıydı.

text: "Two explanations fit the facts," Noor told the crew at the morning meeting. "Number one is that the real air pressure drops, because the cold hull shrinks and opens a tiny leak, which closes again when the metal is warm. Number two is that the pressure is not changing at all. It is only our gauge which changes. The gauge is a thin metal membrane, and every material reacts to temperature."

"How can we tell the difference?" asked Eli. Pip had already thought about it. "We have a second instrument in the laboratory, a mass spectrometer. It does not measure pressure but counts the molecules of oxygen and nitrogen in a sample of air. If the real air leaks, the number of molecules must fall."

They put the instrument on the table in Module B, and they watched it through three complete orbits, almost five hours. Each time the station entered the shadow, the old gauge made its little drop. The mass spectrometer line did not move at all. It stayed completely flat, to the last digit, while the old gauge went up and down like a heartbeat.
"No molecules are leaving," said Pip. "The air is where it was."
Noor wrote it down. "The gauge is changing, and the air is not."
ch.clue: It stayed completely flat
ch.q: What does the flat line of the mass spectrometer prove?
o: The shadow of the Earth has no effect on anything
The mass spectrometer is broken and cannot be trusted
The amount of air is not changing, so the gauge is misleading
The leak is too small for any machine to measure
The air is leaving the station in a very slow way
ch.hint: Gösterge basıncı düşük gösterirken, molekül sayan cihaz sabit kalıyor. Gerçekten hava kaçıyorsa molekül sayısı nasıl değişirdi?
ch.why: Moleküllerin sayısı hiç değişmiyordu; hava kaçmıyordu, yalnızca eski gösterge sıcaklıkla yanlış değer veriyordu.

text: Pip opened the old gauge and looked at it under a lamp. It was a small, round, silver device, with a thin metal disc inside. "Every time the hull cools down, this disc contracts a tiny bit," he said. "The electronics read the movement as a drop in pressure. The factory should have added a correction for temperature, but the setting is wrong. Someone forgot to activate it when the gauge was installed."

He found the correction file in the manual, a table of numbers that matched temperature with the small error, and copied it into the gauge's memory. It took ten minutes. Then they waited. The station entered the shadow at 06:12. The temperature of the hull fell. The gauge's line, on the main screen, stayed perfectly flat.
"The pulse is gone," said Eli, a little disappointed. "I almost liked it."

Noor laughed. "I am glad that it was only a gauge," she said, "but let us record what happened. The most important thing is the way we found it. A regular pattern of ninety minutes pointed at the orbit. The second instrument showed the truth. And the correction made the problem disappear."
She wrote in the logbook: Measurement error, not a leak. Temperature correction activated.
ch.clue: Temperature correction activated
ch.q: How can the crew be sure that the problem is solved?
o: The gauge showed a lower pressure than the day before
The old gauge was replaced by a more expensive one
The crew did not hear any strange noise afterwards
Eli was disappointed because the pulse had disappeared
The gauge stayed flat as the station entered the shadow again
ch.hint: Düzeltme yapıldıktan sonra ekip neyi bekledi ve hangi anda göstergeyi izledi? Sorun çözüldüyse gölgeye girişte ne olmalıydı?
ch.why: Gölgeye girerken gösterge düz kaldı; daha önce düşüşün başladığı anda artık hiçbir şey olmuyordu.

outro: Basınç göstergesi yeniden ayarlandı ve ekip rahat bir uyku uyudu. Noor şunu söyledi: bir ölçüm tekrar eden bir düzen gösteriyorsa, genellikle olay değil ölçüm aracı konuşuyordur.

title: The Bottle on the Beach
hero: Arkeolog Dr. Amira Kent ve öğrencisi Leo
intro: Sahilde bulunan bir şişenin içinde 1805 tarihli bir denizci mektubu var. Müze bu mektubu satın almak üzere. Arkeolog Dr. Amira Kent ile öğrencisi Leo, mektubun gerçek olup olmadığını ve gerçekse ne zaman yazıldığını anlamaya çalışıyor.

text: A schoolboy found the bottle during a walk on the beach at Cape Harrow after a storm. It was green and heavy, and a cork, black with age, closed its neck. Inside there was a small roll of brown paper, tied with a thread. The boy's teacher took it to the museum, and the museum's director, Mr. Pryce, was so excited that he phoned the university the same evening.

Dr. Amira Kent and Leo arrived the next morning. The paper lay on a white sheet under a bright lamp. It was a letter, written with brown ink in a careful, old-fashioned hand. At the top, the writer had put a date: 14 March 1805. Mr. Pryce stood behind them, rubbing his hands. "If it is genuine, it is a beautiful piece," he said. "A message from a sailor in the time of Nelson. The museum could pay a good price."

Leo read the first lines aloud. "My dear Mary, I write to you from the deck of the Orion, ten days out of Portsmouth. The weather has been rough, but our ship's scientist, Mr. Hale, has been kind to all of us. He has shown me how to measure the stars..."
Amira raised a hand. "Stop a moment, Leo. Read that last sentence again."
ch.clue: our ship's scientist, Mr. Hale
ch.q: Which part of the letter makes Amira stop Leo?
o: The mention of the weather being rough
The date written at the top of the page
The name of the ship called Orion
The name of the woman called Mary
The phrase about the ship's scientist
ch.hint: Leo mektubu okurken Amira durdurdu. Mektupta, 1805'te bilim insanlarına hangi sıfatla hitap edildiğini düşün: "scientist" kelimesi o zamanlar yaygın mıydı?
ch.why: Amira, 1805 tarihli bir mektupta geçen "scientist" (bilim insanı) kelimesinde duraksadı; bu kelimenin o dönemde kullanılıp kullanılmadığından şüphelendi.

text: Leo looked puzzled. "Is the word wrong?" he asked. Amira asked him to open the big dictionary of English on the shelf, an old, heavy volume, and to find the entry for the word 'scientist'. He turned the pages, found it and read aloud: "Scientist. Noun. A person who studies science. The word was first used by William Whewell in 1833."

"Whewell invented it," said Amira. "Before that time, people said 'natural philosopher' or 'man of science'. In 1833, Whewell proposed a new word for the people who studied nature, and for many years afterwards it was not at all common. It took a long time before ordinary sailors used it in letters to their wives."
Mr. Pryce's smile slowly became smaller. "But it could still be right," he said. "Perhaps he used the word before Whewell."

"Perhaps," said Amira. "But a word cannot appear in a letter before a person has thought of it. A sailor in 1805 would write 'our ship's philosopher'. A man who writes 'scientist' is a man who lives after 1833. The letter may be genuine, Mr. Pryce, but the date at the top looks wrong."
Leo wrote a short note: Word 'scientist' invented in 1833. Letter dated 1805. Conflict.
ch.clue: The word was first used by William Whewell in 1833
ch.q: What does the history of the word 'scientist' suggest?
o: The letter is a modern fake from the last year
The letter was written in 1833 or later, not in 1805
The letter was written in another country
The word was removed from the letter by someone
The letter was written by William Whewell himself
ch.hint: Sözlük, "scientist" kelimesinin 1833'te ortaya çıktığını söylüyor. 1805'te yazılmış bir mektupta bu kelime geçebilir miydi?
ch.why: Kelime 1833'te icat edildiği için mektup en erken o tarihte yazılmış olabilirdi; 1805 tarihi yanlıştı.

text: "So is it a fake?" asked Mr. Pryce, who was pale. "Not necessarily," said Amira. "A forger who wanted to trick you would have been careful with the date. But look at the ink, and at the paper. They feel right. I would like to know whether the Orion and the people named in the letter really existed."

They went to the library and asked the librarian for the old lists of the Royal Navy. She brought three huge books. Leo found the Orion at once: a ship of the line, built in 1787, which was indeed in the Navy in 1805. He felt a surge of hope. But then he turned the page and found something else. In 1805, the Orion's journey from Portsmouth had been long, but the captain's log did not include any 'Mr. Hale'.

"Try a later date," said Amira. "Try the 1830s." Leo checked. The Orion did not exist after 1815. He turned to another page, and his finger stopped. "There is another ship," he said. "HMS Pioneer, a research ship that left Portsmouth in March 1834. And on its list of scientific officers, here, is Mr. Thomas Hale."
Amira read the line over his shoulder. "March 1834," she said slowly. "Exactly one month after the date in the letter, if the year were different."
ch.clue: HMS Pioneer, a research ship that left Portsmouth in March 1834
ch.q: What did Leo discover in the Navy lists?
o: Mr. Hale was the captain of a ship called the Orion
A sailor named Mary lived in Portsmouth in 1805
No ship in the Navy was called Orion in the 1830s
A scientist named Hale served on a ship that left in March 1834
The Orion sailed to the same place in 1805 and 1834
ch.hint: Donanma listesinde Orion'un hangi yıllarda var olduğunu ve Hale adlı bilim insanının hangi gemide, ne zaman görev yaptığını karşılaştır.
ch.why: Listede, 1834 Mart'ında Portsmouth'tan ayrılan HMS Pioneer'da Thomas Hale adlı bir bilim görevlisi vardı; mektuptaki kişiyle uyuşuyordu.

text: That evening, Amira explained her conclusion to Mr. Pryce and the museum board, in the long room with the portraits. She had written three possible explanations on a card. The first said that the letter was a modern fake, made to look old. The second said that it was a genuine letter from 1805, in which the word 'scientist' had been used by an exceptional person long before Whewell. The third said that it was a genuine letter from the 1830s, in which the writer, or a later owner, had made a mistake with the year.

"The first does not agree with the paper, the ink or the ship's records," she said. "The second needs a miracle, a word invented thirty years early, by a sailor. The third explains everything. A man called Hale was really a scientific officer on a ship leaving in March 1834. The letter says the ship left ten days before. If we read the year as 1834 rather than 1805, every part of the letter agrees, the weather, the date, the word."
"And the wrong year?" asked Mr. Pryce. "It happens very often," said Amira. "In old handwriting, a three and a zero can be confused. Or a later owner may have copied the date from memory."
The director thought for a moment. "Then it is still a treasure," he said, "but a younger one."
ch.clue: every part of the letter agrees
ch.q: Which explanation fits all the evidence best?
o: A genuine letter from the 1830s with a wrongly written year
A genuine letter from 1805 using a very early word
A modern fake made from old paper and ink
A letter written by Whewell to a friend named Mary
A letter copied by a clerk in the twentieth century
ch.hint: Mürekkep, kâğıt, gemi kayıtları, kelimenin tarihi ve Thomas Hale hep aynı döneme işaret ediyor. Tüm bu kanıtlara en iyi uyan açıklama hangisi?
ch.why: Kâğıt, mürekkep, gemi kaydı ve "scientist" kelimesi 1830'lara işaret ediyordu; mektup gerçekti ama yıl yanlış yazılmıştı.

outro: Mektup, 1830'lardan kalma gerçek bir belge olarak müzeye alındı ve yeni tarihiyle sergilendi. Amira şunu dedi: yanlış tarihli bir belge her zaman sahte değildir; bazen yalnızca birisi yılı yanlış yazmıştır.

title: Four White Powders
hero: Bilim insanı Dr. Ilan Voss ve asistanı Dana
intro: Dana'nın laboratuvar rafında etiketleri silinmiş dört beyaz toz var. Hangisinin ne olduğunu, yalnızca güvenli testlerle bulmak gerekiyor. Dr. Ilan Voss ile asistanı Dana, tozları suyla, sirkeyle ve elektrik devresiyle sınayarak etiketleri yeniden yazmaya çalışıyor.

text: On Monday morning, Dana climbed on a chair to reach the top shelf of the chemical cupboard and found four small glass jars, covered in dust. Each held a white powder. The labels had been washed away by a leak from the roof, and only four pale spots were left where they had been. Someone had marked the jars 1, 2, 3 and 4 with a felt pen.

She put them on the bench in a row and called Dr. Ilan Voss. "We do not know what is inside," she said. "It could be anything. But from the cupboard I think that there are only four possibilities, because this shelf is for kitchen chemicals: table salt, sugar, baking soda and flour."

Ilan looked at the jars with interest. "Four powders that look almost identical," he said. "A good puzzle. It would be unwise to taste them, even though they all come from the kitchen, because we do not know what has been stored with them. Let us use safe tests, one by one, and write down each result in a table."
He took a sheet of paper and drew a grid with four rows and three columns: Water, Vinegar, Electricity. "Every powder has its own personality," he said. "We only need to ask it the right questions."
ch.clue: we do not know what has been stored with them
ch.q: Why does Ilan refuse to taste the powders?
o: They are unknown and might not be what they look like
The labels say that tasting is forbidden by law
The powders are too old to have any taste left
They all taste exactly the same to every person
Dana has not yet washed her hands for the test
ch.hint: Kavanozlar etiketsiz ve yıllardır rafta. Bilinmeyen bir maddeyi tatmak neden risklidir, hele yanında başka şeyler saklandığını bilmiyorsan?
ch.why: Kavanozların içeriği bilinmiyordu ve yanlarında başka maddeler saklanmış olabilirdi; tatmak güvenli değildi.

text: Dana began with the simplest test. She put a spoonful of each powder into a separate glass of clean water, stirred with a clean spoon and waited for a minute. Ilan noted the results on his grid. The water with Powder 1 became clear, and the powder vanished completely. The water with Powder 2 also became clear. With Powder 3, the water bubbled for a moment and then became clear. But Powder 4 behaved differently. It did not dissolve at all. The water turned cloudy and white, and after a few minutes a layer of fine sediment collected at the bottom.
"One of them does not dissolve," said Dana. "It stays a suspension, and falls to the bottom. Which of our four powders does not dissolve in water?"

Ilan smiled. "Think about the kitchen," he said. "Salt dissolves in water, so does sugar, so does baking soda. Only one of the four makes a cloudy paste, which does not mix, as anyone who has made a sauce knows."
Dana wrote a name in the fourth row of the table and underlined it twice. "Flour," she said. "We have found one of the four."
"And we have narrowed the other three," said Ilan, "to salt, sugar and baking soda. Now we need a test that separates them from one another."
ch.clue: Powder 4 behaved differently. It did not dissolve at all
ch.q: Which powder is probably Powder 4?
o: Salt
Sugar
Flour
Baking soda
Vinegar powder
ch.hint: Dört tozdan hangisi suda erimedi, bulanık bir süspansiyon oluşturdu ve dibe çöktü? Mutfak malzemeleri arasında suda çözünmeyen hangisi?
ch.why: Suda çözünmeyen ve dibe çöken toz una uyuyordu; tuz, şeker ve kabartma tozu suda çözünür.

text: Next, Dana placed a small amount of each of the three dissolving powders into three clean cups, and Ilan poured a spoonful of vinegar over each of them. For Powders 1 and 2, nothing happened. The vinegar simply covered the white crystals and made them dissolve slowly. But when he poured vinegar over Powder 3, the white powder instantly started to fizz and foam, like a small volcano. Bubbles rose to the top of the cup and spilled over the edge.

"Do not lean over it," said Ilan quickly. "The gas is carbon dioxide. It is not harmful in this quantity, but let us keep our faces away." Dana stepped back and watched the foam slowly fall. "The vinegar contains an acid," Ilan explained. "When an acid meets one particular kitchen powder, it releases a gas. It is the same reaction that makes a cake rise in the oven."
"Which means that Powder 3 is..." said Dana. "I am going to say it only if you tell me I am right." Ilan nodded. "You are," he said. "Write it in the table."
She wrote the name, and then looked at the first two rows of the grid. "That leaves salt and sugar, and two powders that look exactly the same."
ch.clue: started to fizz and foam, like a small volcano
ch.q: Which powder is Powder 3?
o: Chalk
Sugar
Salt
Flour
Baking soda
ch.hint: Hangi toz sirkeyle temas edince köpürdü? Bir asit ile tepkimeye girip karbondioksit çıkaran mutfak tozu hangisidir?
ch.why: Sirkeyle köpüren ve gaz çıkaran toz, kabartma tozuydu.

text: Ilan opened a drawer and took out a small battery, a little light bulb and three wires. He connected them with clips into a simple circuit, and then left two of the wire ends free, with the tips hanging in the air. "If I put the two tips into pure water, the bulb will not light," he said. "Pure water is a very poor conductor of electricity. But if some substances dissolve in the water, they break into tiny charged particles, called ions, and these carry the current."

They stirred a spoon of Powder 1 into a fresh glass of water and put the two tips into the glass. The bulb flashed on, small and yellow. Then they washed the wire ends and repeated the test with Powder 2. The bulb remained dark, however long they waited.

"One of them breaks into ions, and the other stays in whole molecules," said Ilan. "One is a salt, which is exactly what chemists call things like table salt. The other, sugar, dissolves without making ions, and so the current cannot pass."
Dana wrote the last two names in the table and read the complete list aloud. Then she cut four small strips of paper and wrote on each one, in large capitals, the name of its powder.
ch.clue: The bulb remained dark
ch.q: Which pair of names matches Powder 1 and Powder 2?
o: Powder 1 is baking soda, and Powder 2 is flour
Powder 1 is salt, and Powder 2 is sugar
Powder 1 is sugar, and Powder 2 is salt
Powder 1 is flour, and Powder 2 is salt
Powder 1 and Powder 2 are both salt
ch.hint: Hangi toz çözeltisi ampulü yaktı, hangisi yakmadı? Elektrik akımını iyonlar taşır; tuz ve şekerden hangisi suda iyonlara ayrılır?
ch.why: Ampulü yakan 1 numaralı toz iyonlara ayrılan tuzdu; yakmayan 2 numaralı toz, iyon oluşturmayan şekerdi.

outro: Dört kavanozun etiketleri yeniden yazıldı ve rafa geri kondu. Ilan, defterine şunu yazdı: bilinmeyen bir şeyi tanımanın en iyi yolu, onu bilinen şeylerle karşılaştırmaktır.

title: Three Hundred Percent
hero: Muhabir Jonas Reid ve fotoğrafçı Ellie
intro: Bir rakip gazete, Kingsbridge'de hırsızlıkların yüzde 200 arttığını yazdı. Kasaba paniğe kapıldı. Muhabir Jonas Reid ile fotoğrafçı Ellie, rakamın ne anlama geldiğini ve haberin gerçekte neyi gösterdiğini inceliyor.

text: On Friday morning, the whole town was talking about a headline. A weekly paper called the Valley Herald had printed it across the front page, in thick red letters: Burglaries in Kingsbridge rise by 200%! Beneath it was a photograph of a broken window, and under the photograph, a quote from a frightened shop owner. Within hours, the town's shops were selling locks, and the local social media pages were full of angry messages. Mothers were saying they would not let their children walk home from school.
At the Kingsbridge Daily, Mrs. Cole called Jonas into her office. "Our readers are asking if it is true," she said. "I would like you to find out."

Jonas read the article carefully. It was a long piece with three quotes, but it contained exactly one figure. It said: According to police data, the number of burglaries in the town rose by 200 percent between January and June compared with the same period last year. There was no table, no number of burglaries, no explanation. Only the big, round percentage.
Ellie, who had come in with the morning's pictures, looked over his shoulder. "Two hundred percent sounds like the end of the world," she said. "But a percentage of what?"
"That," said Jonas, "is exactly the question. I need the real numbers from the police."
ch.clue: no number of burglaries, no explanation
ch.q: What important information is missing from the Valley Herald's article?
o: A list of other towns with more burglaries
The actual number of burglaries behind the percentage
The name of the police officer who gave the data
The opinion of the shop owners about the locks
A photograph of the thief who broke the window
ch.hint: Makalede yalnızca büyük bir yüzde var. Bir yüzdenin anlam kazanması için hangi temel sayıya ihtiyaç var?
ch.why: Makale yalnızca "yüzde 200" diyordu ama hırsızlık sayısını vermiyordu; yüzde, hangi sayıdan hesaplandığı bilinmedikçe tek başına anlamsızdı.

text: Jonas phoned the police station and spoke to a patient desk sergeant, who sent the figures by email within the hour. They were not hard to understand. A small table showed the number of reported burglaries in Kingsbridge for each month of this year and the previous year. For the period January to June, the numbers were: last year, 2. This year, 6.

Jonas wrote them on a piece of paper and, under them, he made a quick calculation. "Six is three times as large as two," he said. "So the number has risen by two hundred percent. The Herald's figure is correct."
"Correct, but very scary, for something so small," said Ellie. "Six burglaries in half a year, in a town with twelve thousand people?"

Jonas put down his pen. "That is what is wrong with the story. The percentage is true, and the impression is false. When you start from a very small number, even a tiny change looks huge. If next year there were eight burglaries, the paper could write 'up thirty-three percent', and it would sound less dramatic, even though it is more."
Ellie opened the sergeant's table again. "He also sent the earlier years," she said. "Look at the line for the same period in the year before last."
ch.clue: last year, 2. This year, 6
ch.q: Why is the percentage in the headline misleading?
o: The burglaries happened in a different town
The percentage was calculated for the wrong months
The police gave the paper a wrong calculation
The numbers are very small, so a small change looks huge
Six burglaries is a very large number for the town
ch.hint: Geçen yıl 2, bu yıl 6 hırsızlık var. Küçük bir sayıdan başlayınca küçük bir artış neden büyük bir yüzdeye dönüşür?
ch.why: Sayılar çok küçük olduğu için (2'den 6'ya) küçük bir artış bile yüzde 200 gibi dev bir rakam veriyordu.

text: The sergeant's table went back five years. Ellie read the numbers for the first half of each year: five years ago, 9. Four years ago, 7. Three years ago, 8. Two years ago, 5. Last year, 2. This year, 6.

Jonas drew a small chart on a sheet of paper, with six bars of different heights. "Look at the shape," he said. "It is not a staircase going up. It is a hill that went down and came up a little. Last year was the exception. The year before was higher. Five years ago it was nine. This year is, in fact, lower than the average of the last five years, which is almost seven."

"So the town is not in danger?" asked Ellie. "I am not saying that," said Jonas. "Any burglary is a serious matter for the person who suffers it. I am saying that the headline gives a wrong picture of the trend. Last year was unusually low. This year is a return to the normal range."

He phoned the neighbouring town and the county police to ask for comparisons. The sergeant replied by afternoon: in a city of the same size, forty kilometres away, the figure for the same period was eleven.
"Six is not a crime wave," said Ellie. "It is a quiet little town."
ch.clue: Last year was the exception
ch.q: What does the five-year table show about this year's six burglaries?
o: It is a return to normal after an unusually low year
It shows that the police have stopped reporting
It is far below the number in all the other towns
It is the first year that burglaries were counted
It is the highest number that the town has ever had
ch.hint: Beş yıllık tabloya bak: 9, 7, 8, 5, 2 ve şimdi 6. Bu yıl olağanüstü yüksek mi, yoksa geçen yılın olağandışı düşük olmasından sonra normale dönüş mü?
ch.why: Beş yıllık tabloda geçen yıl olağandışı düşüktü; bu yılın 6 hırsızlığı geçmiş yılların ortalamasından (yaklaşık 7) daha az, yani normale dönüştü.

text: Mrs. Cole read Jonas's article on the following Monday morning and nodded slowly. "It is a good piece," she said. "It does not claim that everything is perfect. And it does not say that the Herald is lying. It gives the numbers and lets people think." She asked him to propose three headlines for the front page.

Jonas wrote them on a card. The first said: Burglaries in town up 200%, but it is only four more. The second said: There is no burglary problem in Kingsbridge, say police. The third was longer and a little less exciting: Six burglaries in six months, close to the five-year average: police figures in context.

Mrs. Cole read all three twice. "The first one is correct, but it repeats the scary figure as its first words," she said. "Readers remember the first words. The second claims too much. The police did not say that there is no problem. The third says only what the figures show."
"It is not very exciting," said Jonas. "No," said Mrs. Cole, with a smile. "Honest headlines rarely are. But people trust a paper that does not shout."
The next morning, the lock sellers on Main Street were sitting at their counters, waiting for customers who did not come.
ch.clue: close to the five-year average
ch.q: Which headline is the most accurate and fair?
o: There is no burglary problem in Kingsbridge, say police
Burglaries in town up 200%, but it is only four more
Six burglaries in six months, close to the five-year average
Burglaries triple: police fear a new crime wave
Kingsbridge safer than ever, says the town paper
ch.hint: En doğru başlık, rakamı bağlamıyla vermeli, korku yaratmamalı ve polisin söylemediği bir şeyi söylememeli. Hangisi yalnızca verinin gösterdiğini söylüyor?
ch.why: Üçüncü başlık yalnızca verinin gösterdiğini (altı ay içinde altı hırsızlık, beş yıllık ortalamaya yakın) söylüyordu; diğerleri ya korkutuyor ya da fazla iddialı.

outro: Gazete, rakamları bağlamıyla birlikte yayımladı. Jonas, defterine şunu yazdı: bir yüzde, kaç kişinin ya da kaç olayın arkasında durduğunu söylemedikçe yarım bir bilgidir.

title: The Empty Meadow
hero: Park korucusu Wren Calder ve köpeği Bracken
intro: Vadideki çayırda her yaz görülen kelebeklerin sayısı bu yıl çok azaldı. Park korucusu Wren Calder ile köpeği Bracken, sayımları, havayı ve çayırdaki değişiklikleri inceleyerek kelebeklerin neden kaybolduğunu bulmaya çalışıyor.

text: Every Wednesday between May and September, Ranger Wren Calder walked the same route across Long Meadow, a wide, flat grassland at the bottom of the valley, and counted every butterfly that she saw. The walk was called a transect: always the same path, the same speed, the same time of day, so that the numbers from different years could be compared. She did it with a small clicker in her hand, and Bracken followed her, uninterested in butterflies, but very interested in the rabbits.

This year, in the first week of July, she clicked only thirty-five times. She stopped and looked at the numbers in her notebook. In the same week of last year, she had counted one hundred and twenty. In the week before that, one hundred and ten. For eleven years, she had never recorded fewer than eighty.

"A big change," she said to Bracken. "Not a small one. A decline of seventy percent." She sat down on a stone and wrote a list of reasons that could explain it. The first was the weather: a cold spring or a very wet June could keep butterflies away. The second was a pesticide used on neighbouring fields. The third was something that had changed in the meadow itself.
She looked at the sky, at the fields, at the long grass. "One by one," she said, "I will check them."
ch.clue: always the same path, the same speed, the same time of day
ch.q: Why does Wren walk the same route at the same time each week?
o: So that her dog can learn to ignore the rabbits
So that the council will pay her more for the work
So that counts from different years can be compared fairly
So that she can count flowers and butterflies together
So that the butterflies get used to her presence
ch.hint: Wren aynı rotayı aynı hızda ve aynı saatte yürüyor. Bunu neden yapıyor: yıllar arasında adil bir karşılaştırma için hangi koşullar aynı kalmalı?
ch.why: Aynı yol, hız ve saat kullanmak, farklı yılların sayımlarını adil biçimde karşılaştırmayı sağlıyor.

text: Wren started with the simplest explanation. She downloaded the weather records for the last two years from the national service and put them side by side on her laptop. The spring in the valley had been mild, with an average of eleven degrees in April and fourteen in May, almost identical to last year. June had been drier than usual, with only forty millimetres of rain. The days of sunshine in the month before her count were thirty-one, exactly the same as the year before.

"Normal," she said. "In all the measurements, the weather is within the usual range. A cold, wet spring can reduce butterflies, but this was a sunny, easy one." She turned to the next possibility. A friend of hers, the farmer on the north side of the valley, answered her phone call at once. "No new chemicals this year," he said. "I use exactly the same spray as always, and only on the wheat field, never on the grass. And the wind blows from the south, as you know."

Wren put down the phone and drew a line through the first two items on her list. "So it is not the weather, and it is not the neighbour's spray," she said to Bracken. "Which leaves the meadow itself."
She looked at the long green slope in front of her. It looked as it always did, a beautiful wide green place, full of flowers. Only the butterflies were missing.
ch.clue: the weather is within the usual range
ch.q: What has Wren found out so far?
o: The butterflies have flown to a different valley
Her counting method was wrong this year
The cold spring is the main cause of the missing butterflies
The pesticide drifted over from the wheat field to the grass
The weather and the neighbour's spray do not explain the decline
ch.hint: Hava kayıtları geçen yılla neredeyse aynı çıktı ve komşu çiftçi yeni bir ilaç kullanmamış, rüzgâr da başka yönden esiyor. Bu iki neden hakkında ne söylenebilir?
ch.why: Hava normaldi ve komşu çiftçi yeni ilaç kullanmamıştı; kelebeklerin azalması bunlarla açıklanamıyordu.

text: Wren walked slowly over the meadow, looking at the ground. On the edge near the road, she found the first clue: the grass was short and stiff, only ten centimetres high, as if somebody had cut it a few weeks earlier. In the middle, the grass was as tall as her knee, but the flowers were few. She crouched and looked at the stems. The tops of many plants were cut off, clean and flat.

At the shed by the entrance, she found a notice from the town council, pinned on the board: Long Meadow has been mown for safety on 10 June. A tractor with a mowing machine had cut the whole meadow. In previous years, a note from the same council used to say: Mown in early September, after the end of the butterfly season.

Wren read it twice. "June," she said. "In June, the caterpillars of most of our species are feeding on the leaves of the grass and the nettles. The tractor did not only cut the grass. It cut the caterpillars' food and the chrysalises hanging on the stems."

She remembered the thin, empty-looking flower heads, with no insects at all. "The butterflies came this year and found nothing to lay their eggs on," she said. "It was not a disaster in the sky. It was a machine in June."
ch.clue: Mown in early September, after the end of the butterfly season
ch.q: What is the most likely cause of the decline?
o: A disease had spread among the adult butterflies
The meadow was mown in June, when caterpillars were feeding
The council planted too many flowers in the meadow
The butterflies were frightened by the noise of cars
The grass was left uncut for too many years
ch.hint: Belediyenin eski ve yeni notları arasında hangi fark var: çayır ne zaman biçilmiş? Haziranda tırtıllar ne yapıyor?
ch.why: Çayır, tırtılların beslendiği Haziran'da biçilmişti; eskiden bu iş Eylül'de, kelebek mevsiminden sonra yapılıyordu.
